Architectural assessment · 13 August 2026

Prodma on Lobu

Could Lobu carry a 503-table Turkish manufacturing ERP? Not a feature checklist — a search for the gaps that survive when the agent is assumed perfect.

Subject Prodma — .NET WinForms + SQL Server Industry Automotive injection moulding Scale <20 concurrent users Evidence 22 code-audit agents, claims spot-verified

Bottom line

One difference, four consequences.

Most of what looks like a gap dissolves. Screens generate from schemas. Documents, spreadsheets and translation are agent work. e-Invoicing is an HTTP call to a provider. Those were never the question.

What remains is a single architectural fact: Lobu's entity store is a knowledge store — current state, org-scoped, agent-mediated, mutable. An ERP needs a ledger — historical, row-scoped, deterministic, immutable. Every irreducible gap below is a consequence of that one difference, and none can be closed by a smarter agent.

None of them are unfixable either. Three are additive. The fourth — running deterministic org code inside a transaction — is the one that needs a decision rather than a ticket.

Section 01 · The test

What counts as a real gap

An earlier pass produced a list of missing features: no PDF, no Excel, no report builder, no i18n, no form designer. That list was wrong — not factually, but as a way of judging an agent-native platform. Every one of those has the same answer: an agent does it.

So the test became a counterfactual. If the agent were perfect — infinitely capable, instantly fast, never wrong — would this still be a problem?

Anything answered "no" is a product surface, and product surfaces are the easy kind. What survives is the set of guarantees no amount of intelligence can supply: atomicity, isolation, enforcement, determinism, immutability, and knowing what was true last March. An agent cannot recover a value that was never stored, cannot hold a lock while it thinks, and cannot enforce a permission it is capable of ignoring.

Ruled out by this test, and removed from the register entirely: document and PDF generation, Excel import and export, printing, i18n and Turkish UI, report builders, form builders, column choosers, and e-Fatura transmission (the provider exposes a service; calling it is ordinary integration).

Section 02 · The irreducible set

Four gaps that survive a perfect agent

Consequence 01 · Time

The store keeps current state, not history

Entity edits overwrite in place. manage_entity writes no event and no audit row — the grep returns nothing. There is an entity_type_audit table with before_payload and after_payload, but it audits the schema, not the data. There is no field-level version table anywhere in the migrations.

So when a credit limit or a price changes, the previous value is gone: no actor, no before, no after. Effective dating does not exist. Point-in-time is unanswerable — an asOf read mode is declared in the code and raises NotImplemented. And because there is no period concept, a backdated write has nothing to invalidate: no recompute hook, no replay primitive.

Why an agent can't fix it: it cannot read a value that was never written down. This is the cleanest gap in the system and stays invisible until someone asks who changed what.

Consequence 02 · Immutability

Nothing can be frozen

A posted invoice is an ordinary mutable row. There is no posted or frozen concept, no beforeUpdate hook, and no declarative lifecycle — status is a metadata string and JSON Schema cannot express legal transitions between values. Period close has nothing to enforce it with. Soft delete exists, but a legally retained document cannot be protected from a human who can delete.

Why an agent can't fix it: an agent can be told not to edit a posted document. It cannot be prevented from doing so, and a control that depends on the controlled party's cooperation is not a control.

Consequence 03 · Scope

Enforcement stops at the organization

Reads are scoped by organization, role, allowed columns and admin-only tables — the sandbox's client.query runs through validateAndScopeQuery with all of that plus a row cap. This is more careful than it first appears, and calling it a bypass would be wrong.

But there is no row-level scoping. Two people in the same organization see the same rows, always. "A rep sees only their own customers" is not expressible, and the entity read gate that does exist applies to agents and behaviours — humans skip it by design.

Why an agent can't fix it: enforcement lives in the query path or it does not exist. An agent asked to filter results is an agent that can be asked not to.

Consequence 04 · Determinism

Org code cannot hold a transaction

Business rules must be deterministic code, never a model's judgement — a price or a tax computed by inference is unacceptable. So where does that code run? The sandbox gets read-only scoped SQL and no write handle. Org-installed connectors get no database handle at all, by the worker-credentials invariant. Neither can open a transaction spanning several entity writes.

An atomic multi-write path does exist — a Behaviour's declared output — but it takes data, not code. So today you can have deterministic org logic, or atomic multi-entity posting, but not both in the same operation. There is also no compensation, saga or dead-letter path when a multi-write sequence fails halfway.

Why an agent can't fix it: atomicity is a property of the write path. No amount of reasoning makes twenty-one separate writes into one.

Section 03 · The sleeper

Aggregates don't scale by configuration

This one deserves separating out, because it is the least visible and the most likely to bite at month four.

An ERP is mostly aggregates: customer balance, stock on hand, receivables aging, trial balance, order backlog. Lobu's own invariant forbids aggregating history on user-facing read paths and mandates materializing values at write time. That pattern is real and shipped — but every materialized number is hand-authored, feature by feature.

A new aggregate cannot be declared at runtime. What can be defined without a deploy is read-time SQL through derived types and metrics config — which is the shape the invariant nominally rules out. There is no drift detection, no reconciliation, and no recompute path after a retroactive write.

For a domain with hundreds of distinct numbers across ~500 entity types, that means a developer per number. The audit's phrasing was blunt and I agree with it: the agent's competence cannot close this, because the missing piece is a platform mechanism — declared, write-maintained counters with a recompute path — that does not exist yet.

Section 04 · Generated UI

The ceiling is the verb vocabulary, not the components

Users asking an agent for new screens works, and the machinery behind it is in better shape than expected: templates are admin-authored, structurally validated, versioned with rollback, and backed by read-only org-scoped SQL. Authoring and safety are solved.

There are two registries, though, not one. The renderer resolves components as context.components?.[type] ?? componentRegistry[type], and separately accepts an action registry — actions?: Record<string, RendererAction>. Both are caller-supplied callbacks. Neither is passed at the entity or detail-page call sites; both seams exist and sit unused.

The consequence is precise. A generated template can compose any layout from the existing vocabulary and reference an action by name — but it cannot define one. Generated UI is bounded by the verbs someone already shipped in compiled code.

Which makes the action vocabulary the real extensibility surface, more than the component one. Ship the right verbs and agent-generated screens go a very long way. Ship the wrong ones and every genuinely new behaviour needs a deploy, no matter how good the generation gets. Prodma hands over a ready-made list to start from: its permission tables contain at least 170 named business operations — Teklif_Siparis_Olustur, Siparis_Irsaliye_Olustur, Toplu_Faturalama, Entegrasyon_Boz — drawn from twenty years of what this business actually does.

Section 05 · Effort

What each would take

GapShape of the fixTier
Entity field historyCopy-on-write row versioning or an atomic change log. Additive — nothing conflicts.Hard
Effective datingMetadata convention plus renderer support gets most of it; database-enforced validity windows are the full version.Mechanical
Point-in-time readsImplement the asOf mode that is already declared and raising NotImplemented.Mechanical
Immutability of posted recordsA write-gate deny on posted status — but there is no beforeUpdate hook and humans currently bypass policy.Hard
Declarative state machineA new lifecycle primitive. JSON Schema cannot express transitions, so this is genuinely new surface.Architectural
Period closeA gate interceptor for entities gets it; database triggers make it airtight.Mechanical
Row-level visibilityReal row ACLs or a scoping predicate folded into the query builder. No RLS exists today.Hard
Read policy on every seamFold the per-type policy into buildScopedQuery so it applies beyond manage_entity and search.Mechanical
Tamper-evident auditCreate/delete/merge diffs, delivered durably rather than best-effort.Mechanical
Org code in a transactionA declarative atomic-action primitive, or a threaded transaction handle in the sandbox. The decision, not the ticket.Architectural
Compensation / sagaNothing exists for a failed org multi-write today.Architectural
Declared runtime aggregatesWrite-maintained counters with reconciliation and a recompute path.Architectural
Cross-entity write serializationTwo users posting against one stock item are serialized by nothing today.Hard
Action registry supplied at call sitesBoth seams exist and are never passed. An afternoon.Trivial
Gapless document numberingA counter row and a lock; 63 advisory-lock sites already exist.Trivial

Section 06 · The other system

What Prodma actually is

503live database tables
441distinct end-user screens
637klines that are actually live
~10%of that is real business rules

The dump holds 1.63M lines, but a quarter is dead duplicates — the team versioned by filename rather than git, leaving 134 date-suffixed files and roughly fifteen copies of one 25,000-line report file. Strip those, the generated designer files and the decompiled third-party assemblies and the product is 637,000 lines across 4,183 files.

Of that: 31% generated UI, 25% reporting and printing, 35% CRUD plumbing, and 8–12% genuinely non-trivial rules. That last slice — roughly 50–75k lines — is the entire risk surface.

Screen classCountWhat it is
Config-driven CRUD207TanitimSablon forms generated from a field table — Prodma's own schema-driven admin
Hand-coded reports142ListeYap.XxxList methods, buried in 25k-line files
Real business logic~113Documents, postings, MRP, pricing, costing

The hard 10%, read closely

Four audits went line-by-line through the files holding the real rules. What matters is not what the algorithms do — it is why they are hard. They are not sophisticated. They are undocumented accumulations, sector forks and known defects, and in places the original developers said so in the source.

  • The price engine carries a comment reading HATALIDIR — "it is faulty." Two engines run simultaneously and disagree; the warehouse screen still renders the legacy result.
  • Posting commits row by row with no transaction, and someone built manual repair tools for the resulting inconsistency. Drift is routine enough to have tooling.
  • Around 30 fork points switch on sector and firm globals, one commented out in a way that hides the intent.
  • Inbound e-invoice was never implemented — the download methods are dead code.
  • Receivables aging depends on a filter that appears dead and must be confirmed dead before the rule can even be stated.

The one thing a rewrite must not touch. The money primitives depend on .NET tie-to-even rounding, per-line rather than per-document rounding, and discount precision keyed to the company record. The audit's warning, verbatim: any clean-up silently changes money. Port these as literal translations with tests pinned to known outputs. Not improved, not tidied, not modernised.

Where Prodma is weaker than its reputation

A fair assessment records where the incumbent isn't delivering what its schema suggests. Each of these lowers the bar.

  • Field-level permissions are cosmetic — applied as .Visible = false across 1,245 WinForms call sites. Anyone reaching the database sees every column.
  • Authentication is plaintext passwords. No AD, no LDAP, nothing to preserve.
  • There are no transactions at all — no locking, no concurrency detection, single-client globals.
  • The MRP run is a stub returning null. Capacity is ignored entirely.
  • The scheduler is broken by default — dead due-checker, no watchdog, no duplicate prevention.

One capability does cut the other way. The database is partly self-describing: a field table plus runtime ALTER TABLE lets users add their own fields without a code change. Any replacement must reproduce that — and Lobu's schema-per-type over a JSONB column does it natively, without the DDL.

Section 07 · Method

Verified versus assumed

Twenty-two code-audit agents ran in parallel — twelve over Prodma, ten over Lobu — each scoped to one module or capability, required to cite files, and in the final round required to justify every finding against the perfect-agent test. Their claims were not taken at face value.

  • Independently verified: the entities DDL and its JSONB shape; AJV validation on create and update; relationship foreign keys with cascade; the absence of any entity data-history table; that manage_entity writes no audit record; the component and action registry resolution and that neither is supplied at call sites; 132 sql.begin( sites; 63 advisory locks; the sandbox's 180-second ceiling and its scoping path; the 1,245 UI-hiding call sites in Prodma.
  • Claims discarded: one agent reported no transaction API — contradicted by 132 call sites. Another described a read-seam bypass; the scoping path is in fact careful, and the accurate finding is the narrower absence of row-level scoping.
  • Not verified: neither application was run. Every finding is a static read of source.

Section 08 · Open

What would sharpen this

  • An hour watching someone work. Which 10–15 of the 441 screens do people open daily, and what do they do in them? No code reading recovers this.
  • Which price engine is authoritative. Two are live and disagree; only production data settles it.
  • Whether org logic gets a transaction boundary — a declarative atomic action, or a threaded handle in the sandbox. This is the one decision the other gaps wait on.
  • Whether aggregates get a declared-counter primitive, or whether a developer per number is acceptable at this scale.

Assessment prepared 13 August 2026 from a source dump dated June 2026, a live M_MENU export, and the Lobu monorepo at main. Counts are measured. Tier ratings are engineering judgement and should be re-tested against a working slice before a schedule depends on them.

## One difference, four consequences

Everything reduces to this: **Lobu's entity store is a knowledge store** — current state, org-scoped, mutable, agent-mediated. **An ERP needs a ledger** — historical, row-scoped, immutable, deterministic. Every irreducible gap is a symptom of that.

**Time.** Entity edits overwrite in place. `manage_entity` writes no event and no audit row; `entity_type_audit` covers the schema, not the data; there's no field-version table anywhere. So prior values are simply gone. Effective dating doesn't exist, and the `asOf` read mode is declared in code and raises *NotImplemented*. No period concept means a backdated write has nothing to invalidate.

**Immutability.** A posted invoice is an ordinary mutable row. No frozen state, no `beforeUpdate` hook, no declarative lifecycle — status is a metadata string, and JSON Schema can't express legal transitions. An agent can be *told* not to edit a posted document; it can't be *prevented*, and a control that depends on the controlled party's cooperation isn't one.

**Scope.** Reads are scoped by org, role, columns and admin-only tables — genuinely careful. But there's no row-level scoping, so two people in one org always see the same rows. "A rep sees only their own customers" is inexpressible.

**Determinism.** Business rules must be deterministic code, never inference. The sandbox gets read-only SQL and no write handle; connectors get no DB handle at all by the worker-credentials invariant. **An atomic multi-write path does exist — a Behaviour's declared output — but it takes data, not code.** So today: deterministic org logic, or atomic multi-entity posting, not both in one operation. That's the one that needs a decision rather than a ticket.

**And the sleeper:** aggregates don't scale by configuration. Write-time materialization is the only invariant-correct shape and every number is hand-authored. Runtime-definable aggregates are read-time SQL — the shape the invariant rules out. No drift detection, no recompute after retroactive writes. For hundreds of ERP aggregates that's a developer per number.

## On `json_template`

You're right that templates plus JSON Schema cover forms. The ceiling is elsewhere and it's sharper than I first said: there are **two** registries, `components` and `actions`, both caller-supplied, and **neither is passed at any call site**. A generated template can reference an action by name but cannot define one. So generated UI is bounded by the verbs someone shipped — which makes **the action vocabulary your real extensibility surface**, not the component one. Prodma hands you 170 named business operations to seed it from.

**Confidence: 85.** I verified the load-bearing claims directly — the absent history table, that `manage_entity` writes no audit, both registry seams unused, 132 `sql.begin(` sites, the sandbox scoping path. I discarded two agent claims that source contradicted, including the "read-seam bypass," which was wrong. Nothing runtime-verified on either system.

**The two decisions everything else waits on:** whether org logic gets a transaction boundary (declarative atomic action, or a threaded handle in the sandbox), and whether aggregates get a declared-counter primitive or a developer per number is acceptable at this scale. Both are worth settling before any slice gets built, because they change what the slice should look like.

Çalışma dokümanı · 13 Ağustos 2026

Prodma → Lobu Modeli

Prodma'nın 503 tablosu ve 441 ekranı Lobu üzerinde nasıl modellenir? Önerilen veri yapısı, kritik tasarım çatalları ve cevap bekleyen kararlar.

Kaynak Prodma — .NET WinForms + SQL Server Sektör Otomotiv plastik enjeksiyon Ölçek <20 eşzamanlı kullanıcı Dayanak 22 kod analiz ajanı

Özet

Tek bir fark, dört sonuç

Boşlukların çoğu eriyor. Ekranlar şemadan üretiliyor, belge ve tablo üretimi ajanın işi, e-Fatura sağlayıcıya yapılan bir HTTP çağrısı. Bunlar soru değildi.

Geriye tek bir mimari gerçek kalıyor: Lobu'nun entity deposu bir bilgi deposu — güncel durumu tutar, organizasyon kapsamlıdır, değiştirilebilir. ERP'nin ihtiyacı olan ise bir defter — geçmişi tutar, satır kapsamlıdır, deterministiktir, dondurulabilir. Aşağıdaki her boşluk bu tek farkın sonucu ve hiçbiri daha akıllı bir ajanla kapanmıyor.

Ama hiçbiri imkânsız da değil. Üçü eklemeli iş. Dördüncüsü — organizasyona ait deterministik kodun transaction içinde çalışması — bir görev değil, bir karar.

Bölüm 01 · Cevap bekleyen kararlar

Önce bunlar

Aşağıdaki sekiz karar, veri modelinin nasıl kurulacağını doğrudan değiştiriyor. Her birine bir öneri koydum; katılmadığın yerde yönü sen belirle, modeli ona göre güncelleyelim.

S1 — BELGE YAPISI

Fatura satırları nerede dursun?

Bu dokümandaki en belirleyici karar. Bir faturanın başlığı ve 20 satırı Lobu'da nasıl saklanacak? Seçim, atomiklik ile sorgulanabilirlik arasında bir takas.

ASatırlar metadata içinde dizi olarak. Başlık + satırlar tek bir entities satırı. Tek yazma işlemi, dolayısıyla doğal olarak atomik — transaction sorununu tamamen ortadan kaldırır.
BSatırlar ayrı entity, parent_id ile bağlı. Her satır bağımsız sorgulanabilir ve stok/reçete ile ilişkilendirilebilir. Ama 21 ayrı yazma, transaction yok.
CHibrit. Satırlar metadata'da yazılır, arka planda okuma amaçlı ayrı satırlara türetilir.

Önerim: A. Mimari boşlukların en sertini (atomik çok satırlı yazma) tasarımla yok ediyor. Bedeli, "hangi müşteriye kaç adet X sattık" gibi satır bazlı sorguların türetilmiş bir görünüme ihtiyaç duyması — ki bu zaten backing_sql ile çözülebilir.

S2 — DETERMİNİSTİK KOD

Fiyat ve muhasebe kuralları nerede çalışsın?

Fiyat, KDV ve muhasebeleştirme kuralları model çıkarımıyla değil, deterministik kodla çalışmak zorunda. Bugün sandbox'ta yazma yetkisi ve transaction yok; connector'a DB handle hiç verilmiyor.

ASandbox'a transaction sınırı eklenir. Organizasyon kendi kodunu yazar, platform transaction'ı yönetir.
BBildirimsel "atomik işlem" primitifi. Kural veri olarak tanımlanır, platform deterministik olarak uygular. Behavior'ın declared-output yolu zaten böyle çalışıyor.
CKurallar çekirdek koda gömülür. En hızlı yol, ama her müşteriye özel kural bir deploy demek.

Önerim: S1'de A seçilirse bu sorun büyük ölçüde kayboluyor — tek satır yazması zaten atomik. O zaman kural motoru sandbox'ta rahatça çalışır, sadece okur ve hesaplar. Bu ikisi birlikte karar verilmeli.

S3 — GEÇMİŞ

Alan bazlı değişiklik geçmişi tutulacak mı?

Bugün entity düzenlemeleri üzerine yazıyor; önceki değer kayboluyor. manage_entity hiçbir olay ya da denetim kaydı yazmıyor.

AHer belge tipi için tam geçmiş. Kim, ne zaman, önce/sonra. Yasal denetim ve "31 Mart'ta bakiye neydi" sorusu için şart.
BSadece belgeler için, ana veri için değil. Fatura ve mahsup geçmişi tutulur; müşteri kartı tutulmaz.
CPoC kapsamında ertelenir, bilinen eksik olarak not düşülür.

Önerim: B. Maliyeti sınırlı, yasal riski olan yeri kapatıyor. Prodma'nın kendisinde de düzgün bir denetim izi yok, dolayısıyla bu bir gerileme değil.

S4 — DONDURMA

Kesilen fatura değiştirilebilsin mi?

Bugün kayıtlar dondurulamıyor: beforeUpdate kancası yok, durum alanı sıradan bir metin ve herkes değiştirebilir.

AHayır — kesilen belge kilitlenir, düzeltme ancak ters kayıtla yapılır. Muhasebe doğrusu bu.
BYalnızca dönem kapanışına kadar değiştirilebilir.
CŞimdilik serbest, kural ajan seviyesinde tavsiye olarak kalır.

Önerim: A, ama S1'de A seçilirse bu ucuzluyor — tek satırda durum alanına bakan bir yazma kapısı yeterli.

S5 — YETKİ

Aynı organizasyonda kişiler farklı veri görecek mi?

Bugün okuma organizasyon, rol, kolon ve tablo düzeyinde kapsanıyor — ama satır düzeyinde değil. "Plasiyer sadece kendi carilerini görür" ifade edilemiyor.

AEvet, satır düzeyi yetki gerekli. Plasiyer/bölge kapsamı gerçek bir ihtiyaç.
BHayır, herkes her şeyi görür. 20 kullanıcılı tek şirkette kabul edilebilir; Prodma'nın alan yetkisi de zaten sadece arayüzde gizliyor.

Önerim: PoC için B, ürün için A. Prodma'nın mevcut yetkisi gerçek bir güvenlik kontrolü değil, o yüzden B bir gerileme sayılmaz — ama satıştan önce A gerekir.

S6 — TOPLAMLAR

Bakiye ve stok miktarı nasıl hesaplansın?

Lobu'nun kuralı okuma yolunda geçmiş toplamayı yasaklıyor; toplamlar yazma anında maddeleştirilmeli. Ama bugün her sayı elle kodlanıyor; çalışma anında yeni bir toplam tanımlanamıyor.

ABildirimsel sayaç primitifi yazılır. Toplamlar tanımlanabilir hale gelir, yeniden hesaplama yolu olur. Asıl çözüm.
BTüretilmiş tipler / backing_sql kullanılır. Çalışma anında tanımlanabilir ama okuma anında SQL — kuralın istisnası.
CHer sayı için elle alan açılır. PoC'de yürür, yüzlerce sayıda yürümez.

Önerim: PoC için B, sonrasında A. Bu, uzun vadede en çok iş çıkaracak kalem — ay dördünde fark edilir.

S7 — FİYAT MOTORU

Hangi fiyat motoru doğru kabul edilecek?

Prodma'da iki fiyat motoru aynı anda çalışıyor ve birbiriyle çelişiyor; ambar fişi ekranı hâlâ eskisinin sonucunu gösteriyor. Kaynak kodda HATALIDIR yorumu var.

AYeni motor (FiyatService) esas alınır, eskisi hata kabul edilir.
BCanlı veriyle karşılaştırılır, hangisi kullanıcının beklediği sonucu veriyorsa o alınır.
CKural sıfırdan sahiple birlikte yeniden yazılır.

Önerim: C. İki motorun uzlaştırılması, kuralı sahiple konuşup temiz yazmaktan daha pahalı. Bu zaten yeniden yazımın en değerli çıktılarından biri olur.

S8 — KAPSAM

PoC hangi dilimle başlasın?

ATeklif → Sipariş → İrsaliye → Fatura. Klasik zincir, en anlaşılır, tohum veri kolay.
BCari 360. 52 tablo, kredi limiti, yaşlandırma — sohbet arayüzünün en iyi göründüğü yer.
CÜretim / MRP. Taklidi en zor olan, dolayısıyla çalışırsa en etkileyici.

Önerim: A, çünkü belge yapısı kararını (S1) gerçek bir yükle test eden tek dilim bu.

Bölüm 02 · Veri modeli

Önerilen entity tipleri

Bölüm 03 · Şema örneği

Fatura, S1-A modeliyle

Satırların metadata dizisi olarak tutulduğu hâli. Tek satır yazması olduğu için doğal olarak atomik — bugünkü Lobu'ya hiçbir ekleme yapmadan çalışır.

Aynı şekilde x-link-entity-type tabloda gösteriliyor ama formda seçici olarak çalışmıyor. Üç alan tipi eksik: tarih, tarih-saat, entity seçici.

Bölüm 04 · İlişkiler

Belge zinciri nasıl bağlanır

Lobu'nun entity_relationships tablosunda gerçek foreign key'ler var — her iki uçta entities(id)'ye ON DELETE CASCADE ile bağlı, üstelik hangi tipin hangi tiple ilişkilenebileceğini kısıtlayan tip kuralları da mevcut. Yani Prodma'nın 1.175 foreign key'i veritabanı seviyesinde korunabilir; sadece kolon yerine ilişki satırı olarak ifade edilir.

Bu yapının bir yan faydası var: belge zincirini takip etmek tek bir ilişki sorgusu. Prodma'da aynı şey her belge tipinde ayrı link kolonlarıyla yapılıyor ve iki denetim raporu bu kolonların tutarsız doldurulduğunu tespit etti.

Bölüm 05 · Mimari boşluklar

Mükemmel bir ajanın bile çözemeyecekleri

Ölçüt şuydu: ajan sonsuz yetenekli olsaydı bu hâlâ bir sorun olur muydu? Cevabı hayır olan her şey — PDF, Excel, çeviri, rapor tasarımcısı, e-Fatura iletimi — listeden çıkarıldı. Kalanlar bunlar.

S1'de A seçilirse bu tablonun üç satırı küçülüyor. Belge tek satır olduğunda çok satırlı yazma atomikliği sorun olmaktan çıkar, dondurma tek bir yazma kapısına iner, eşzamanlılık da tek satır kilidine. Veri modeli kararı, mimari boşluğu tasarımla yok ediyor — bu yüzden ilk soru o.

Bölüm 06 · Üretilen arayüz

Tavan bileşenler değil, fiiller

Kullanıcının ajandan yeni ekran istemesi çalışıyor ve arkasındaki mekanizma beklediğimden iyi durumda: şablonlar yönetici tarafından yazılıyor, yapısal olarak doğrulanıyor, sürümleniyor ve geri alınabiliyor; veri kaynağı olarak salt-okunur ve organizasyon kapsamlı SQL kullanılıyor.

Ancak iki kayıt defteri var, bir değil: components ve actions. İkisi de dışarıdan verilen callback'ler ve ikisi de hiçbir çağrı noktasında verilmiyor. Sonuç net: üretilen bir şablon mevcut kelime dağarcığından her düzeni kurabilir ve bir fiili adıyla çağırabilir, ama yeni bir fiil tanımlayamaz.

Bu da asıl genişleme yüzeyinin fiil dağarcığı olduğu anlamına geliyor, bileşen dağarcığı değil. Ve Prodma başlangıç listesini hazır veriyor: yetki tablolarında en az 170 adlandırılmış iş operasyonu var — Teklif_Siparis_Olustur, Siparis_Irsaliye_Olustur, Toplu_Faturalama, Entegrasyon_Boz. Yirmi yıllık gerçek kullanımdan süzülmüş bir fiil listesi.

Bölüm 07 · Prodma gerçeği

Karşıdaki sistem ne durumda

Dump 1,63 milyon satır ama dörtte biri ölü kopya — ekip git yerine dosya adıyla sürümlemiş, 134 tarih ekli dosya ve tek bir 25 bin satırlık rapor dosyasının yaklaşık on beş kopyası var. Bunlar, üretilmiş arayüz dosyaları ve decompile edilmiş üçüncü parti kütüphaneler çıkarılınca geriye 4.183 dosyada 637 bin satır kalıyor. Bunun da yalnızca %8–12'si gerçek iş kuralı — yaklaşık 50–75 bin satır. Bütün risk orada.

441 ekranın 207'si zaten bir alan tablosundan üretilen genel CRUD formu, 142'si elle yazılmış rapor, ~113'ü gerçek iş mantığı. Yani Prodma'nın kendisi de şema güdümlü bir yönetim ekranı kurmuş — Lobu'nun yaptığının aynısı.

Yeniden yazımda dokunulmaması gereken tek şey. Para hesapları .NET'in çift-yuvarlama davranışına, belge değil satır bazlı yuvarlamaya ve şirket kaydına bağlı iskonto hassasiyetine dayanıyor. Denetimin uyarısı aynen şöyleydi: her temizlik parayı sessizce değiştirir. Bu fonksiyonlar birebir çevrilmeli ve bilinen çıktılara sabitlenmiş testlerle korunmalı. İyileştirilmemeli, sadeleştirilmemeli.

Prodma'nın itibarından zayıf olduğu yerler de var ve her biri çıtayı düşürüyor: alan yetkileri sadece arayüzde gizliyor (1.245 çağrı noktasında .Visible = false), kimlik doğrulama düz metin parola, hiç transaction yok, MRP çalıştırması null dönen bir taslak, zamanlayıcı varsayılan olarak bozuk. Fiyat motorunda geliştiricinin kendi yazdığı HATALIDIR yorumu duruyor ve muhasebeleştirmedeki tutarsızlığı düzeltmek için elle onarım araçları yazılmış.

Tersine çalışan tek yetenek şu: veritabanı kısmen kendini tanımlıyor — bir alan tablosu ve çalışma anında ALTER TABLE ile kullanıcılar kendi alanlarını ekleyebiliyor. Bir replasmanın bunu karşılaması şart, ve Lobu'nun tip başına şema modeli bunu DDL'siz olarak zaten yapıyor.

13 Ağustos 2026. Kaynak: Haziran 2026 tarihli kod dökümü, canlı M_MENU ve YETKI aktarımı, Lobu main deposu. Sayımlar ölçüldü; seviye değerlendirmeleri mühendislik yargısıdır ve çalışan bir dilimle sınanmadan takvim bağlanmamalı. Hiçbir uygulama çalıştırılmadı — tüm bulgular statik kod okumasıdır.

**ARCHITECTURAL GAPS (the only ones that survive "would a perfect agent fix this?"). Everything else — PDF/Excel/i18n/print/report-builder/e-Fatura transmission — DISSOLVES and was removed from the register.**
Root cause, one sentence: **Lobu's entity store is a KNOWLEDGE store (current state, org-scoped, mutable); an ERP needs a LEDGER (historical, row-scoped, deterministic, immutable).** Four consequences:
1. **No history.** `manage_entity` writes NO event and NO audit row (grep-verified). `entity_type_audit` audits the SCHEMA only. No entity field-version table exists. `asOf` read mode is DECLARED but raises NotImplemented. No period concept ⇒ backdated writes have nothing to invalidate.
2. **No immutability.** No frozen/posted concept, no `beforeUpdate` hook, no declarative state machine (JSON Schema can't express transitions). Status is a plain metadata string.
3. **No row-level scope.** Reads scoped by org+role+column+table (`validateAndScopeQuery` — careful, NOT a bypass; an agent claimed "read-seam bypass", overstated), but never per-row. Two humans in one org always see identical rows.
4. **No transaction boundary for org code.** Sandbox = read-only scoped SQL, no write handle; connectors get no DB handle (worker-credentials invariant). An atomic multi-write path EXISTS (Behavior declared-output) but is data-in/no-code.
Plus the sleeper: **aggregates don't scale** — write-time materialization is hand-authored per number; runtime-definable aggregates are read-time SQL that the invariant forbids. "No without a developer per number."

**★ KEY DESIGN INSIGHT — store document lines as a metadata ARRAY, not child entities.** Header+lines then = ONE `entities` row = ONE write = **naturally atomic**. This dissolves gap 4, shrinks immutability to a single write-gate check, and reduces concurrency to a single-row lock. The data-model decision erases the architectural gap. Cost: line-level queries need a derived view (`backing_sql`). This is question S1 in the Turkish working doc and everything else hangs off it.

**Generated-UI ceiling is the ACTION vocabulary, not components.** TWO registries exist — `components` AND `actions` (`RendererAction`) — both caller-supplied, and **neither is passed at any call site**. A generated template can REFERENCE an action by name but cannot DEFINE one. Seed the verb list from Prodma's 170+ operation codes.

**Artifact is now a TURKISH working doc** with 8 numbered decisions (S1–S8) for the user to answer, the proposed 24 entity types, a concrete `fatura` JSON Schema, and the relationship graph.

Türkçe çalışma dokümanı hazır: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/b65a24ee-a91d-4a7e-a364-e881ed9c7cd0**

Sorularım muğlaktı, haklısın. Şimdi **S1–S8** olarak numaralı, her birinde 2–3 somut seçenek ve benim önerim var — üzerinden geçip "S1: A, S3: B" diye cevaplarsan modeli ona göre güncellerim.

İçerik olarak eklenenler: önerilen **24 entity tipi** (Prodma kaynağı ve alan sayısıyla birlikte), somut bir **fatura JSON Schema'sı**, ve belge zincirinin **ilişki grafiği**.

## Bu turda çıkan asıl bulgu

Veri modelini yazarken bir şey fark ettim, ve sanırım bütün işin en değerli çıktısı bu:

**Fatura satırlarını `metadata` içinde dizi olarak tutarsan, başlık + 20 satır tek bir `entities` satırı oluyor — yani tek bir yazma işlemi, yani doğal olarak atomik.**

Bu, listedeki en sert mimari boşluğu (organizasyon kodunun transaction tutamaması) kod yazarak değil, **tasarım tercihiyle** ortadan kaldırıyor. Yan etkileri de var: dondurma tek bir yazma kapısı kontrolüne iniyor, eşzamanlılık tek satır kilidine iniyor. Üç boşluk birden küçülüyor.

Bedeli, satır bazlı sorguların (`bu müşteriye kaç adet X sattık`) türetilmiş bir görünüme ihtiyaç duyması — ki `backing_sql` bunu zaten karşılıyor.

Bu yüzden S1'i ilk soru yaptım. Diğer yedi kararın çoğu ona bağlı; özellikle S2 (deterministik kod nerede çalışsın) S1'de A seçilirse büyük ölçüde konu olmaktan çıkıyor.

## Bir de şu

Ekran üretimindeki tavanın bileşenler değil **fiiller** olduğu bulgusu doğrulandı: `components` ve `actions` diye iki kayıt defteri var, ikisi de hiçbir çağrı noktasında verilmiyor. Üretilen şablon bir fiili adıyla çağırabiliyor ama tanımlayamıyor. Yani genişleme yüzeyin fiil dağarcığı — ve Prodma'nın yetki tablolarındaki 170+ operasyon kodu bunun için hazır bir başlangıç listesi.

**Güven: 85.** Şemadaki `format: "date"` ve `x-link-entity-type` alanlarının formda çalışmadığını doğrudan koddan doğruladım; entity geçmiş tablosunun yokluğunu ve `manage_entity`'nin denetim kaydı yazmadığını da. Doğrulanmayan: hiçbir uygulama çalıştırılmadı, ve önerdiğim 24 tipin alan sayıları Prodma'nın kolonlarından benim tahminim — gerçek kullanım verisiyle değişir.

Sen S1–S8'i cevapla, ben modeli güncelleyip tohum veriyle çalışan bir dilime geçeyim.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user owns/has access to **Prodma**, a Turkish manufacturing ERP at `/Users/burakemre/Downloads/emre_project`, and wants to know whether it could be rebuilt on **Lobu** (their agent platform monorepo at `/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu`).

   Intent evolved substantially across the conversation:

   - **After interview:** Goal is "Rebuild the ERP itself on Lobu" but as a **proof of concept** — "live in production but this is going to be a demo if lobu could replace prodma app from scratch." Audience is **Prodma's owner** (a domain expert). The real deliverable is a **gap analysis**: "full replacement if possible, the point is to see where lobu lacks." Scale is **<20 concurrent users**. Turkish statutory compliance initially declared "non-negotiable." All four deliverables wanted: written gap report, working slice, Lobu roadmap, pitch for the owner. Time unbounded.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`/Users/burakemre/Downloads/emre_project/`** — the Prodma source dump. 5,598 `.cs` files FLAT (no subdirs), no `.sln`, not a git repo. 1.63M LOC total; **637k live LOC in 4,183 files** after stripping generated/decompiled/duplicates.

   - **`_analysis/` staged inside the Prodma dump** — `BRIEF.md`, `menu-tree.txt`, `entities.txt`, `scopes/*.txt`, `runner.sh`, `reports/*.md`. 12 Prodma reports produced.

-- migrate:up

-- External-backed derived entity types. A derived entity type (backing_sql IS NOT
-- NULL) normally runs its view over Lobu's own org-scoped tables. When
-- backing_source references a connection, the view instead executes LIVE against
-- that connection's single external database (read-only, no copy): the read goes
-- get_type → query_sql({ sql: backing_sql, connection: backing_source }) →
-- runConnectorQuery (connector-pushdown.ts), which runs the SQL in the
-- connection's connector. NULL ⇒ internal (today's behavior). backing_source is
-- only meaningful on a derived type (backing_sql IS NOT NULL).
--
-- Deliberately NO foreign key to connections: if the source connection is deleted
-- the read must FAIL ("source connection no longer exists") rather than silently
-- fall back to internal scoping (ON DELETE SET NULL — which would run external SQL
-- against internal tables) or block connection deletion (ON DELETE RESTRICT).
-- runConnectorQuery validates the connection exists, is in-org, and is visible to
-- the caller at read time.
--
-- Stored as the connection SLUG (text), not an id: the slug is what the config
-- diff compares (no churn), it survives a connection delete+recreate, and
-- runConnectorQuery resolves slug → connection → DATABASE_URL fresh at read time.
--
-- Idempotent: no-op on databases that already have the column.
ALTER TABLE public.entity_types ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS backing_source text;

-- migrate:down

/**
 * Promote keyed watcher-window rows into real child entities (P2 phase 1).
 *
 * For each row in one declared entity output, this module computes an internal
 * stable key and upserts a child entity. The key is persisted as an
 * `entity_identities` row in a dedicated `watcher_key` namespace. Its identifier
 * is a fixed-size SHA-256 digest of the Behavior, output, entity type, and exact
 * typed key tuple; the full tuple remains in entity metadata for inspection,
 * so a re-run — or a second replica racing the same window — resolves to the
 * existing entity instead of creating a duplicate. The partial unique index
 * `idx_entity_identities_live_unique (organization_id, namespace, identifier)
 * WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` is the lock.
 *
 * Origin provenance (the window that first produced the entity, its stable key,
 * and the watcher) is stamped onto the entity's own `metadata` at creation —
 * `metadata.window_id` / `stable_key` / `watcher_id`. There is NO separate
 * observation event: an entity is promoted once (it's an identity, not a time
 * series), so its origin lives on the row itself.
 *
 * The upsert runs on the caller's transaction handle so the entity and identity
 * writes commit atomically with the window itself.
 *
 * Multi-replica notes:
 *   - `entities.id` / `entity_identities.id` are `nextval()` sequence columns,
 *     so concurrent inserts never collide on the PK (no advisory-lock allocator
 *     needed here — that's only for the MAX(id)+1 tables).
 *   - The window (canvas chain root) is guarded by `idx_canvas_chain_root`, so at
 *     most one completion creates a given window; idempotent replays reuse it and
 *     re-enter this function, where the per-key identity claim makes repeats
 *     no-ops.

Mutasyon kancası koyup exception atamaz mıyız?

“Entity mutasyonları için kanca yaparsak, değişikliği engellemek için exception atabiliriz değil mi?”

Kodda
Evet — ve o kanca zaten yazılmış. authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts tam olarak bu: her kullanıcıya dönük entity yazmasının önünde duran, kayıtlı bir interceptor zinciri. Sonuçlar allow / deny / defer. İlk deny kazanıyor. Dosyanın kendi başlığı diyor ki yeni bir kural eklemek tek bir yeni dosya, çekirdek kodda sıfır değişiklik. registerMutationInterceptor() ile takılıyor.
Tek engel
Kapı insanlar için kısa devre yapıyor. entity-policy.ts:796: if (args.principalKind === "user") return "allow"; — ve aynı desen dosyada beş ayrı yerde. Yorum açık: “İnsan düzenlemeleri burada hiç kapılanmaz.” Yani bugün dondurma ajanlara karşı çalışır, kullanıcıya karşı çalışmaz.
Maliyet
Bir interceptor dosyası + insan yolunu bu kapıya sokan cerrahi bir değişiklik. İkincisi güvenlik katmanına dokunduğu için dikkat ister (yöneticinin kendi kendini kilitlememesi), ama yeni mimari değil.
DÜZELTİLDİ → HAKLIYDIN Kanca var, genişletilmek üzere tasarlanmış. Bunu “mimari boşluk” diye yazmam hataydı.

JSON Schema migration kütüphaneleri bunu çözmez mi?

“json schema migrations, bunun için kütüphaneler vardı değil mi?”

Ayrım
Bunlar iki farklı problem. JSON Schema migration, belgenin şeklini zamanla değiştirmek için (v1’de tutar vardı, v2’de tutar_kdv_haric oldu). Durum makinesi ise bir değerin geçişini kısıtlamak için: taslak → onaylandı → kesildi, ve asla geriye değil.
Neden kütüphane çözmez
JSON Schema bir belgeyi tek başına doğrular. “Yeni değer, eski değere bağlıdır” ifadesini hiçbir JSON Schema sürümü kuramaz — girdide eski değer yok. Bu bir kütüphane eksikliği değil, biçimin sınırı.
Doğru yer
İ2’deki aynı interceptor. O, hem current’ı hem proposed’ı görüyor — yani geçişe bakabilir. İzin verilen geçişler metadata_schema içinde x-state-machine gibi bir ek açıklamada durur, tek bir interceptor onu yorumlar. İ2 ile aynı iş; ikisi tek dosyada biter.

İ4 — SATIR BAZLI YETKİ

Bu ilişkilerle yapılamaz mı? Member entity zaten var.

“Buna ihtiyacımız olabilir ama member entity zaten var değil mi, bu ilişkiler üzerinden yapılabilir mi?”

Kodda
Tam olarak öyle yapılıyor — zaten. authz/access-graph.ts genel bir erişim grafiği motoru: üye entity’sinden kaynak entity’sine member_of kenarları yazıyor, ayrılanları uzlaştırıyor, grafiği taze/bayat olarak damgalıyor. authz/resource-visibility.ts ise okuma anında bunu uyguluyor: bir kayıt yalnızca istek sahibi ilgili kaynağın member_of’u ise görünüyor, ve grafik bayatsa kapalı düşüyor (veriyi gizler, sızdırmaz).
Ama
Bu kapı events okuma dikişine bağlı — entities’e değil. Slack kanalı ve GitHub reposu bu şekilde korunuyor; bir fatura entity’si korunmuyor.
Ek olarak
Yazma tarafında ayrıca entity_approval_policies.entity_id var — bir politika satırı tek bir entity’yi hedefleyebiliyor. Ve entities.field_controls satır+alan bazında sahiplik tutuyor. Yani satır düzeyi kavramı sisteme yabancı değil.
DÜZELTİLDİ → ORTA İŞ Mekanizma doğru ve mevcut. Yapılacak iş, aynı üyelik yüklemini entity okuma yoluna da bağlamak — sıfırdan tasarım değil, kanıtlanmış bir deseni ikinci dikişe taşımak.

İ5 — TRANSACTION

Event sourcing yaptığımıza göre güncel çözüm ne?

“Event sourcing yaptığımız için lobu ile alakalı state of the art çözüm ne?”

Önce düzeltme
Lobu, entity’ler için event sourcing yapmıyor. entities güncel durumu tutan, yerinde güncellenen bir tablo. events ise connector’lardan gelen dış dünya akışı — entity yazmalarının günlüğü değil. Dolayısıyla event sourcing kalıpları (projection rebuild, event replay) buraya doğrudan uygulanmıyor.
Bugün var olan
updateEntity oku-değiştir-yaz’ın tamamını tek sql.begin içinde ve satırda FOR UPDATE kilidiyle yapıyor. Yani tek entity yazması zaten atomik ve sıralı. Ayrıca Behavior’ın declared-output yolu N entity’yi pencere transaction’ı içinde birlikte commit ediyor — “declared outputs are an atomic contract”.
S1=A sonrası
Fatura tek satır olduğu için sorunun büyük kısmı zaten yok. Geriye kalan tek gerçek ihtiyaç: fatura + stok_hareket + mahsup aynı anda işlenmeli. Bunun için doğru kalıp event sourcing değil, transactional outbox ya da daha basiti: mevcut declared-output atomik sözleşmesini muhasebeleştirme adımına da açmak.
Sandbox
client.query zorla SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY. client.entities.* yazma metodları var ama her biri ayrı çağrı, ortak transaction yok. S2=A ile bu sorun değil: sandbox okur ve hesaplar, sonucu tek yazmada bırakır.
KÜÇÜLDÜ → TEK ADIMA İNDİ S1+S2 kararlarından sonra geriye sadece muhasebeleştirme adımı kalıyor. Onun da atomik yazma yolu Behavior tarafında zaten mevcut.

İ6 — TOPLAMLAR

Bunu açıkla: neden ölçeklenmiyor?

“Bunu bana açıkla, potansiyel çözümler, tuzaklar vs.”

Kısaca
Bugün Lobu’da bir sayıyı hesaplamanın iki yolu var, ikisi de okuma anında hesaplıyor. Fatura sayısı arttıkça o hesap uzuyor, ama cevap (tek bir bakiye rakamı) aynı kalıyor. Detaylı anlatım Bölüm 03’te.
Neden ciddi
Bakiye, stok miktarı ve yaşlandırma bir ERP’de en sık okunan sayılar ve tarih ilerledikçe sadece büyüyor. Repo’nun kendi kuralı da okuma yolunda geçmiş toplamayı zaten yasaklıyor.
AÇIK — EN PAHALI KALEM Yedi maddenin içinde tek gerçek yeni-yapı ihtiyacı bu. Diğer altısı ya mevcut, ya birleşti, ya küçüldü.
İ7 — EŞZAMANLILIK

Event’leri user id ile yazmıyor muyuz?

“Event’leri user id ile yazıyoruz değil mi? Yani kimin ne üzerinde çalıştığını biliyoruz, bu çakışma çözümüne yardım eder.”

Kodda
events.created_by gerçekten var. Ama İ1’de görüldüğü gibi entity yazmaları event üretmiyor — dolayısıyla “kim neyi düzenliyor” izi bugün oluşmuyor.
Aslında daha iyisi var
İki mekanizma zaten çalışıyor. Birincisi FOR UPDATE satır kilidi: aynı entity’ye eşzamanlı iki yazma sıraya giriyor, kayıp güncelleme olmuyor. İkincisi field_controls: bir insan bir alanı düzenlediğinde o alanın sahipliğini alıyor; sonradan gelen ajan yazması o alanı ezemiyor, onay kuyruğuna düşüyor. Bu, gerçek bir alan bazlı çakışma çözümü — insan ile ajan arasında.
Eksik olan
İnsan ile insan arasında. İki kullanıcı aynı faturayı açıp kaydederse sürüm kontrolü yok; ikinci kayıt sessizce kazanıyor. S1=A ile satırlar da aynı hücrede olduğundan, B kullanıcısının kaydı A’nın bütün satır dizisini ezer.
Çözüm
İyimser kilit. Okurken alınan sürüm damgası (updated_at zaten var) yazarken geri gönderilir, kilidin zaten tutulduğu transaction içinde karşılaştırılır, uymuyorsa hata. Var olan bir bloğun içine giren ~10 satır.

Bölüm 03

S6 açıklaması — toplamlar neden ayrı bir problem

Sorunun kendisi basit: “Bu müşterinin bakiyesi ne?” Cevap tek bir sayı. Ama o sayıyı üretmek için bugün, o müşterinin bugüne kadarki bütün faturalarını ve tahsilatlarını toplamak gerekiyor.

İlk yıl bu 400 kayıt, göz açıp kapayıncaya kadar biter. Beşinci yıl 12.000 kayıt, ve bu sorgu müşteri kartı her açıldığında, her sipariş girişinde, her yaşlandırma raporunda tekrar koşuyor. Cevap hep tek sayı, ama hesabın maliyeti tarihle birlikte büyüyor. Repo’nun kendi sert kuralı da bunu zaten yasaklıyor: kullanıcıya dönük okuma yollarında geçmiş tablolarını toplamak yasak, toplam yazma anında maddeleştirilmeli.

Bugün Lobu’da ne var

backing_sql — türetilmiş tipler

  • Bir entity tipi backing_sql alırsa satır saklamaz; kendi tablolarımızın üstünde canlı bir SQL görünümü olur.
  • “Cari bakiye” böyle tanımlanabilir, ve çalışma anında tanımlanabilir — deploy gerekmez.
  • Ama her okumada baştan hesaplar. Migration’larda tek bir MATERIALIZED VIEW yok; önbellek katmanı hiç yok.

metrics_config — bildirimsel ölçüm katmanı

  • Entity tipine measure / dimension / segment tanımlatan gerçek bir semantik katman. Derleyici bunu SQL’e indiriyor.
  • Ama derleyici yalnızca FROM events üretiyor — entity’leri eventSet.by: "alias" ile, yani metin eşleşmesiyle bağlıyor.
  • Entity’ler arası join, window/link ve asOf okumaları açıkça NotImplemented.
  • Yani “bu carinin faturalarının toplamı” bu katmanda ifade edilemiyor — faturalar entity, event değil.

Üç çözüm, üç maliyet

YolNasılTuzakUygun
1. Türetilmiş tip backing_sql ile bakiye görünümü. Kod yazılmaz, tanım yazılır. Her okumada tam tarama. Kural ihlali; birkaç bin kayıttan sonra hissedilir. PoC
2. Denormalize alan Cari entity’sinin metadata.bakiye alanı, fatura yazılırken güncellenir. Sapma. Bir yazma kaçarsa sayı sessizce yanlış kalır ve kimse fark etmez. Yeniden hesaplama yolu şart. İlk müşteri
3. Sayaç primitifi Platform seviyesinde bildirimsel sayaç: “şu tipin şu alanı, şu ilişkideki şu alanın toplamıdır.” Yazma anında bakım, tanımlı yeniden hesaplama. Gerçek bir yapı işi. Ama tek seferlik — sonrasında her yeni sayı sadece bir tanım. Ürün

Asıl tuzak 2. yolda ve isim vermeye değer. Denormalize bakiye, doğruluğunu “her yazma yolu bu alanı güncelledi” varsayımından alır. Bir tane atlanan yol — bir düzeltme scripti, bir toplu içe aktarım, bir ajan — sayıyı sessizce bozar ve hata aylar sonra mutabakatta çıkar. Bu yüzden 2. yola geçilecekse aynı anda bir yeniden hesaplama ve karşılaştırma işi de yazılmalı. Bunun olmaması, Prodma’da “muhasebe tutarsızlığı onarım aracı” ekranlarının neden var olduğunun cevabı.

Önerim değişmedi: PoC için 1, ürün için 3. Ama artık 3’ün ne olduğunu daha net söyleyebiliyorum — metrics_config zaten doğru biçim; eksik olan, derleyicisinin events yerine entities üzerinden de derleyebilmesi ve sonucu maddeleştirebilmesi. Yani sıfırdan bir primitif değil, mevcut ölçüm katmanının ikinci bir kaynağa açılması.

Bölüm 04

Güncellenmiş boşluk tablosu

İlk turdaki liste yedi maddeydi ve hepsi “mimari” etiketliydi. Kod okunduktan sonra tablo şu hale geliyor.

**ARCHITECTURAL GAPS (the only ones that survive "would a perfect agent fix this?"). Everything else — PDF/Excel/i18n/print/report-builder/e-Fatura transmission — DISSOLVES and was removed from the register.**
Root cause, one sentence: **Lobu's entity store is a KNOWLEDGE store (current state, org-scoped, mutable); an ERP needs a LEDGER (historical, row-scoped, deterministic, immutable).** Four consequences:

Cost: line-level queries need a derived view (`backing_sql`). This is question S1 in the Turkish working doc and everything else hangs off it.

**Generated-UI ceiling is the ACTION vocabulary, not components.** TWO registries exist — `components` AND `actions` (`RendererAction`) — both caller-supplied, and **neither is passed at any call site**. A generated template can REFERENCE an action by name but cannot DEFINE one. Seed the verb list from Prodma's 170+ operation codes.

So freeze binds AGENTS today, not humans.
3. **State machine = same lift as #2.** JSON Schema can't express old→new transitions in ANY draft (validates a doc in isolation) — no library fixes it. The interceptor sees both `current` and `proposed`, so declare transitions as `x-state-machine` in `metadata_schema` and interpret in the same file.
4. **Row-level authz via relationships is EXACTLY what Lobu already built.** `authz/access-graph.ts` writes `member_of` edges + reconciles leavers + stamps freshness; `authz/resource-visibility.ts` enforces membership at read time and FAILS CLOSED on a stale graph. **But it is wired to the `events` read seam, not `entities`.** Also `entity_approval_policies.entity_id` targets ONE entity (write-side, non-human only) and `entities.field_controls` is per-row-per-field.

Behavior declared-output commits N entities in the window tx (promote-keyed-entities.ts:438, "atomic contract"). Sandbox `client.query` forces `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` (client-sdk.ts:263). Yedi maddenin hepsini koda sordum. **Dördünde haklıydın** — ilk turdaki listem yanlıştı.

## S6, plain English

The question is just: *what's this customer's balance?* One number. To produce it today you have to sum every invoice and every payment that customer has ever had.

Year one that's 400 rows, instant. Year five it's 12,000 rows, and that query runs every time someone opens the customer card, enters an order, or pulls an aging report. **The answer stays one number; the cost of computing it grows with history.** The repo's own hard invariant already forbids exactly this — aggregating history on a user-facing read path.

Lobu has two ways to compute a number today, and both compute at read time. `backing_sql` derived types are live SQL views — runtime-definable, no deploy, but recompute on every read (there is not a single `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` in the migrations). `metrics_config` is a real declared semantic layer, but its compiler only emits `FROM events` and joins entities by *text alias matching*; cross-entity joins are `NotImplemented`. So "sum of this customer's invoices" can't be expressed there at all — invoices are entities, not events.

Three routes, in the artifact: derived view (PoC), denormalized field (first customer), declarative counter primitive (product). The trap worth naming is the middle one — a denormalized balance is only correct if *every* write path updates it. One missed path (an import, a fix script, an agent) corrupts it silently and you find out months later in reconciliation. That's precisely why Prodma ships "accounting inconsistency repair tool" screens.

## Where I was wrong

**The freeze hook exists.** `authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts` is a registered interceptor pipeline sitting in front of every user-facing entity write — allow/deny/defer, first deny wins. Its own header says a new rule is one new file with zero core edits. The only blocker is `entity-policy.ts:796`: `if (args.principalKind === "user") return "allow";` — so it binds agents, not humans. Calling that "architectural" was my mistake.

**Relationships are already the row-level mechanism.** `access-graph.ts` writes `member_of` edges and reconciles leavers; `resource-visibility.ts` enforces membership at read time and fails closed on a stale graph. Exactly what you proposed. It's just wired to the `events` read seam instead of `entities`.

**State machines merge into the freeze hook.** JSON Schema can't express "new value depends on old value" in any draft — it validates a document in isolation, so no library solves it. But the interceptor sees both `current` and `proposed`. Declare transitions as `x-state-machine`, interpret them in the same file. Same lift as the freeze.

**Concurrency is half done.** `FOR UPDATE` serializes same-entity writes, and `field_controls` already gives a human per-field ownership an agent can't overwrite. What's missing is human-vs-human — no version check. With S1=A that means the second save clobbers the entire line array, so it matters more now. Fix is an optimistic lock inside a transaction that already holds the row lock.

One correction on your framing: **Lobu isn't event-sourced for entities.** `entities` is mutated in place; `events` is the connector ingestion stream, not the entity write log. So event-sourcing patterns don't apply here — after S1+S2 the only remaining multi-row write is the posting step, and that's an outbox/saga shape.

**Net: seven architectural gaps down to one.**

---

**Güven: 88.** Her iddiayı dosya:satır olarak doğruladım — interceptor kaydı, insan kısa devresi (dört ayrı yerde), `member_of` okuma kapısı, metric derleyicisinin `FROM events` kısıtı, sıfır materialized view, `FOR UPDATE` + `field_controls`. Doğrulanmayan: hiçbir şey çalıştırılmadı; interceptor'ı insanlara açmanın Lobu'nun geri kalanında ne kıracağını okuyarak değil deneyerek görmek gerekir.

Sıradaki adımlar:
1. **S6'yı karara bağla** — PoC için türetilmiş tip, ürün için metric compiler'ı entity kaynağına açmak. Onaylarsan model kesinleşir.
2. **İnsan yolunu mutation gate'e sokmanın etkisini ölç** — bu ERP kararı değil, Lobu'nun genel davranışı; ayrı konuşulmalı.
3. **Üç alan tipini yaz** (date, datetime, entity-lookup) — bunlar olmadan hiçbir ERP ekranı çalışmaz, ve en ucuz kalem.
4. **Tohum veriyle Teklif→Fatura zincirini ayağa kaldır** — üretilen ekranın nerede yetmediği ancak orada görünür.

input.content:
Round 3 — corrected findings and the work plan

Prodma on Lobu

A second pass through the source overturned my biggest claim: Lobu does record field-level change history, and has since before this project started. What's left is a much smaller, much sharper list — and one genuine architectural question about who is allowed to author a rule.

Source lobu@main · prodma 637k live LOC Method claim → grep → file:line Open gaps 5 work packages

Section 01

Correction: history already exists

In the last round I said “manage_entity writes no event and no audit row”. That was wrong, and the way it was wrong is worth naming: I grepped for the literal string INSERT INTO events inside the file. The write goes through a helper, so the grep found nothing and I read absence into it.

What is actually there, at manage_entity.ts:547:

recordChangeEvent({
  entityIds: [entityId],
  organizationId: ctx.organizationId,
  title: `Entity updated: ${changes.map(c => c.field).join(", ")}`,
  content: `Entity "${name}" (id: ${entityId}) updated:\n${contentLines}`,
  metadata: { changes },        // ← [{ field, old, new }] — a real before/after diff
  createdBy: ctx.userId,        // ← who
  clientId: ctx.clientId,
});

That lands in events with semantic_type = 'change', indexed by entity_ids. Who, when, which field, old value, new value. It is a working audit trail, and there is a whole family around it — recordConfigChangeEvent, recordWorkspaceChangeEvent, recordLifecycleEvent — all writing through one idempotent insertConnectionlessAuditEvent.

So the task you asked for isn't “build audit logging.” It's consolidation — and that framing was right. Here is precisely what is missing, which is what work package WP-1 has to close.

HoleDetailWhy it matters for an ERP
Only update handleCreate, handleDelete, handleLink, handleUnlink, handleMerge, handleUnmerge, handleUpdateLink record nothing. “Who deleted this invoice?” has no answer. Creation of a document is unrecorded.
Fire-and-forget recordChangeEvent never throws. Two retries, then logs at ERROR and drops the row. A dropped audit row is a silent hole in a legal record. It must commit with the change or the change must fail.
Post-commit Runs outside the entity transaction, after it commits. A crash in the window between the two loses the audit for a change that did happen.
Content redacted Body text diffs record as the literal string "[changed]". Probably fine — but it's a policy decision, not an accident, and it should be a stated one.

The one design question I need you to answer. Making the audit row durable means writing it inside the entity transaction. That changes Lobu's behaviour for everyone, not just this ERP: today a failing audit write is survivable, afterwards it fails the user's edit. That is correct for a ledger and arguably wrong for a knowledge tool, where losing an audit line is better than losing the edit. Two ways out — make it durable everywhere, or make durability a property of the entity type (fatura yes, note no). I lean to the second, but it's your platform.

Section 02

Is a state machine a workaround?

You asked whether this is a crutch — whether proper guardrails and permissions would let the agent work it out, since we want this as agentic as possible. Half of that is right, and the half that's right changes the design. But the premise doesn't hold, for a reason worth being precise about.

What a permission answers

  • May this principal write this field?
  • Inputs: principal, resource, field.
  • Stable — the answer doesn't change as the row changes.

What a transition rule answers

  • May this value become that value?
  • Inputs: current data, proposed data.
  • Changes as the row changes. Same accountant, same field — allowed on a draft, refused once posted.

That's the crux. A permission system that only sees who can never express “posted invoices are immutable,” because the principal is identical in both cases and only the data differs. So this isn't a workaround for proper permissions — it is the shape proper permissions take once the decision depends on data. Lobu already half-believes this: entity_approval_policies.entity_id scopes a rule to one row, and entities.field_controls scopes ownership to one field of one row. Both make the answer depend on data rather than principal alone.

Three reasons the agent's own judgement can't be the enforcement point:

  • The agent isn't the threat. The other writers are — a bulk import, a retry, a second agent, a person clicking in the UI, a connector. A rule that lives in one agent's reasoning binds that agent and nobody else. This is the repo's own rule about putting the check at the chokepoint.
  • It's on every write. Making the gate a model call puts an LLM in the critical path of every save: latency, cost, nondeterminism — and it can be argued out of its position, which is the one thing a freeze must not be.
  • Audits need a stable reason. “Why was this refused?” has to have the same answer next month. “The model decided” doesn't survive that.

Where you're right, and it matters more than the above. The mistake would be making the transition table a developer artifact — a config file someone edits and deploys. It shouldn't be. It should be data on the entity type, authored by an agent from a conversation with the accountant, exactly the way metadata_schema, event_kinds, metrics_config and backing_sql already are: all four are writable at runtime through manage_entity_schema, no deploy.

So the division is agent-authored, deterministically enforced. The agent writes the rule, explains it, and changes it when the accountant's process changes. The gate just reads it and refuses. Nothing about that is less agentic — it's the difference between an agent that advises and an agent that configures the system.

And there's a stronger version of your instinct worth putting on the table. Instead of enforcing immutability with a rule, get it from structure: make a posted document append-only, so a correction creates a new version rather than editing the old one. events.supersedes_event_id already establishes this pattern in the codebase, and “never DELETE, tombstone instead” is already a repo invariant. Then “frozen” isn't a rule anyone enforces — it's a property of how the row is stored, and there is no gate to argue with. Fewer rules, more structure. The cost is that entity identity, dedupe and every relationship pointing at the document have to follow the version chain. This is a real fork and I'd like your call on it — see Q1.

Section 03

How the hooks actually work

You asked how the mutation gate works and whether it's something people can trigger with code. The short answer to the second part is no — not today, and that turns out to be the most interesting gap in this document.

The mechanism

// packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts

interface MutationInterceptor {
  name: string;
  evaluate: (req: EntityMutationRequest) => Promise<Decision | null>;
}

// create / delete → first `deny` wins; first `defer` short-circuits
// update         → per-field `requireApproval` sets UNION across interceptors
// `null`         → no opinion, pass through

const BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS = [ approvalInterceptor ];   // ← the only one in production
const registry = [...BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS];

export function registerMutationInterceptor(i: MutationInterceptor): void {
  if (registry.some(x => x.name === i.name)) return;    // idempotent by name
  registry.push(i);
}

Every user-facing entity write — create, update, delete, and Behavior window promotion — builds one EntityMutationRequest and calls runMutationGate. The core mutation code is deliberately policy-blind: it never imports the ACL, it just acts on the decision. An interceptor can allow, deny (hard refusal, no approval queued), or defer (hold the write and queue a durable approval card, executed strictly post-commit so approvals never ride the caller's transaction).

The update path is finer-grained than allow/deny: an interceptor returns a set of field paths that need approval, and those sets union across interceptors. Reserved $name, $parent_id, $content paths let a field-scoped rule also cover the entity's own attributes.

Can people trigger it with code?

No. registerMutationInterceptor is a TypeScript function called at module init. Outside tests it is never called — production runs exactly one interceptor, the approval one. Adding a rule means writing a server file and deploying. Neither a connector, a Behavior, nor sandbox code can register one, and the sandbox couldn't host one anyway: client.query is forced SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY and the gate runs inside the caller's transaction.

This is the sharpest architectural statement in the whole analysis. Every declarative layer in Lobu is already agent-authorable at runtime — schema, event kinds, metrics, derived views, view templates, all writable through manage_entity_schema with no deploy. The write gate is the one layer that is not.

That's the real gap behind your question, and it's bigger than this ERP. It's the difference between an agent that can configure what the system knows and one that can also configure what the system refuses. WP-2 proposes the smallest honest version: one interceptor that reads its rules from entity-type data, so agents author policy without anyone executing arbitrary code in the write path.

Section 04

Derived entities, and what they don't cover

You said you thought derived entities were meant for exactly the computed-attribute case. They're close, and they're more capable than I credited — but there's one structural limit that decides how the data model has to look.

What they do

  • Set backing_sql on an entity type and it stores no rows — it is a live SQL view over our own tables. A DB trigger rejects any attempt to insert rows into it.
  • Runtime-definable by an agent through manage_entity_schema. No deploy, no developer.
  • backing_source can point it at an external database through a connection instead.

The limit

  • It is whole-type, not per-field. A type either stores rows or is a view. There is no stored cari with 30 real fields plus one computed balance.
  • So a computed attribute becomes a second type (cari_balance) that you join — the number is a separate row, not a field on the customer.
  • And it recomputes on every read. There is not one CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW in the entire migration history.

So: derived entities do cover the use case in the sense you meant — calculations defined at runtime by an agent, no deploy. What they don't do is attach the result to the stored entity, or stop recomputing it. That's fine for the PoC and it's the reason S6 stays open rather than closed: the question isn't whether we can express a balance, it's whether reading it stays cheap in year five.

Section 05

Dates: the primitive exists, the wiring doesn't

You asked me to check whether we use dates and build the UI properly. Both halves have answers, and together they make this the cheapest item on the list.

  • The convention is already in production data. format: "date" and format: "date-time" appear across shipped connector manifests — apple_health, apple_screen_time, chrome_history, chrome_downloads, apple_photos. This isn't a convention I'm inventing for the ERP; it's already the house style.
  • The components already exist. ui/calendar.tsx and ui/date-range-picker.tsx are built and tested. The range picker is wired into the events filter bar.
  • The form ignores both. dynamic-schema-form.tsx branches on format exactly once — for uri/url. A format: "date" field renders as a plain text box today.

So this is not new construction: it is connecting a schema convention that already ships to a component that already exists. It also fixes every existing manifest that declares a date, not just the ERP. The entity-lookup field (x-link-entity-type) is the genuinely new one of the three, and it's the one every ERP screen needs most — no document exists without picking a customer.

Section 06

The gap register

Everything still open, with the correction from Section 01 applied. Product-surface items that a capable agent dissolves — PDF rendering, Excel, i18n, report building, e-invoice transmission — are not listed; they were removed in an earlier round and the owner has since confirmed they are on e-Fatura, which also retires the pre-printed stationery question for good.

GapStatus in codeSizeWP
Audit coverage & durability Update is fully diffed and attributed. Create/delete/link/merge are not. Write is fire-and-forget, post-commit. Medium WP-1
Data-dependent write rules Interceptor pipeline exists, tested, extensible. Registration is compile-time; humans short-circuit to allow at entity-policy.ts:796 (+3 more). Medium WP-2
Form field types Schema convention shipped, calendar component built, form wires neither. No entity-lookup control at all. Small WP-3
Human-vs-human concurrency FOR UPDATE serializes; field_controls resolves human-vs-agent. No version token for two humans. Small WP-4

Row-level read scope member_of graph + fail-closed read gate fully built — wired to events, not entities. Medium deferred
Runtime component registry components and actions registries exist in the renderer; neither is supplied at any call site. Medium deferred

Section 07

Work packages

Five packages, ordered so each is independently shippable and reviewable. WP-3 and WP-4 are genuinely parallel — separate files, no shared surface. WP-1 and WP-2 both touch the entity write path and should not run concurrently.

WP-1

Consolidate entity audit onto events

Extend recordChangeEvent coverage to create, delete, link, unlink, merge, unmerge and update-link, each with a real before/after payload. Then make it durable for types that ask for it: write the audit row inside the entity transaction rather than post-commit, so it commits with the change or the change fails. Blocked on Q2.

manage_entity.ts (7 handlers) · utils/insert-event.ts · entity-management.ts:616 (the open tx)

WP-2

Data-driven mutation interceptor

One new interceptor file that reads its rules from entity-type data rather than code, so an agent can author them through manage_entity_schema with no deploy. Covers both the freeze and the transition constraint — they're the same check. Requires opening the human short-circuit, which is the part that needs care and its own review.

authz/ (one new file) · authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts:186 · authz/entity-policy.ts:796,883,916,976

WP-3

Date, datetime and entity-lookup form fields

Branch dynamic-schema-form.tsx on format: "date" and "date-time" into the existing calendar component, and add an entity-lookup control driven by x-link-entity-type / x-link-lookup-field. Fixes shipped connector manifests too, not just the ERP.

owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx · ui/calendar.tsx · ui/date-range-picker.tsx

WP-4

Optimistic concurrency token

Return a version stamp on read, require it on update, compare inside the transaction that already holds the row lock, reject on mismatch. Small, but load-bearing once document lines live in one JSON cell — otherwise the second save silently discards the first writer's entire line array.

entity-management.ts:616–623 (inside the existing sql.begin + FOR UPDATE)

WP-5

Entity-sourced, materialized measures

Teach the metric compiler a second source — entities as well as events — and materialize the result at write time with a defined recompute path. This is the only genuine new structure in the list. Design review first; not a codex task yet.

metrics/compiler.ts · metrics/run-metric.ts · entity_types.metrics_config

Section 08

What I need from you

Three decisions gate the packages above. Everything else I can carry.

  • Q1 — immutability by rule or by structure? A gate that refuses edits to a posted document, or posted documents that are append-only so there is nothing to refuse. The second is closer to what you're asking for and further from what exists. This decides WP-2's shape and part of the data model.
  • Q2 — should durable audit be global or per-entity-type? Writing the audit row inside the transaction makes a failed audit fail the user's edit. Right for an invoice, arguably wrong for a note. Per-type is my recommendation; global is simpler and more honest. WP-1 is blocked on this.
  • Q3 — S6, confirm the two-stage plan? Derived types for the PoC, entity-sourced materialized measures for the product. Both are in WP-5; I want the fable review's verdict before you commit to the second.

Still outstanding from Prodma's owner, now down to two: the untruncated YETKI sheets with column headers — the current permission counts are floors, cut at 200 rows — and an hour watching ten to fifteen screens in real daily use. e-Fatura is answered.

Entity types

Sixteen types for the Quote → Invoice slice, with lines stored as a JSON array inside the document row. Field counts are the Prodma column counts; the PoC carries a working subset.

You are reviewing an architecture plan as a skeptical senior reviewer. Your job is to find where it is WRONG, not to praise it. Read-only — do not edit any files.

CONTEXT: We are evaluating whether a Turkish manufacturing ERP (Prodma: .NET WinForms + SQL Server, 503 DbSets, 441 screens, 637k live LOC) can be rebuilt on Lobu, an agent platform monorepo. Repo to inspect: /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/prodma-gap-audit (branch is current main). Scale target: under 20 concurrent users. This is a proof-of-concept to find where Lobu falls short, not a migration.

Key design decisions already locked:
- Document lines (invoice lines etc.) stored as a JSON array inside `entities.metadata`, so header+lines = ONE row = ONE write = naturally atomic.
- Deterministic pricing/VAT rules run in the Lobu sandbox (read + compute), result written in that single write.
- Posted invoices immutable.
- Row-level authz wanted (salesperson sees own customers only).

THE PLAN I WANT YOU TO ATTACK — five work packages:
- WP-1 Consolidate entity audit onto `events`. Today `manage_entity.ts:547` calls `recordChangeEvent` on UPDATE only, with a real {field, old, new} diff, createdBy, entity_ids, semantic_type='change'. Missing on create/delete/link/unlink/merge/unmerge/update_link. It is fire-and-forget (never throws, 2 retries then logs ERROR and drops) and runs POST-COMMIT outside the entity transaction. Plan: extend coverage, and make the audit row commit INSIDE the entity transaction for entity types that opt in.
- WP-2 A data-driven mutation interceptor. `packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts` is an interceptor pipeline (allow/deny/defer) in front of every user-facing entity write; `registerMutationInterceptor` at :186 is compile-time and outside tests is NEVER called (only `approvalInterceptor` ships). `entity-policy.ts:796,883,916,976` short-circuit `principalKind === "user"` to allow, so the gate binds agents but not humans. Plan: one new interceptor that reads its rules from entity-type data (so agents author policy at runtime via manage_entity_schema, no deploy), covering both "frozen once posted" and legal state transitions; and open the human short-circuit.
- WP-3 Wire `format: "date"` / `"date-time"` in `packages/owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx` to the existing `ui/calendar.tsx`, and add an entity-lookup control driven by `x-link-entity-type`.
- WP-4 Optimistic concurrency token, compared inside the existing `sql.begin` + `FOR UPDATE` in `packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:616-623`.
- WP-5 Teach `packages/server/src/metrics/compiler.ts` a second source (entities, not just events) and materialize measures at write time. Today it emits `FROM events` only, resolves entities by `eventSet.by:"alias"` text matching, and cross-entity joins are NotImplemented. There is ZERO `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` in all migrations.

Also under debate, and I especially want your verdict here:
(Q1) Immutability by RULE (a gate refuses edits to a posted doc) versus by STRUCTURE (posted docs are append-only; corrections create a superseding version, following the existing `events.supersedes_event_id` pattern and the repo's "never DELETE, tombstone instead" invariant). Which is actually right given `entities` is mutated in place and entity identity/dedupe/relationships all point at a single row id?
(Q2) Should durable (in-transaction) audit be global or per-entity-type?
(Q3) Is the two-stage aggregate plan (derived `backing_sql` types for the PoC, entity-sourced materialized measures for the product) sound, or is there a better shape already latent in the repo?

Read `AGENTS.md` at the repo root first — it has hard invariants that constrain all of this (notably: "Request paths never aggregate history", "events is append-only", "Coordination design brake", "Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state", multi-replica correctness). Judge the plan against those invariants specifically.

WHAT TO RETURN (be concise and concrete, cite file:line):
1. Any claim in the plan above that is factually WRONG about the code. Verify the central ones yourself rather than trusting me.
2. The single biggest risk in the plan that I have not named.
3. Your verdict on Q1, Q2, Q3 with reasoning — pick one, don't survey.
4. Anything in WP-1..WP-5 that is mis-sized (I called WP-3/WP-4 small, WP-1/WP-2 medium, WP-5 large).
5. Whether the ordering is right, and specifically whether WP-2's "open the human short-circuit" is safe to do at all — that short-circuit may be load-bearing for reasons I haven't understood.

Do not write files. Return your findings as your final message.

---
name: reference_entity_change_history_already_exists
description: "Lobu DOES record field-level entity change history via recordChangeEvent — I wrongly claimed it didn't by grepping for literal `INSERT INTO events` inside manage_entity.ts"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

`manage_entity.ts:547` (handleUpdate) calls `recordChangeEvent` with a **real field-level diff**:
`metadata.changes = [{field, old, new}]`, plus `createdBy`, `clientId`, `entityIds`, landing in
`events` with `semantic_type='change'` (indexed by `idx_events_entity_ids`).

A whole audit family exists in `utils/insert-event.ts`: `recordChangeEvent`,
`recordConfigChangeEvent`, `recordWorkspaceChangeEvent`, `recordLifecycleEvent`, all routed through
`insertConnectionlessAuditEvent`, which enforces idempotency via a reserved
`metadata._lobu_idempotency_key` + `idx_events_org_idempotency_key`.

**The trap that produced a wrong finding:** I grepped `manage_entity.ts` for `INSERT INTO events`,
found nothing, and reported "writes NO event and NO audit row". The write goes through a *helper*.
Grepping for raw SQL inside a call site proves nothing about whether a write happens — grep for the
**concept** (`audit`, `recordChange`, `Event(`) or trace the imports. Same class as
[[feedback_absence_needs_origin_main_grep]]: absence needs the right probe, not just a probe.

**Real gaps (verified, narrower than my claim):**
- Only `handleUpdate` records. `handleCreate`, `handleDelete`, `handleLink`, `handleUnlink`,
  `handleMerge`, `handleUnmerge`, `handleUpdateLink` record nothing.
- `recordChangeEvent` is **fire-and-forget** — never throws, retries twice, then logs ERROR and
  DROPS the row. Not acceptable as a legal audit trail.
- It runs **post-commit**, outside `updateEntity`'s transaction (`entity-management.ts:616`).
- `content` diffs are redacted to the literal string `"[changed]"`.
- Coverage is safe on one axis: `updateEntity` has exactly ONE caller (manage_entity.ts:480), and
  the sandbox `client.entities.*` routes through manage_entity actions — so there is no unaudited

description: "Every declarative layer in Lobu is agent-writable at runtime via manage_entity_schema — the entity mutation gate is the sole exception, and that asymmetry is the real extensibility gap"
