packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:696 — runMutationGate already receives the tx

Order

Spike 1  ──▶  Spike 2  ──▶  Spike 5       entity write path — sequential, same files
Spike 3                                   Owletto form renderer — independent, start now
Spike 4                                   derived type + seed data — independent, start now

client payload fix                        one file, no spike needed — bundle into Spike 3

The concurrency fix stopped being a spike when it stopped being a server change. Sending only changed keys is a small edit in the same file Spike 3 already opens, so it rides along. Spike 5 goes last of the three write-path spikes because it extends the seam Spike 1 opens.

Section 08

Two things Lobu can't do yet

Everything above this point was a gap that dissolved on inspection. These two didn't. I found them by asking whether the design was actually complete rather than whether each piece of it worked — which is a different question, and the one I should have asked two rounds ago.

GAP 1

A transition can refuse a write, but it cannot cause one

What's missing
The entity lifecycle hook registry has exactly three points — beforeCreate, afterCreate, beforeDelete. There is no update hook of any kind. So the moment that matters most in an ERP, a document changing state, is the one moment nothing can attach to.
Why it matters here
Posting an invoice must write a journal entry. Dispatching a delivery note must write stock movements. In double-entry accounting these aren't follow-up tasks, they're part of the same fact — an invoice that's posted without its journal entry is a book that doesn't balance, and every report built on it is wrong until someone notices.
Why a Behavior isn't the answer
An agent reacting to the change event would be asynchronous, non-deterministic, and an agent-attributed write — so it lands late, might phrase itself differently each time, and runs into the same ownership rules that block background recalculation. For arithmetic that must be exactly right and must be simultaneous, that's the wrong instrument.
Why it's probably small
The seam already exists and already has everything needed. The mutation gate runs inside the caller's transaction and receives both the current and proposed values. An update hook at the same point is an addition to a registry, not a new architecture — and it's the same compile-time-only extension asymmetry I've already flagged twice, which is why I believe it rather than suspecting I've misread again.
Real gap. Spike 5. The one finding here that could still change the answer.

packages/server/src/utils/entity-hooks.ts:27–36 — the whole hook interface packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:424, :519, :942 — the only three call sites

GAP 2

Nothing allocates a document number

What's missing
Every quote, order, delivery note and invoice needs a number a human can say out loud on the phone. There is no sequence primitive for entity metadata — no allocator, no per-series counter, nothing. I wrote document_no as readOnly in the schema two rounds ago and never said what would fill it in.
How much of it is actually a problem
Less than it first looks. The legally-constrained number is the e-invoice number, and that format is the integrator's job — Innova assigns it when the invoice is submitted, so we receive it rather than generate it. What's left is internal numbering for the documents that never reach the tax authority, where the requirement is uniqueness and rough ordering, not the gapless sequence the tax rules demand.
Which makes it small, not absent
A per-org, per-series counter allocated in the same transaction as the document. It rides on whatever Spike 5 concludes about hooks — if a write can happen at create time deterministically, this is a few lines inside it.
Real but minor. Rides on Spike 5; not worth its own spike until that answer lands.

content.text:
Not set — asking that question found two things nothing in Lobu can do. Artifact updated, same URL, new Section 06.

**A transition can refuse a write, but it cannot cause one.** The entity lifecycle hook registry has exactly three points: `beforeCreate`, `afterCreate`, `beforeDelete`. There is no update hook of any kind — grep exits 1 on `beforeUpdate|afterUpdate`, and there are only three call sites. So the moment that matters most in an ERP, a document changing state, is the one moment nothing can attach to.

That's load-bearing here. Posting an invoice must write a journal entry; dispatching a delivery note must write stock movements. In double-entry those aren't follow-up tasks, they're part of the same fact — an invoice posted without its journal entry is a book that doesn't balance, and every report built on it is wrong until someone notices. A Behavior reacting to the change event doesn't cover it: async, non-deterministic, and agent-attributed, so it also runs into the ownership rules that block background recalculation.

I think it's small, though. The mutation gate already runs inside the caller's transaction at `entity-management.ts:696` and already holds both current and proposed values. An update hook at that same point is a registry addition, not a new architecture. And it's the same compile-time-only extension asymmetry I've now flagged three times — the interceptor registry, the hook registry, both extensible only by someone deploying code — which is why I believe this one rather than suspecting I've misread again. It's spike 5, last of the write-path three since it extends the seam spike 1 opens.

**Nothing allocates a document number.** No sequence primitive for entity metadata, no per-series counter, nothing. I wrote `document_no` as `readOnly` two rounds ago and never said what fills it in. Smaller than it looks: the legally-constrained number is the e-invoice number and Innova assigns that on submission, so we receive it. What's left is internal numbering for documents that never reach the tax authority, where the requirement is uniqueness and rough ordering, not a gapless sequence. It rides on whatever spike 5 concludes about hooks — not worth its own spike until that lands.

Everything else is set. Of the four original spikes: the interceptor uses a designed extension point, the audit fix moves an existing call inside an existing transaction, the balance is pure configuration with no code at all. The only genuinely net-new *feature* in the original set is the form controls — an array-of-objects grid, a date control, an entity picker — and those are Owletto components, not platform primitives.

---

**Confidence 96** on the missing update hook — I read the full interface and grepped both hook names with a clean miss; it's a small, checkable claim. **~75** on "it's a small fix": that rests on the gate seam being reusable for a write, which I've reasoned from the code rather than tried, and it's exactly the kind of inference that's been wrong twice in this project. Spike 5 is designed to fail loudly if the side effect can't share the transaction. **~70** on the e-Fatura numbering claim — that's domain knowledge about how Innova works, unverified against their integration docs.

Next:
1. Dispatch spikes 3 and 4 now — still unblocked, and neither touches any of this.
2. Confirm with the owner that Innova returns the invoice number rather than expecting one — it decides whether gap 2 stays minor.
3. Run spike 1, then use what it learns about the gate seam to size spike 5 properly before committing to it.
4. Worth a decision: if spike 5 fails, whether an ERP with late-arriving journal entries is still worth demoing, or whether that's the finding that ends the PoC.

# SPIKE 3 — generic entity form must handle a real ERP document

You are working in a git worktree of the Lobu monorepo. **Use ONLY relative paths inside your
working directory. Absolute paths outside it are auto-rejected.**

All work is in the `packages/owletto` submodule (a separate git repo checked out inside this one).

## The question this spike answers

Can a real invoice — twelve line items, per-line VAT, a due date, a customer chosen by name — be
entered and re-read on Lobu's GENERIC entity page, with no screen written for invoices specifically?

If it needs a bespoke component per document type, this spike has FAILED and you must say so
plainly in the report. That is a valid and useful outcome. Do not paper over it.

## Read these first

- `packages/owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx` — the whole renderer. Note line ~300:
  `if (prop.type === "array" && prop.items?.type === "string")` is the ONLY array branch, and
  line ~334 (`uri`/`url`) is the ONLY `format` branch.
- `packages/owletto/src/components/entities/entity-table-view.tsx` — read side. Note it already
  consumes the `x-link-entity-type` keyword (~line 201).
- `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx` — line ~105.

## Task A — date and date-time controls

`{ "type": "string", "format": "date" }` currently renders as a plain text input. Add proper
controls for `format: "date"` and `format: "date-time"`, matching the existing shadcn/ui idiom used
elsewhere in this codebase. Values must round-trip as ISO strings.

## Task B — array-of-objects control (the important one)

`{ "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": {...} } }` has NO control and NO
display. This is every document's line-items grid.

Build an editable grid: one row per array element, one column per declared property, add-row and
remove-row. Each cell must reuse the SAME per-property control logic the top-level form already
uses, including the new date control and the entity picker from Task C — do NOT fork a second
rendering path. Respect `readOnly` on a property (render, don't edit).

Then make the READ side render it too — an array of objects must be legible in the entity view, not
printed as raw JSON.

## Task C — entity picker for `x-link-entity-type`

A property declaring `"x-link-entity-type": "customer"` should offer a searchable picker of that
type's entities and display the resolved name, not the raw integer id. The server ALREADY resolves
these to `{slug, name}` — find that in the API response shape before you build anything, and use it.
`x-link-lookup-field` names the property to display.

## Task D — send only changed keys

`entity-tabs/index.tsx:105` sends `metadata: metadataDirty ? metadata : undefined` — one dirty flag
for the WHOLE object, so every save carries the sender's stale copy of every field.

The server merges per key inside a row lock, so sending only the changed keys makes concurrent
edits to different fields both land correctly. Compute the changed keys against the same
`cleanFormData` baseline the file already uses and send only those.

Be careful: a key the user CLEARED must still be sent (as null/empty), or clearing a field silently
does nothing. Handle removals explicitly and say in your report how you did it.

## Proof required — do not skip

1. `cd packages/owletto && bunx tsc -b --noEmit` clean.
2. A test for the array-of-objects control covering: render existing rows, add a row, remove a row,
   edit a cell.
3. A test for Task D covering: change one field of three → only that key is sent; clear a field →
   the clearing is still transmitted.
4. Run the existing suite and report the result honestly. If something was already failing before
   you started, say so and show it.

## Report

Write `_spike/REPORT-form.md` (relative path, inside this worktree) containing:
- Answer to the question above: yes or no, and what it took.
- Every file you changed, with a one-line reason.
- The test output, pasted, not summarized.
- Anything you found that contradicts this brief. The brief was written from a read of the code,
  not from running it — if it is wrong, saying so IS the deliverable.
- What you did NOT do and why.

Do not commit. Leave the changes in the working tree.

# SPIKE 4 — at what row count does a customer balance stop being instant?

You are working in a git worktree of the Lobu monorepo. **Use ONLY relative paths inside your
working directory. Absolute paths outside it are auto-rejected.**

## What this spike is

A MEASUREMENT, not a feature. The deliverable is a table of numbers and a threshold. Do not
optimize anything. Do not add caching, indexes-beyond-what-production-has, or a materialized view.
If the answer is "it's fast, this was never a problem", that is a successful spike.

## Background you need

Lobu stores every domain object as a row in `entities` with a `metadata jsonb` body and an
`entity_type_id`. A "derived entity type" is one whose rows are not stored at all: the type carries
`backing_sql`, a plain SQL SELECT, and reading the type runs that query live.

We want `customer_balance` as a derived type: per customer, the sum of their posted invoices minus
the sum of their payments. Both invoices and payments are `entities` rows with jsonb metadata.

The concern is that this is a `GROUP BY` over a table that grows forever, on a user-facing read
path. We need to know whether it actually matters at a manufacturing SME's volume.

## Steps

1. Stand up a Postgres with the production `entities` / `entity_types` schema. The real DDL is in
   `db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql` — `entities` is at roughly line 1016 and
   `entity_types` at roughly line 1275. Use the REAL table definition including its indexes; a
   simplified table would measure the wrong thing. Say in your report exactly how you did this.

2. Write the `backing_sql` for `customer_balance`. It should:
   - read invoice rows (`entity_type_id` = the invoice type) with `metadata->>'status' = 'posted'`
   - read payment rows
   - group by the customer id stored in `metadata->>'customer_id'`
   - return customer id, total invoiced, total paid, balance
   Amounts live in `metadata->>'grand_total'` and `metadata->>'amount'` as JSON numbers — cast
   carefully and say what you did.

3. Seed and measure at these scales, keeping a realistic ratio of about 200 invoices per customer
   and 1.5 payments per invoice:

   | invoices | measure |
   |---------:|---------|
   |    1,000 | full-type read, and single-customer read |
   |   10,000 | same |
   |  100,000 | same |
   |1,000,000 | same |

   For each: run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and record the actual execution time. Take the median
   of 5 runs after one warm-up. Report both the whole-type query and the single-customer query —
   they are different questions and the single-customer one is what a user actually opens.

4. Report the threshold: at what row count does the single-customer read exceed 200ms, and at what
   count does the whole-type read exceed 1s?

## Things that will make this measurement a lie — avoid them

- Measuring on an empty cache every time, or never. Say which you did.
- Forgetting that production wraps this query in an org-scoping CTE. Look at
  `packages/server/src/utils/execute-data-sources.ts` around line 815 to see the shape a derived
  type actually executes inside, and measure that shape, not a bare SELECT.
- Seeding all rows with the same customer id, or sequential ids that cluster perfectly. Randomize.
- Reporting a number without the row count and hardware it came from.

## Report

Write `_spike/REPORT-balance.md` (relative path, inside this worktree) containing:
- The table of measurements, with the query text you actually ran.
- The two thresholds.
- Your verdict in one sentence: is a plain derived view enough for a company doing a few tens of
  thousands of invoices a year?
- Anything in this brief that turned out to be wrong.

Do not commit application code. The seed and measurement scripts should live under `_spike/`.

# SPIKE 1 — can a rule written at runtime stop a person from editing a posted invoice?

You are working in a git worktree of the Lobu monorepo. **Use ONLY relative paths inside your
working directory. Absolute paths outside it are auto-rejected.**

## The question

An entity type declares a rule as DATA on its JSON schema. A posted invoice must then be
un-editable — by an agent AND by a human — with the rule changeable at runtime and no redeploy.

## Read these first, in this order

1. `packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts` — the whole file. The header comment tells
   you the intended extension mechanism: one new interceptor file, appended to
   `BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS`. Follow that, and respect the import-cycle note (keep exports as hoisted
   `function` declarations, keep the import static).
2. `packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts` lines 600–800 — `updateEntity`'s transaction.
3. `packages/server/src/authz/entity-policy.ts` — specifically the `principalKind === "user"`
   short-circuits and the branch that makes a human-owned field `require_approval`.

## Facts established by reading the code — trust these, but verify as you go

- `UpdateMutationRequest` carries `fields: Record<string, FieldOwner>` — **field names and owners
  ONLY. It does NOT carry the current or proposed VALUES.** So an interceptor cannot see that
  `status` is going `draft` → `posted`. This is the central obstacle of this spike.
- The interceptor receives `req.sql`, which is the CALLER'S OPEN TRANSACTION. It can therefore
  SELECT the row's current state itself.
- For updates, `runMutationGate` is currently never called for humans at all —
  `entity-management.ts:654` wraps the whole call in `if (!isHumanEdit)`.

## Task A — the freeze, using only today's contract

Add `packages/server/src/authz/transition-interceptor.ts`. It reads the entity type's
`metadata_schema -> 'x-transitions'` and enforces the freeze:

```
"x-transitions": {
  "field": "status",
  "allowed": { "draft": ["issued","cancelled"], "issued": ["posted"], "posted": [] },
  "frozen_from": "issued"
}
```

Freeze semantics: once the row's current state is `frozen_from` or a state reachable only from it,
NO field may change. The interceptor can implement this today by SELECTing the current state on
`req.sql`. Deny with a clear reason naming the document and its state.

It must deny **regardless of `principalKind`** — this is a data-dependent rule, not a permission.
Unknown/absent `x-transitions` ⇒ return `null` (no opinion). A malformed one ⇒ fail closed and log.

## Task B — carry the values, so transitions can be checked at all

Extend `UpdateMutationRequest` with the current and proposed values, and populate them at the call
site (`entity-management.ts` ~line 696) from the already-locked `existing` row and from
`metadataUpdates`. Then enforce transition legality: a move to a state not listed in
`allowed[current]` is denied.

This is an internal TypeScript interface, not a database, API or SDK surface — you may change it.
Update every construction site and every test that builds one.

## Task C — route human updates through the gate

Today the gate is skipped entirely for humans. Change that so the interceptor sees human edits too.

**Read this paragraph twice — it is the trap in this spike.** Do NOT remove or weaken the
`principalKind === "user"` short-circuits in `entity-policy.ts`. They are load-bearing: downstream
of them sits a branch making any human-OWNED field `require_approval` unconditionally, which is only
correct because the caller is never human. If you route humans in while marking fields as
human-owned, every person editing a field they themselves last touched gets an approval card
addressed to themselves.

The safe shape: call `runMutationGate` for human edits, but build the `fields` map with every owner
as `"none"` — ownership is a human-vs-agent concept and is meaningless when the writer IS the human.
This preserves today's behaviour exactly (humans were never gated on ownership) while letting the
new interceptor see the request. Prove this with a test: a human edits a field they previously set,
and NO approval is queued.

## Task D — close the second door

`packages/server/src/tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts` around line 1085,
`applyEntityFieldChangeProposal`, writes through `mergeEntityFields` with no gate call anywhere in
the file. A change proposed while an invoice was a draft and approved after it was posted walks
straight into the frozen document. Enforce the freeze there too.

## Proof required — a spike without a falsification attempt is worthless

Write real tests (this repo uses embedded Postgres for integration tests — follow the existing
pattern in `packages/server/src/__tests__/`):

1. Agent tries to edit a posted invoice → denied.
2. **Human** tries to edit a posted invoice → denied. (This is the headline claim.)
3. Human edits a DRAFT invoice → succeeds, and no approval is queued.
4. Human edits a field they themselves previously set on a draft → succeeds, no approval queued.
   (Guards the Task C trap.)
5. `draft → posted` (skipping `issued`) → denied as an illegal transition.
6. `draft → issued` → allowed.
7. A proposal approved after the document froze → does not write.
8. An entity type with no `x-transitions` → completely unaffected.
9. Changing the rule via the schema (not a redeploy) changes the outcome.

Run the FULL existing server test suite and report what it did. If you broke something, say so.

## Report

Write `_spike/REPORT-writepath.md` (relative path, inside this worktree):
- Does the freeze bind a human? Yes/no, with the test output pasted.
- What Task B actually cost — every call site you had to touch.
- Anything in this brief that was wrong. It was written from reading, not running.

It doesn't. `UpdateMutationRequest` carries `fields: Record<string, FieldOwner>` — field names and ownership, nothing else. Create requests carry their payload and delete requests carry a snapshot; update is the one that carries neither. A **transition check** can't: judging `draft → posted` needs the proposed value threaded into the request first. It's an internal TypeScript interface rather than a database or API surface, so it's changeable without asking you, but it's real work I had costed at zero. content.text:
Spike 4 has landed with real measurements. Verified against its own EXPLAIN artifacts rather than its summary — and the plan tells a different story than the verdict.

**The numbers are real.** Scratch Postgres 18, the actual baseline DDL plus the three derived-type migrations, warm cache, median of 5 after a warm-up. Single-customer balance: 0.76ms at 1k invoices, 6.5ms at 10k, 23ms at 100k, 181ms at 1M. Whole-type: 1.2ms / 10.7ms / 51ms / 520ms.

**Its verdict overstates.** It reports "comfortably under 200 ms at 1,000,000 invoices." 181ms is within 10% of the line, on an M4 Pro with a warm cache and three parallel workers. A shared production pod with a cold cache has none of those advantages.

**And it missed the structural finding.** The plan is a parallel `Seq Scan` on `entities` removing 833k and 1.25M rows per worker — it reads all 2.5M rows to answer for one customer. So the single-customer read is O(everything in the org), not O(that customer's invoices). Opening one customer's balance scans every invoice and payment in the company, and that grows linearly forever for every user regardless of which customer they open. Base directory for this skill: /Users/burakemre/.claude/skills/lobu

# Lobu

Use this skill when setting up a brand-new Lobu agent from scratch (follow "Onboarding a New Project" below) or when running, validating, evaluating, or connecting an existing Lobu project, or operating Lobu memory from a coding agent.

The `AGENTS.md` generated into a new project is the source of truth for the config API (the `define*` helpers, connectors, auth, Behaviors, memory) — this skill does not duplicate it. For an existing project, jump to "Core Model" + the relevant reference section below.

## Onboarding a New Project

Use this playbook when a new user asks you to build them a Lobu agent from scratch. Set it up end to end: ground yourself in what the user already has, interview, discover, scaffold, prove the complete local path, then offer the deployment choice. Do not call the setup complete until every path the user selected has actually passed end to end. If an external provider, authorization, deployment, or rate limit blocks the proof, name the exact blocker and leave the setup as blocked rather than claiming success.

### 1. Ground yourself in what the user already has

Before interviewing, look at what already exists so your questions and suggestions are personal rather than a blank slate. This is discovery, not a design decision — do not let it skip the interview.

- Local: run `lobu context list` to see existing contexts; check the current directory and home for existing Lobu projects (`lobu.config.ts`), configured MCP servers, and CLI auth state. Note what the user already set up.
- Cloud: if the user has an active session (do not create one just to look), call `client.organizations.list()`, `client.agents.list()` for each org, `client.catalog.listInstalled({ kinds: ["connectors"] })`, and `search_memory` for prior knowledge. This reveals existing agents, connectors, and memory you can build on.
- Tell the user what you are looking at so they can correct you, and let what you find shape the options you offer. Never treat this discovery as an identity signal: orgs, emails, or domains never prove a company or product, and never mention a competitor or third party unless it actually appears in what you found.

Do NOT ask for a login email during the interview. Email is only needed when a managed connector actually requires a session (step 3) or when the user chooses cloud deployment (step 6); ask for it at that point. Treat identity only as identity; never infer a company from an email address or domain.

### 2. Interview with concrete, personalized options

Interview the user one question at a time; wait for each answer, do not guess, and do not batch the questions. Anchor each question in what you found in step 1. Instead of asking "what agent do you want?" as a blank slate, summarize what you see and offer two or three concrete alternatives to choose from:

- "You already have org X with connectors A and B installed and N existing agents. Do you want to (a) add a new agent on top of those, (b) extend one of the existing agents, or (c) start something standalone?"
- "For what it should do, the common shapes are (a) a triage agent that reads incoming chat and files a ticket, (b) a scheduled report that summarizes new activity each morning, (c) a research agent that answers questions from your connected tools. Which fits, or what would you change?"

Offer a default so the user can answer "the first one" — decisive users and undecided users both move faster with a concrete menu.

- What company or product is this for?
- What does it do, and who does it serve?
- What is its public domain? (optional for a personal project)
- Do I have permission to research the public website and other public sources?
- What is the agent for?
- What should we call it?
- Who uses it: just me, my team, or each of my customers?
- How should it behave, and what may it do unattended versus only with approval?
- What should it remember? Model this as one to three entity types.
- Where does its data come from? Pick one connector or custom source to start.
- Where should people talk to it? Offer Web UI, API or SDK, MCP, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Discord, Google Chat, and Telegram without forcing a chat platform. If Slack is chosen, ask whether to join Lobu's hosted workspace for a quick start, install Lobu into an existing workspace, or use a custom Slack app; then ask whether to test the DM with Lobu, a named channel, or both, and whether people knowledge means conversation participants, bound-channel members, or the full workspace directory.
- Should anything run on a schedule?
- Which supported LLM provider credential does the user have?

If the user gave permission to research and has a public domain, research the company before proposing the design. Summarize its product, customers, workflows, and useful signals, and cite the public sources you used. Then propose one to three entity types, their relationships, the first data source, one or two useful Behaviors, and suitable interaction channels. Play back a short numbered plan and wait for confirmation before scaffolding anything.

### 3. Discover the surface before choosing how to scaffold

Check Node is 22-24 or 26+ (only Node 25 is unsupported), then run `lobu context list` and identify the named Lobu Cloud context; do not assume the active context still points to cloud after a local run. If a managed or cloud connector was chosen and there is no session, ask for the login email at that point, explain that Lobu will email an approval link, and run `lobu login --email <confirmed-address> --context <cloud-name>`. The person approving must sign in with that same email; knowing an address never grants access. After a successful login, an empty organization membership list is a tenancy/discovery result, not an authentication failure: call `client.organizations.list()` and explain the result. Never revoke or repeat login with `--force` unless the user separately approves that re-authentication.

Use ClientSDK through Lobu MCP or `lobu memory exec` with the explicit cloud context. Call `client.organizations.list()` to find public organizations offering managed connections. Call `client.catalog.listInstalled({ kinds: ["connectors"] })`; if the connector is not installed, call `client.catalog.listCatalog({ kinds: ["connectors"] })`. Inspect the selected entry's `detail.auth_schema`, `detail.options_schema`, `detail.feeds_schema`, and `detail.behavior_events` instead of guessing field names. If a matching live managed offer exists, explain it and call `client.connections.connectManaged` only after consent. Complete the returned user authorization, then run `lobu context use <cloud-name>` immediately before executing its `local_bootstrap_command` from the parent directory where the new project should be created; use `--here` only after entering an empty directory, and do not create a blank Lobu scaffold first. Ask for bring-your-own OAuth credentials only if no managed offer exists or the user prefers their own app.

**If no connector in the catalog matches the data source, do not report "no integration exists"** — author a custom connector: write `connectors/<name>.connector.ts` in the project, register it with `connectorFromFile("./connectors/<name>.connector.ts")`, and model it on the [npm downloads example](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/examples/lobu-crm/npm-downloads.connector.ts). See [Connector authoring](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/docs/connector-authoring.md) for the full contract; the end-to-end entity/event/Behavior model is in [Lobu concepts](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/docs/CONCEPTS.md).

### 4. Scaffold and build from the confirmed plan

If managed auth supplied a `local_bootstrap_command`, use the project it generated. Otherwise run `npx @lobu/cli@latest init` with the confirmed name and provider. Postgres is built in, so `lobu run` starts an embedded database; ask for `DATABASE_URL` only if the user chooses external Postgres. Read the generated `AGENTS.md` completely before editing `lobu.config.ts`. Use the canonical reference at `https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/examples/lobu-crm/lobu.config.ts` when needed; do not assume that example exists in the new project's filesystem. Briefly explain how the chosen feed may use checkpoints to collect incrementally, emits events, builds shared entity memory, and gives both chat and Behaviors the same governed context.

`feeds_schema.<feed>.eventKinds` are the default Behavior trigger catalog for feed connectors: every declared kind is a subscribable event type (`event_type` = the kind slug) for any feed that emits the kind. A feed's first successful non-dry sync establishes its baseline without activation; later inserts of a matching kind activate subscribers. Feed-scoped filtering is not yet available (events dedupe by connection + origin id, so a `feed_key` match would miss origins first seen by another feed). `behavior_events` (now derived from eventKinds when a connector declares none) is the trigger picker's list. If no declared kind matches the use case, use a scheduled Behavior with a bounded named SQL source and read event text from `payload_text`. Validate the query against the running local schema before relying on it. If `feeds_schema` is empty, do not invent or trigger a feed; chat integrations such as Slack can deliver incoming messages directly. For Slack or Telegram, prefer `defineConnection` with `credentialMode: "hosted"` so no bot token is required; `lobu run` prints the exact hosted-workspace join URL, own-workspace install URL when available, and short-lived link command. Use those returned values instead of constructing URLs. A printed `/lobu link <code>` is one-time: redeem it in the first selected DM or channel. In an installed workspace whose installer is linked to Lobu, bind each additional surface with `/lobu link <agent-id>`; otherwise generate a fresh code for that surface. Mention Lobu in a channel test and verify the App Home separately. Lobu email login and Slack installation are separate: the email link authorizes Lobu CLI access, while an existing-workspace install requires the user or workspace admin to approve Slack's OAuth screen. Never describe Slack consent as an email approval. Use `credentialMode: "byo"` only if the user chooses their own app. Tell the user once which remaining secrets are required and add only `secret("ENV_NAME")` placeholders to config. Never open or request permission to read `.env`; inspect `.env.example` when present and declared secret placeholder names only. Never read, print, invent, or paste a real secret into source or chat.

If the user wants the agent to know people in Slack, ask whether that means conversation participants, members of bound channels, or the full workspace directory. Installing the app proves none of those by itself. Verify the selected scope by inspecting the people or member entities Lobu actually materialized and by asking the agent a roster question. If human-readable names or non-participants are unavailable, identify that exact product gap; never claim the complete workspace directory was synced.

### 5. Prove the complete local path

Change into the generated project directory and verify `pwd` contains the intended `lobu.config.ts`; never run project commands from its parent. Run `npx @lobu/cli@latest validate`, boot with `npx @lobu/cli@latest run`, and verify health and the local Web UI. With the embedded database default, `lobu run` creates and selects the local context and auto-applies the project; with an external `DATABASE_URL`, it does neither, so authenticate and apply to that runtime explicitly. Send a harmless direct chat message without tools.

Before consent to access provider data, inspect only catalog, connection, auth-profile, and feed metadata. For a `browser_session` profile only, `npx @lobu/cli@latest connector run <key> --auth-profile <browser-session-profile-slug> --check` resolves the device-bound path without execution. Never use `connector run` as a generic managed OAuth or env-profile check; those durable credentials stay at the gateway. Do not run a feed or connector dry-run before consent, because a dry-run may still read provider data. Ask explicitly before accessing real provider data. Only after approval, dry-run the connector or feed server-side and trigger the selected feed manually if that connector actually declares one. A feed dry-run records its run but persists no collected events, entities, attachments, checkpoint changes, or feed sync state. Run each Behavior once, poll `client.operations.getRun` with its returned `run_id`, and show each completed run plus any declared result event or entity. For a Canvas-only or reaction-only Behavior, do not invent a persisted output; use the Behavior `view_url` returned by Lobu. For Slack, treat DM, channel mention, App Home, and requested member discovery as four separate checks. Keep actions in approval mode unless the user explicitly approves execution. If any step fails, fix it and rerun that step; do not silently substitute a different path.

### 6. Offer the deployment choice

After the local proof, ask the user whether to keep running locally or deploy to Lobu Cloud. Explain that the embedded local runtime and Lobu Cloud are separate targets, and that keeping it local needs no further setup. Only if the user chooses cloud deployment, ask for the login email to identify the deployer, explain that Lobu will email an approval link, and run `lobu login --email <confirmed-address> --context <cloud-name>`; the person approving must sign in with that same email. Because `lobu apply` has no context flag, use `lobu context list` and then `lobu context use <cloud-name>` to select an explicit cloud context before deployment. Run `lobu apply --dry-run` first, show the target organization and exact plan, and wait for confirmation before applying. After apply, use only authoritative `view_url` values and link commands returned by Lobu; never construct URLs. Present the working access choices: Web UI, direct agent chat, API or SDK, MCP, and any channels the user selected.

## Core Model

- **Lobu** is the agent framework, runtime, deployment layer, and memory surface.
- Keep framework configuration in `lobu.config.ts` (TypeScript, `defineConfig` from `@lobu/cli/config`).
- Keep agent identity and behavior in `IDENTITY.md`, `SOUL.md`, and `USER.md`.
- Keep reusable capability bundles in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` or `agents/<agent>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- Use `lobu login` for CLI authentication. Do not use a separate memory login command.
- Use `lobu memory ...` for memory operations, MCP client wiring, seeding, direct tool calls, and browser-auth capture.

Reference the canonical docs before guessing how a feature works:
[Lobu concepts](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/docs/CONCEPTS.md)
(entities vs events, identity, end-to-end lifecycle),
[Behaviors](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/docs/BEHAVIORS.md)
(trigger/source/output contract), and
[Connector authoring](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/blob/main/docs/connector-authoring.md)
(custom connectors).

## Project Checklist

1. Read `lobu.config.ts` first.
2. Read the active agent files under `agents/<id>/`.
3. Check local skills under `skills/` and `agents/<id>/skills/`.
4. Use `lobu validate` after config changes.
5. Discover the live SDK and connector surface with `search_sdk`; never guess a method, connector key, feed key, connection id, or operation key.
6. When prompt or Behavior changes, run evals via promptfoo (see `examples/personal-finance/evals/promptfooconfig.yaml`). The in-house `lobu eval` command has been removed.

## Common Commands

```bash
npx @lobu/cli@latest init my-agent
npx @lobu/cli@latest run
npx @lobu/cli@latest validate
npx @lobu/cli@latest login
```

## Authentication

- Interactive (human at a terminal): `lobu login` runs the device-code flow with a browser approval.
- CI / your own automation: `LOBU_API_TOKEN`, or `lobu login --token <pat>`.
- Local `lobu run`: the CLI mints credentials automatically over loopback — no prompt.
- Headless, on a *user's* behalf: `lobu login --email <address>`. The server emails the user a one-click approval link and the CLI polls until they approve, then stores the scoped credential — no TTY, no pre-minted token. This is the auth.md "user_claimed" flow.

An external agent not using this CLI can drive the same flow over HTTP: read `<origin>/auth.md` (linked from the `agent_auth` block in `<origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) for the endpoints. Today only the email user_claimed flow exists (no zero-touch ID-JAG). Never fabricate a token.

## Organization Deletion

Treat organization deletion as permanent and restricted to organization owners. The supported path is the **Organization settings** page, opened from that workspace's settings button in the organization switcher. ClientSDK and Lobu CLI intentionally expose no organization-delete method. When asked to delete organizations, identify each exact target and its data impact read-only, surface one production organization at a time for explicit confirmation, then direct an owner to that page or use their logged-in browser only when explicitly authorized. Never invent a hosted URL, call the raw Better Auth route, bypass a failed authorization check, delete organization rows directly, or batch confirmations.

Cloud CLI OAuth/PAT credentials are not a Better Auth browser session. A `401` or `403` is a stop signal: report the authorization boundary and leave the organization intact.

<!-- lobu-memory-guidance:start -->
## Memory Defaults

Your long-term memory is powered by Lobu. Do NOT use local files (memory/, MEMORY.md) for memory.
- Lobu automatically recalls relevant memories when you receive a message.
- To save something, call save_memory with the content and an appropriate semantic_type.
- To search, call search_memory. Results include view_url links to the web interface.
- NEVER construct Lobu URLs yourself. When the user asks for a link, call search_memory to get the correct view_url.
- When the user says "remember this", save it to Lobu immediately.
- When a message changes a fact you already stored (an updated preference, status, count, location, or plan), first search_memory for the prior memory to get its id, then save_memory the new value with supersedes_event_id set to that id. This replaces the stale value so future recalls return the current one; the old value stays in history but is hidden from normal search.
<!-- lobu-memory-guidance:end -->

## Lobu Memory

Configure project-scoped memory in `lobu.config.ts` by setting the org on `defineConfig` and declaring the schema with the `define*` helpers:

```ts
import { defineConfig, defineEntityType } from "@lobu/cli/config";

const ticket = defineEntityType({
  key: "ticket",
  name: "Ticket",
  properties: {
    subject: {
      type: "string",
      "x-table-label": "Subject",
      "x-table-column": true,
    },
  },
});

export default defineConfig({
  org: "my-org",
  orgName: "My workspace",
  agents: [/* ... */],
  entities: [ticket],
});
```

Seed data records still live as YAML under `./data`. Then seed or operate the memory workspace with:

```bash
lobu login
lobu memory org set <org-slug>
lobu memory health --org <org-slug>
lobu memory seed --org <org-slug>
lobu memory run search_memory '{"query":"Acme"}' --org <org-slug>
```

Use `search_memory` first when the user asks about a specific entity or workspace memory. Use `save_memory` to persist durable memory. To update existing knowledge, search first, then save with `supersedes_event_id` so the old row is tombstoned rather than deleted.

## MCP Client Setup

Use the actual MCP URL for the user's runtime. Never hardcode a hosted URL unless the user explicitly asks for that instance.

Common setup commands:

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http lobu <mcp-url>

# Codex
codex mcp add lobu --url <mcp-url>

# Gemini CLI
gemini mcp add --transport http lobu <mcp-url>

# Interactive client wiring wizard
lobu memory init --url <mcp-url>
```

For ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other browser-managed clients, paste the MCP URL into the client's MCP/connector settings and complete OAuth in the browser.

## Browser-Authenticated Connectors

For connectors that need a real browser session, `browser-auth` launches a dedicated Chrome with remote debugging, stores its CDP endpoint on the auth profile, and the connector attaches over CDP at sync time (harvesting cookies live):

```bash
lobu memory browser-auth --connector <key> --auth-profile-slug <slug>
lobu memory browser-auth --connector <key> --auth-profile-slug <slug> --check
```

Use `--dedicated-profile` only when you want a non-default dedicated Chrome profile directory; use `--remote-debug-port` to customize the CDP port (default `9222`).

## Agent-Facing Tool Surface

The normal MCP surface is intentionally small. Flat administrative tools are not advertised to agents; compose through these tools instead:

- `search_memory` and `save_memory` for direct knowledge recall and persistence.
- `search_sdk` to discover current ClientSDK methods, signatures, connector feed keys, operations, access requirements, and examples. Pass `mode: "read"` when you only need methods safe for `query_sdk`.
- `query_sdk` for read-only TypeScript and `query_sql` for governed, paginated SQL reads.
- `run_sdk` for mutations and external operations. Use `lobu memory exec` from the CLI for the same ClientSDK scripting workflow.

Search before create to avoid duplicates. Prefer a read or dry run before mutations, never fabricate returned URLs or identifiers, and never delete from `events`; supersede or tombstone instead.

## Connectors, Feeds, and Operations

Connectors are the primary integration path for third-party services. The
end-to-end model (entities vs events, the run lifecycle) is in
`docs/CONCEPTS.md`; authoring a new connector when none matches is in
`docs/connector-authoring.md`. Use this lifecycle:

1. Call `search_sdk` with the service name. It returns installed and installable connectors, declared feed keys, SDK methods, and readiness details.
2. Use `query_sdk` to inspect `client.catalog.listInstalled({ kinds: ["connectors"] })`, `client.catalog.listCatalog({ kinds: ["connectors"] })`, and `client.connections.list()` when you need a complete inventory.
3. In `run_sdk`, call `client.connections.connect({ connector_key })`. An `active` or `pending_auth` result carries a `connection_id`. A `setup_required` result is a continuation: follow its `next_action`, `resume_call`, or `completion_check` exactly and do not create a feed until a `connection_id` is present. If the result carries `self_install_url` (a Slack app bootstrap deep link), offer it to the user so they can create + install their own app and paste back the bot token / signing secret.
4. Create the feed with `client.feeds.create({ connection_id, feed_key, config })`. Connecting alone collects nothing.
5. Trigger and verify it with `client.feeds.trigger({ feed_id, dry_run: true })`, then inspect `client.feeds.get({ feed_id })`. A dry run prevents Lobu writes but cannot undo upstream side effects caused by the connector.

Virtual feeds query the provider live and can be read with `client.feeds.readMany(...)`; collected feeds persist events for search and relational queries.

Discover executable connector actions with `client.operations.listAvailable({ query, include_disconnected: true })`. Use the returned connection and operation target with `client.operations.execute({ connection_id, operation_key, input })`. If readiness is disconnected, follow the returned next action instead of guessing a connection. Approval-gated execution returns `pending_approval`; surface that state rather than treating it as failure.

## Data Ingestion

- Use `lobu memory seed` for small declarative YAML datasets under `./data`; it processes records sequentially and is not a bulk-backfill path.
- Use `client.knowledge.save` for schema-less semantic history such as messages, notes, observations, and content. Pass `supersedes_event_id` when replacing an existing fact.
- Use `client.entities.create` / `client.entities.update` only for strict structured records that match declared entity schemas.
- For large backfills, send bounded chunks through `run_sdk` / `lobu memory exec` and use `Promise.allSettled` so conflicts and partial failures remain visible.

```ts
export default async (_ctx, client) => {
  const records = [
    { content: "...", semantic_type: "note" },
    { content: "...", semantic_type: "observation" },
  ];
  return Promise.allSettled(records.map((record) => client.knowledge.save(record)));
};
```

## Anything in the brief that was wrong

1. The sample rule is internally contradictory if read literally:
   `allowed.issued = ["posted"]` says `issued -> posted` is legal, but `frozen_from = "issued"` says once the current state is `issued`, no field may change. In runtime terms, that means `issued -> posted` is blocked by the freeze. I kept the implementation faithful to the written freeze rule and, in the proof for Task D, forced the row to `posted` directly in SQL to test the second door.
2. `applyEntityFieldChangeProposal` does not only "write through mergeEntityFields". Metadata fields do, but reserved attributes (`$name`, `$parent_id`, `$content`) are written by a separate direct `UPDATE` branch in the same function. The brief was directionally right that the path was ungated, but incomplete about how the write actually happens.

# Spike 3 Report

## Answer

Yes.

A real invoice can now be entered and re-read on the generic entity page without an invoice-specific screen. What it took was:

- generic `date` and `date-time` controls in `DynamicSchemaForm`
- a generic array-of-objects grid that reuses the same field renderer as top-level fields
- a generic linked-entity picker for `x-link-entity-type`
- generic structured read formatting so arrays of objects are not shown as raw JSON
- per-key metadata patching so saves only send changed keys, with explicit `null` for cleared top-level keys

## Changed Files

- `packages/owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx` — added shared field rendering, date/date-time controls, linked-entity picker, and array-of-objects grid editing.
- `packages/owletto/src/components/create-entity-form.tsx` — passed org context into the generic schema form so linked-entity fields can query entities.
- `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx` — changed metadata saving to send only changed keys and explicit nulls for removed top-level keys.
- `packages/owletto/src/lib/json-renderer/format-value.ts` — made arrays of objects and objects render as structured readable text instead of raw JSON.
- `packages/owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.test.tsx` — added the required array-of-objects control test.
- `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/index.test.ts` — added the required changed-keys/cleared-field patch test.

## Clearing Behavior

Top-level removals are handled by diffing the current cleaned form state against the same cleaned baseline already used for dirty detection. If a key existed in the baseline but is absent from the current cleaned form state, the outgoing metadata patch includes that key with `null`. That makes clears transmit even though `cleanFormData` omits empty values.

## Contradictions / Notes

- The package's declared existing suite command, `bun run test`, is already failing broadly in this worktree because Vitest cannot resolve several workspace imports such as `@lobu/core/reserved`, `@lobu/core/errors`, and `@lobu/core/refs`. I did not fix that infrastructure problem as part of this spike.
- The generic entity detail page is primarily an editable generic form. The re-read path for this spike is the same generic form plus the existing generic renderer path, not a separate invoice-specific read-only screen.
- Because the package-wide Vitest run is already failing during module resolution, the two new required tests were verified with `bun test` directly instead of relying on `bun run test`.

## Did Not Do

- I did not add any invoice-specific component or screen, because that would fail the spike's goal.
- I did not repair the package-wide Vitest workspace import-resolution failures, because they are broader than the invoice-form spike and already affect many unrelated tests.

content.text:
Substantial progress. Here's where it stands.

**The project is live.** `~/Code/prodma-demo`, a real Lobu project scaffolded with the published CLI, running on embedded Postgres at `localhost:8790` with Claude wired in. Five entity types applied — customer, product, quote, invoice, payment — with Turkish field labels, `x-link-entity-type` foreign keys on every document reference, and line items as arrays of objects. Seeded with three customers (Anadolu Makina, Ege Plastik, Konya Tarım) and four products, and I confirmed they persisted by reading them back: ids 2-4 and 5-8.

Two things I got wrong on the way, both from guessing instead of reading: the SDK parameter is `type`, not `entity_type` (it maps internally), and `lobu memory exec` takes source, not a path. Fixed by reading `sandbox/namespaces/entities.ts` rather than trying variations.

**Spike 1 passed, and I verified it myself rather than trusting the report.** Re-ran the suite independently: 9/9. The denials are real and I can read them in the log — `invoice "Invoice posted" is frozen in state "posted" and cannot be edited`, thrown from `entity-management.ts:733` through `handleUpdate`, which is the human path. And `cannot transition status from "draft" to "posted"` for the illegal jump. A rule declared as data on the schema now stops a person, changeable at runtime.

**It caught a real bug in my own schema.** `frozen_from: "issued"` combined with `allowed.issued: ["posted"]` is self-contradictory — if everything freezes at `issued`, the invoice can never reach `posted`. The freeze has to exempt a legal status transition, otherwise documents strand one state short of terminal. That's a design error in what I published, not an implementation detail.

**And it surfaced spike 2's premise as a live fact.** In the test log: `[insert-event] change audit event DROPPED after retry — audit trail is missing this row`, on an ordinary draft edit. The trigger there is a test-harness FK, but the behaviour is exactly the one I described from reading — one retry, log, drop. I'd argued it from code; now I've watched it happen.

**Spike 3 reports yes** — date controls, an array-of-objects grid reusing the same field renderer, an entity picker, structured read rendering, and per-key metadata patching with explicit nulls for cleared fields. `tsc -b --noEmit` clean. I have **not** independently verified this one yet, and its own report flags that the package-wide vitest run was already broken on workspace import resolution before it started.

**Spike 4** settled earlier: 23ms at Prodma's scale, nothing to build.

---

Confidence **95** on spike 1 — I re-ran it and read the actual denial stack traces. **60** on spike 3 until I run it myself; a passing typecheck and two new tests are not a working line-items grid. **90** on the demo being real — I created and read back the entities through the live server.

Next, in order:
1. Verify spike 3 myself, in the browser against this running instance, entering a real twelve-line invoice.
2. Fix the freeze/transition contradiction in the schema and re-test.
3. Drive the end-to-end agent demo — ask the agent in chat to build a quote for Anadolu Makina and convert it to an invoice.
4. Spikes 2 and 5 in the writepath tree, which is now free.

content.text:
End-to-end demo works. Quote id 9 is in the database.

**What the agent did**, unassisted, from one Turkish sentence: resolved "Anadolu Makina Sanayi" to customer id 2 and both products to ids 5 and 7 by name, computed 50 × 185.50 = 9,275 and 3 × 4,750 = 14,250, subtotal 23,525, VAT at 20% = 4,705, grand total 28,230 — arithmetic correct — built the line items as an array of objects matching the schema, generated a document number, set status `draft`, and persisted it. Verified by reading it back: `id 9, draft, 28230, 2 lines`.

It also hit the **approval gate** before writing. The agent proposed the write, the runtime held it, and it only landed once approved. That's the governance layer working on a real ERP document without anything being configured for it.

**The freeze contradiction is fixed.** The state field is now exempt from the freeze so a document can still advance along a legal transition, while every other field stays immutable. 12/12 tests pass, including three I added: a frozen `issued` invoice can move to `posted`; a `posted` invoice still can't transition anywhere because its `allowed` list is empty; and bundling a field edit with a legal transition is denied, so the exemption isn't an escape hatch.

**The central design claim is now observed, not argued.** I added `x-transitions` to the live invoice type through `manage_entity_schema` on the **published** server — no deploy, no schema change — and it persisted through a full `lobu apply` without being clobbered. The unknown `x-` keyword survives the AJV round trip in production, exactly as the design assumed. There's also precedent I hadn't seen: `x-lobu-resolution` is already a typed CLI field that folds into `metadata_schema`, which is the same pattern one step further along.

**Four things went wrong and are worth knowing:**

The SDK parameter is `type`, not `entity_type` — I guessed twice before reading `sandbox/namespaces/entities.ts`, which I should have done first.

A native `sharp` binary nested under `@xenova/transformers` was broken and blocked every reboot. Moved aside so it resolves to the working top-level copy.

**The published worker's model registry is behind its own CLI.** `providers.json` advertises `claude-sonnet-5`, `gpt-5.6-sol` and friends; the worker bundle only knows `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `gpt-4.1` and `gpt-5.1-codex-max`. For OpenAI the two lists don't intersect at all. That's a real version-skew bug in the published stack.

**Every provider key is out of credit.** Anthropic: balance too low. OpenAI: no credits remaining. Gemini: monthly spend cap exceeded. OpenRouter had a little left, and I had to pick `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` specifically because the worker requests 16,384 max_tokens and that was the only model the remaining balance could afford. The demo is running on fumes — worth topping one up before showing it to anyone.

---

Confidence **93** on the demo: I created the quote through the agent and read it back from the database. **95** on the freeze fix — 12/12 with adversarial cases I wrote to try to break my own exemption. Spike 3 remains **unverified by me**.

Next:
1. Verify spike 3 in the browser against this instance — enter a twelve-line invoice by hand.
2. Spikes 2 and 5 in the now-free writepath tree.
3. Drive quote → invoice → post → try to edit, to show the freeze end-to-end in the product rather than in a test.
4. Top up a provider key if this is going in front of Prodma's owner.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user owns/has access to **Prodma**, a Turkish manufacturing ERP at `/Users/burakemre/Downloads/emre_project`, and wants to know whether it could be rebuilt on **Lobu** (their agent platform monorepo at `/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu`). This is a **gap analysis / proof of concept**, explicitly *not* a migration — "the point is to see where lobu lacks." Audience is Prodma's owner (a domain expert). Scale: <20 concurrent users. All four deliverables wanted: written gap report, working slice on Lobu, Lobu roadmap, pitch for the owner.

   Intent across this session's messages, in order:
   - **Challenge the two DB changes I'd asked approval for**, scope out row-level read authz (WP-0), explain the Prodma-owner questions, re-examine the metrics design, and **finalize the design so spikes can start**.
   - **Challenge `xmin`, challenge the `x-durable-audit` opt-in, ask what `x-link-entity-type` is for, ask what a materialized view is and whether we need one.** Relay two owner answers: chat + CRUD pages is enough (no bespoke screens), and decide YETKI (permissions) from what I already know rather than waiting for the sheets.
   - **Ask whether any new Lobu features are actually needed** ("did you need any new features now in lobu or are we set?").
   - **Execute all the spikes, offloading to opencode CLI as a subagent.**
   - **Reject scope creep on scaling** ("why are you thinking about 1m invoices?").
   - **Demand an actual local project + end-to-end demo with a model plugged in** — this was the sharpest correction: I had been doing platform surgery without ever standing the product up.
   - **"yes go ahead fix those"** — proceed with my stated next steps (verify spike 3, fix the freeze contradiction, run the agent demo, then spikes 2/5).

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Prodma:** .NET Framework 4.6.1, WinForms + DevExpress, SQL Server, EF EDMX + raw ADO.NET + typed DataSets. 503 DbSets, 441 screens, 637k live LOC. Field visibility is client-side `.Visible = false` (per-screen/per-field, NOT row filtering).
   - **Lobu:** Bun workspace; `entities` table with `metadata jsonb`; `entity_types` with `metadata_schema` (JSON Schema Draft-7), `event_kinds`, `backing_sql`, `backing_source`, `metrics_config`; `entity_relationships`; AJV validation with `strict:false`; Behaviors; connectors; sandbox ClientSDK; MCP; Owletto frontend submodule.
   - **The mutation-gate interceptor pipeline** — allow / deny / defer; `registerMutationInterceptor` + `BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS`; per-field `requireApproval` unions on update; reserved `$name`/`$parent_id`/`$content` paths.
   - **`field_controls`** — per-row, per-**top-level** metadata key human ownership; `FieldControl = { note?, set_by?, set_at? }`.
   - **`x-` extension keywords in `metadata_schema`** — the central design vehicle. `x-link-entity-type` (shipped precedent), `x-lobu-resolution` (typed CLI field folded into metadata_schema), and the new `x-transitions`.
   - **Derived entity types** — `backing_sql` makes a type a live SQL view with no stored rows.
   - **Turkish ERP domain:** Cari, Stok, Fatura, İrsaliye, Sipariş, Teklif, Çek/Senet, KDV, Tevkifat, e-Fatura/GİB, YETKI (permissions), PLASIYER (salesperson).
   - **opencode CLI as subagent** — sandboxes file access to cwd, auto-rejects outside paths, **still exits 0**.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts`** — the extension point. Header states a new gate is ONE new file appended to `BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS` with zero core edits; import-cycle note requires hoisted `function` declarations and a STATIC import.
     - `:120-125` — **the critical discovery**: `UpdateMutationRequest` carries only field names + owners, NO values:
       ```ts
       action: "update";
       entityTypeSlug: string;
       entityId: number;
       entityOrgId?: string | null;
       /** field path (incl. reserved $-attributes) -> current owner. */
       fields: Record<string, FieldOwner>;
       ```
     - `:186` `registerMutationInterceptor` — idempotent by name.

   - **`packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts`** — `updateEntity` at `:554`.
     - `:588` `const isHumanEdit = !!ctx.userId && !ctx.agentId;`
     - `:616` `const result = await sql.begin(async (tx) => {` then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` — **the locked read is INSIDE the tx**
     - `:654` `if (!isHumanEdit) {` wraps the entire gate call
     - `:684-694` ownership computed per **top-level** metadata key via `Object.keys(metadataUpdates)`
     - `:696` `runMutationGate({ action: "update", ..., sql: tx, fields: fieldOwners })`
     - `:728` `computeFieldMerge({ metadata: existing, controls: existingControls, fields: metadataUpdates, source: isHumanEdit ? "human" : "watcher", ... })` — **proves the read-modify-write is serialized and field-grained**
     - `:776` `updated_at = current_timestamp` (= transaction start, can go backwards)
     - `:424`, `:519`, `:942` — the only three `getEntityHooks` call sites

   - **`packages/server/src/utils/entity-hooks.ts:27-36`** — **GAP 1**, the entire hook interface:
     ```ts
     interface EntityLifecycleHooks {
       beforeCreate?: (data: EntityData, ctx: EntityHookContext) => Promise<EntityData>;
       afterCreate?: (entity: CreatedEntity, ctx: EntityHookContext) => Promise<void>;
       beforeDelete?: (entity: {...}, ctx: EntityHookContext) => Promise<void>;
     }
     ```
     No `beforeUpdate`/`afterUpdate`. Only `$member` registered.

   - **`packages/server/src/authz/transition-interceptor.ts`** (NEW, 169→178 lines, written by opencode, **fixed by me**). My fix:
     ```ts
     if (typeof currentState === "string" && frozenStates.has(currentState)) {
       // The state field itself is exempt from the freeze: a frozen document may
       // still advance along a LEGAL transition, checked below. Without this, a
       // `frozen_from` at a non-terminal state strands the document one step
       // short of terminal forever — an invoice frozen at `issued` could never
       // reach `posted`. Every other field is immutable from here; a state move
       // that is not in `allowed[current]` is still denied by the transition
       // check, so a terminal state (empty `allowed`) remains fully sealed.
       const changed = Object.keys(req.fields).some(
         (field) =>
           field !== spec.field &&
           valueChanged(req.currentValues[field], req.proposedValues[field]),
       );
       if (changed) {
         return { outcome: "deny", reason: `${label} is frozen in state \"${currentState}\" and cannot be edited.` };
       }
     }
     ```

   - **`packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/tools/entity-transition-freeze.test.ts`** — 9 tests from opencode + **3 added by me**:
     ```ts
     it("allows a frozen invoice to advance along a legal transition", ...)   // seedInvoice "issued" → status "posted" succeeds
     it("still seals a terminal state against its own state field", ...)      // posted → draft rejects /cannot transition status from "posted" to "draft"/
     it("denies a field edit that rides along with a legal transition", ...)  // {status:"posted", notes:"smuggled"} rejects /frozen in state "issued"/
     ```
     **12/12 pass.**

   - **`packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx:105`** — the real concurrency bug: `metadata: metadataDirty ? metadata : undefined` (whole-object dirty flag).

   - **`packages/owletto/src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx:300`** — `if (prop.type === "array" && prop.items?.type === "string")` is the ONLY array branch. `cleanFormData` exported at ~:129.

input.content:
---
name: reference_entity_update_validates_the_patch_not_the_merge
description: manage_entity update validates args.metadata ALONE against the type schema, so any entity type with `required` metadata fields cannot take a partial update — callers are forced to resend the whole object
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`handleUpdate` in `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts` (~line 432 on
`origin/main`, confirmed 2026-08-14) calls `validateEntityMetadata(entity_type,
args.metadata, ctx)` — **the patch alone**, not the patch merged over the stored
row. It has `before.metadata` in hand two statements earlier and does not use it.

Consequence: on any entity type declaring `required` metadata fields, a partial
update fails with `Metadata validation failed: missing required field: <x>` for
every required key the caller did not resend. Observed live: an `invoice` type
with `required: ["customer_id","date","status"]` rejected
`update({entity_id, metadata:{notes:"..."}})` even though `customer_id` was
present in the stored row.

This is the ROOT CAUSE behind the Owletto client bug in
[[reference_write_gate_is_the_only_non_agent_authorable_layer]]:
`entity-tabs/index.tsx:105` sends `metadata: metadataDirty ? metadata : undefined`
— the whole object on any change. The client is not being lazy; the server makes a
true PATCH impossible. Fixing the client alone would break every required-field
type.

**How to apply:** validate the MERGE (`{...before.metadata, ...args.metadata}`),
which is also what the write path actually stores (`computeFieldMerge` replaces
top-level keys). Fixed this way in the `prodma-writepath` worktree; not yet on
`origin/main`. Any per-field write feature — approval gates, transitions, field
ownership — is untestable through the SDK until this lands.

content.text:
The dev server is up and everything is wired. **http://127.0.0.1:9455** — it auto-signs you in (single-user mode), org `local-install`.

I built one combined rig instead of two: the `prodma-writepath` worktree runs the server, and I copied spike 3's form work into its Owletto submodule. So a single UI has both the transition interceptor and the array-of-objects line editor. Provider is OpenRouter on `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` — I checked balances live first: Anthropic still returns "credit balance too low", and OpenRouter shows `total_credits: 0`, so luna is running on free-tier allowance. It does tool calls fine, but it's the only thing standing.

What's loaded: 3 customers, 4 products, one posted invoice, and quote #10 which the agent wrote itself — `lobu chat` in Turkish, and it resolved the customer and both products by name, computed 40 × 185.50 + 2 × 4750 = 16,920, VAT 3,384, total 20,304, and stopped at the approval gate. I've since deleted the 1-hour standing grant it created, so the gate will fire again when you test chat in the UI.

**The document lifecycle now enforces itself end to end**, from a rule stored as data in `metadata_schema`:

```
draft: edit notes                    ALLOWED
draft -> posted (skip)               DENIED  cannot transition status from "draft" to "posted"
draft -> issued                      ALLOWED
issued: edit grand_total             DENIED  frozen in state "issued" and cannot be edited
issued -> posted                     ALLOWED
posted: edit notes                   DENIED  frozen in state "posted"
posted -> draft                      DENIED  cannot transition status from "posted" to "draft"
```

Final state: `posted`, total still 8250 — the 999999 tamper never landed.

**Getting there turned up a real bug in shipped code.** Every one of those seven steps first failed with `missing required field: customer_id`, on a row that has `customer_id: 4`. `handleUpdate` in `manage_entity.ts` validates `args.metadata` — the patch by itself — against the full type schema including `required`. It has the stored row in hand two statements earlier and doesn't merge it. Confirmed on `origin/main`, not just my branch. The effect is that **no entity type with required metadata fields can take a partial update at all**, through the SDK, MCP, or the tools.

That's also the root cause of the Owletto concurrency bug I'd blamed on the client. `entity-tabs/index.tsx:105` sends the whole metadata object on any change — I read that as laziness, but the server makes a true PATCH impossible. Fixing the client alone would have broken every required-field type. I changed the validation to run on `{...before.metadata, ...args.metadata}`, which is what the write path actually stores.

One correction: I reported the UI 404ing earlier. That was my probe — curl sends `Accept: */*`, and the SPA fallback requires `text/html` or a session cookie. With a browser Accept header it's 200. The server was fine.

```
packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts      |  14 +-   (new: merge-before-validate)
packages/server/src/authz/transition-interceptor.ts   | 178 ++    (new file)
packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts        | 170 +-
packages/server/src/tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts | 86 +-
packages/server/src/utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts   |  21 +
packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts     |   6 +
+ entity-transition-freeze.test.ts (12 tests, passing)
owletto: dynamic-schema-form.tsx +724, entity-tabs +50, create-entity-form +15, format-value +27
```

---

Confidence **95** on the freeze and the lifecycle — driven through the real `manage_entity` path against a running server, with the denials quoted above. **90** on the partial-update fix: proven on the live path and on `origin/main` by inspection, but I haven't run the server suite since changing it. **60** on spike 3 — the form tests pass (3 of them, which is thin) and the page serves, but I still haven't typed a twelve-line invoice into it, which is the part I'd want you to do.

Next:
1. You drive the UI — create an invoice with several lines, then post it and try to edit, and see whether the denial surfaces readably or as a raw error string.
2. Run the server suite against the `manage_entity` change before it goes anywhere near a PR.
3. Spikes 2 and 5 (durable in-tx audit, update hook) — the writepath tree is free and already booted.
4. Top up a provider key; luna is the last one standing.
only 10 entities? also you can use my chatgptsubscription to test, what are the gaps and what did you fix and build

content.text:
Seeded properly — **241 entities** now, and I wired up the ChatGPT path.

| type | count |
|---|---|
| invoice | 86 |
| quote | 56 |
| product | 43 |
| payment | 29 |
| customer | 26 |

Invoice book is ~37M TRY: 46 posted, 21 issued, 10 draft, 9 cancelled. The 67 posted-and-issued ones are frozen by the live rule right now, so the freeze is testable on real rows rather than one fixture.

**ChatGPT subscription: Lobu supports this natively.** `lobu providers catalog` lists a `chatgpt` kind — *"Sign in with ChatGPT Plus/Pro (device code). Uses your subscription, not metered API billing."* Server-side device-code OAuth is implemented (`gateway/auth/oauth/client.ts:246`). I can't complete it for you — it's a sign-in approval against your account, and there's no CLI subcommand for it, only the web flow. Go to **http://127.0.0.1:9455/local-install/agents/prodma-demo/models** and add a ChatGPT provider there; it'll hand you a device code. Once that's the default, luna's dead free-tier balance stops mattering.

---

## The gaps

**1. There is no update hook — the biggest one.** `entity-hooks.ts` exposes exactly `beforeCreate`, `afterCreate`, `beforeDelete`. Nothing on update. A rule can *refuse* a write but can never *cause* one. For an ERP that means posting an invoice cannot emit the journal entry, and dispatching an irsaliye cannot move stock. Every accounting system is built on exactly that reflex. **Not fixed** — needs design, not a patch.

**2. No numbering primitive.** Nothing allocates a gapless per-type, per-year sequence server-side. Turkish invoice law requires it. Prodma partly escapes because Innova assigns the e-invoice number, but internal `document_no` has no allocator — my seed made them up.

**3. Update validates the patch, not the merge — fixed.** `manage_entity.ts` validated `args.metadata` alone against the full schema including `required`, with the stored row sitting in a variable two lines above. Any entity type with required fields could not accept a partial update at all. Confirmed on `origin/main`. This also root-caused the Owletto bug I'd blamed on the client: `entity-tabs/index.tsx` resends the whole metadata object because the server left it no choice.

**4. The mutation gate couldn't see values — fixed.** `UpdateMutationRequest` carried field *names* and owners, no before/after values. A freeze was expressible; a transition check was not. Threaded `currentValues`/`proposedValues` through all three construction sites.

**5. The generic form had no array-of-objects control — fixed.** `dynamic-schema-form.tsx` handled `array` only when `items.type === "string"`. Invoice lines — the central object in the entire domain — could not be typed into the UI. +724 lines.

**6. Audit events get dropped.** Observed live in the test log, not argued: `change audit event DROPPED after retry — audit trail is missing this row`, on an `events_created_by_fkey` violation. The before-snapshot is taken outside the lock and the insert isn't in the caller's transaction. **Not fixed** (that was spike 2).

**7. The worker's model registry lags its own CLI.** `providers.json` advertises models the published worker bundle rejects; for OpenAI the two lists don't intersect at all.

**8. Row-level read scope doesn't exist.** Relationship types carry no SQL predicate, and there are four separate read paths (tools, REST, search, SDK) — a gate on one leaks while looking like protection. Scoped out on the owner's answer that per-field hiding is enough.

## What I built

`transition-interceptor.ts` — a declarative document lifecycle read from an `x-transitions` key inside `metadata_schema`. **Zero new tables, zero new columns, zero deploy.** I added the rule to a running published server through the normal schema API and it survived a full `lobu apply`. That was the central bet of the design and it's now observed rather than assumed. Twelve tests, including three adversarial ones I wrote to try to break my own freeze exemption.

Plus the demo itself: `~/Code/prodma-demo`, five entity types with Turkish labels, 241 entities, and a live rig where the agent authored a quote from a Turkish sentence and stopped at the approval gate.

## What I proposed and then killed

Worth stating, because it's most of the value: **the design needs no schema changes at all.** I asked you to approve two DB changes and both collapsed. `xmin` row versioning was wrong — concurrency is already field-grained, so a row token would produce false conflicts on a system that doesn't have the bug I thought it had. An `x-durable-audit` per-type flag was wrong — `recordChangeEvent` already fires on every update, so it changed nothing but made some types' history quietly untrustworthy. Write-time rollups contradicted your own settled metric design.

---

Confidence **90** overall. High on the gaps I demonstrated with running code; the update-hook and numbering gaps are structural reads of the source, not things I tried to build and failed at.

Next:
1. Sign in with ChatGPT at the models page — then the agent runs on your subscription.
2. Click through the invoice list and open a posted one; try to edit it.
3. Refresh the gap-report artifact — it predates every spike result and the new bug.
4. Spike 5 (the update hook) is the one gap that actually decides whether an ERP can live on Lobu.

=== arch.md ===
## PORT VERDICT

- **Data-access patterns (EF per-call contexts + raw SQL side-channels):** MECHANICAL — the three generations are readable and map cleanly onto one repository layer; the ~270 inline writes and 32 `SqlCommand` files are enumerable, but every call site must be re-expressed against a typed model.
- **Service/Cntrl/Vm CRUD tier:** TRIVIAL to MECHANICAL — 706 VMs + 419 Services + 362 Cntrls follow one template (`AService`/`BaseCtrl`); they are the single most automatable part of the port (grid metadata in `M_ALANLAR` even supplies field lists).
- **Report/query engine (ListeYapBase/ListService, ~46k lines + CariGrupBilgileriAl*):** HARD — hundreds of report methods encode business definitions of balances/aging/margin directly in LINQ with no spec; each must be re-derived against a live DB to verify numbers match.
- **Voucher posting logic (StokFisHelper/MuhasebeFisHelper/FisOrtakService + Fis forms):** HARD — correctness-critical, fused to DevExpress grid events, and written as sequential non-atomic commits with sector- and client-specific branches (`Gemi`/`DEGA`); it must be re-derived, not extracted.
- **Transaction/concurrency behavior:** HARD — Prodma has *none* (no transactions, no locking, no concurrency detection, single-client globals); re-implementing it correctly (true atomic posting, stale-write detection, per-user state) is additive work a port must design from scratch, not translate.
- **e-invoice / e-archive / e-irsaliye transmission (GIB integrations):** STATUTORY-BLOCKED — direct GIB/Payflex web-service client code (eFaturaYazService.cs, eArsivYazService.cs, eIrsaliyeGonderService.cs) must be re-certified against current Turkish Revenue Administration schemas and envelopes; this is legal integration, not application logic.

=== cari.md ===
## PORT VERDICT
