**The SDK contract exists and connectors honour it.** `packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-normalize.ts` exports `normalizePhone` / `normalizeEmail` / `normalizeEmailDomain` / `normalizeAuthUserId` / `normalizeIdentifier` over an identity-namespace registry, and documents the design decision explicitly: "Connectors should pass in values that already represent a specific E.164 number. The normalizer's job is cleanup (spaces, dashes, parens, `+`), **not country-code guessing**." WhatsApp obeyed — it wrote `905395102240` into `entity_identities` with a namespace and `source_connector`. **Do not propose a workspace-default-region / country-code inference feature; the contract deliberately rejects it and the importer is where the region knowledge actually lives.**

**The bad data never met a connector.** The 07-06 address-book import was `run_sdk`: 26 `run_sdk completed` audit events spanning 21:44:00→21:45:36 bracket 541 person entities created 21:45:10→21:45:16 with metadata keys `aliases, email, first_name, last_name, phone`. Only 3 of 541 got an `entity_identities` row. No entity-creating run row exists (the only runs in that window are `chrome` browser actions), no `connector_key` on any related event, `created_by` is a user id. Same shape for the LinkedIn batches (18:59 / 19:02 / 21:19, keys `company, email, first_name, last_name, linkedin_url`) and the Instagram/X batch on 07-08.

**Scale of the split** — live persons in `buremba`, `deleted_at is null and merged_into is null`:

```
persons  meta_phone  meta_email  ident_phone  ident_email
   4358         534         535           18           69
```

1069 identifiers in `metadata` against 87 identity claims. ~92% of the workspace's resolvable identity carries no namespace, no provenance, no normalization, and no uniqueness — and was not matchable at all until #2152 taught the matcher to read metadata defensively. `packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts` has **zero** `entity_identities` references, so `createEntity` cannot resolve identity even in principle.

**Consequence.** `053-559-51101` (Turkish local) and `905355951101@s.whatsapp.net` are the same number in two formats on two entities. Deterministic rules can't join them, so they surface as a human approval — paying human attention for a plumbing bug. Under the SDK contract the honest outcome is that a non-E.164 value never becomes an identity claim at all: it stays a display string until the source data is fixed.

**Fix direction (not built):** `run_sdk`/`createEntity` accept identity claims and run them through `normalizeIdentifier`, so collisions happen at write time. "Fozkan" would then have hit the April WhatsApp shell as it was created — no proposal, no queue, no fingerprint to go stale. Backfilling the 534 metadata-only phones is downstream of that and only worth doing once the writer stops producing more.

**It is a MISSING CAPABILITY, not a bypass (verified 2026-07-29 against the working tree).** `packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts` has no identity parameter on create or update at all — its only `identit*` hits are merge/unmerge prose and `merge_evidence.identity_ids`, which is provenance for a merge, not a write. `manage_entity.ts` imports only `loadLiveEntityIdentities` (read). So an agent can create a person and has literally no way to say "this phone is an identity claim" — metadata is the only slot that exists. Per [[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]] the fix is to add the capability, not to infer identities from metadata after the fact.

**There is no chokepoint to add it to.** Seven independent `INSERT INTO entity_identities` sites: `tools/save_content.ts:326`, `auth/subject-identities.ts:60` and `:107`, `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512`, `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424`, `utils/canvas-events.ts:161`, `utils/member-entity.ts:136`. Any identity contract has to land as a shared writer these seven adopt, or it will be an eighth dialect.

**The storage question comes first.** Prod `entity_identities` is 11 columns: `id, organization_id, entity_id, namespace, identifier, source_connector, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, merged_from_entity_id, connection_id`. `ConnectorFact` carries `assurance`, `providerStableId`, `sourceAccountId`, `validTo` and `normalizedValue` — **all five are discarded at the write boundary**. Two open decisions before any code: (1) which of those become columns; (2) `identifier` uniqueness is on normalized *spelling*, not canonical value, so `05355951101` and `905355951101` both satisfy `idx_entity_identities_live_unique` — a correct identity write still would not collide. Also note `providerStableId`/`sourceAccountId` are required on `ConnectorFact`, which is exactly what makes the contract unusable for a non-connector writer and guarantees the bypass.

**Measured cost of the storage gap, 2026-07-30.** Of the 16 merge approvals still pending in `buremba`, exactly **4** (runs 702088, 702091, 702092, 702094) yield **zero** evidence and therefore cannot be healed in one click — in every case the winner holds a national-format `metadata.phone` (`05067888845`) against a loser identity row `905067888845`. The other 12 match on exact digits and heal on one Confirm. That 4/16 is the concrete price of decision (2) above: **it is the missing canonical-value column, not a missing normalizer.** Adding country-code inference to `normalizeScalar` would "fix" all four and is the wrong fix — the contract rejects guessing, and the region knowledge lives in the importer. A canonical-value column populated at write time by the importer that knows the region is the fix that does not require guessing later.

## Diagnosis of `entity_identities` itself (2026-07-30) — the table is sound, its uniqueness rule serves the wrong half

**Deleting it is not an option: it is the authz substrate.** `packages/server/src/authz/member-claim-predicate.ts` calls itself "the single source of truth for does this (org, user) resolve to a live `$member`" and answers it through one `entity_identities` row with `namespace='auth_user_id'`. `channel-visibility.ts`, `channel-messages-visibility.ts`, `resource-visibility.ts`, `access-graph.ts`, `channel-entity.ts`, `channel-about.ts` and `auth/subject-identities.ts` all join it. Any "should we just drop it?" question is really about the phone/email rows only.

**Prod splits into two populations wanting opposite rules** (live rows, all orgs): opaque provider IDs — `linkedin_slug` 2626, `github_user_id` 1116, `github_login` 1093, `x_user_id` 736, `x_handle` 557, `ig_username` 499, `wa_jid` 357, `watcher_key` 165, `auth_user_id` 45, `slack_user_id` 25, `domain` 19, `slack_channel_id` 11 — where spelling **is** the identity and exact match is correct (~7,200 rows, working fine); versus human-entered contact identifiers `phone` 357 + `email` 105 (462 rows), where spelling is an accident of the typist. Only the second group is broken.

**`uniquePerOrg` is declared and never read.** `packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-namespaces.ts` defines `uniquePerOrg: boolean` ("true means a value should identify at most one entity per org") and sets it false on `email_domain` with a note that many people share a domain. Verified on `origin/main`: the identifier's ONLY occurrences are its own declarations — no consumer. Meanwhile the DB enforces one blanket `UNIQUE (organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` over every namespace. Declared semantics and enforced semantics are disconnected; the knob that would fix this already exists and is inert.

**CORRECTION (same day, before building): the paragraph below OVERSTATES the silent-skip bug — I read `insertIdentities` without reading its caller.** `lookupMatches` (`utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:332`) resolves every incoming `(namespace, identifier)` to its owning entity *before* any insert, so in the common same-spelling case the connector path finds the existing owner and attaches to it: no duplicate created, no evidence lost. The ON CONFLICT skip is deliberate and documented at line 785 ("an identifier that ON CONFLICT-skipped because another entity already owns it stays with that entity, so the map must not mis-claim it"). What survives as real is narrow: (a) the `catch` → `return []` swallows genuine DB errors into a success shape, a fail-closed violation; (b) the contested drop has no log in the one-sided case, even though line 772 already warns for the *ambiguous* case. Neither justifies a redesign. **Lesson: read the caller before calling a guarded skip a silent bug** — [[feedback_gateway_predicate_cannot_replace_worker_state]] is the same shape of mistake.

**Also DROPPED: my "assurance-gated uniqueness" design was solving a problem the policy declines to have.** `entity-resolution/policy.ts:19` defines `ResolutionDecision = "auto_merge" | "review"`, and every rule in `DEFAULT_PERSON_RESOLUTION_RULES` is **`review`** — email and phone both. So no uniqueness mechanism (canonical column, assurance column, threshold index) would have prevented the 18 approvals: the shipped policy asks for review on contact-identifier matches on purpose, because a shared phone is not proof. The 18 were the system working as designed; the only bug was the fingerprint. `onMatch` in `x-lobu-resolution` is already the knob if auto-merge is ever wanted — configuration, not a migration. Do not re-propose assurance-gated uniqueness without first re-reading those default rules.

**The perverse part (OVERSTATED — see correction above): the unique index destroys the evidence of sameness in BOTH directions.** `insertIdentities` (`utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512`) does `ON CONFLICT (organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL DO UPDATE … WHERE entity_identities.entity_id = EXCLUDED.entity_id`, so a claim already held by a *different* entity is **silently skipped** — no exception, omitted from `RETURNING`, and the sole caller uses the result only to seed `metadata.aliases`, so the dropped identifier does not even become an alias. Two answers, and one thing I have to correct about the PR.

## First: #2765 was overtaken, so I closed it instead of merging

`pi-review` passed (0 bugs, 0 blockers, simplicity 98) — but it flagged something I hadn't checked: **`origin/main` already pins `958e5481`.** PR **#2758** merged while I was working and carried the same pointer move. Verified directly:

```
git diff origin/main HEAD -- packages/owletto   →  (empty)
```

So merging would have had zero net effect. I closed it as superseded rather than land a no-op commit on main. The UI proof stands on its own at owletto#842.

**The queue is unblocked, just not by me.** #2718 now passes `check-drift`. #2764 and #2762 still fail it — their branches are stale, so they need a **rebase**, not another pointer PR.

## Connectors generating edges — yes, but nothing was built

The capability already existed. What happened was a **correction, not a feature**: I reported it as an open gap, you pushed back with "didn't we do 2 already?", and you were right. Three paths exist:

- **Reaction client** — `entities.create/update/delete/link/unlink/updateLink`, with `EntityLinkInput` as `{from_entity_id, to_entity_id, relationship_type_slug, metadata?}`. Full imperative relationship CRUD.
- **Declarative** `identities` + `createWhen` in the connector manifest — the server materializes entities and links from emitted events.
- **`attributions` on `eventKinds`** — `authored_by` / `about` / `mentions` / `belongs_to`.

Only the **sync** path is events-only (`SyncResult` genuinely has no entities field). My original error was generalizing that one true fact to connectors as a whole, plus grepping for invented symbol names. The memory is fixed.

**What's still a real gap: bulk relational import.** The reaction client is per-call, not a loader — so pulling an ERP's relational graph in bulk has no good path. That part of the original conclusion survives.

## Edge-authority model — I can't find it, and I'm not going to invent it

I searched the memory directory, the 10 gap-audit scope reports, and this session's history. There's no "edge-authority" anywhere. So it either predates what I can see, or it's a name for something recorded differently.

The closest real thing is the **ACL/authz work** (`project_authz_acl_finalized`): PG-native, "reuse entity graph, one two-sided SQL gate", with `access-graph.ts` deciding authority by traversing entity edges. That is an edge-shaped authority model, and Slack channel visibility shipped as vertical 1 via #1586. If that's what you meant, it's real, partly shipped, and the next step was GitHub repo membership as source #2 before extracting a generic engine.

But I'd rather you confirm than have me build on a guess. What did the edge-authority model cover — relationship provenance (which source owns an edge), or the authz graph?

**Next actions:**
- Rebase #2764 and #2762 onto current main to clear their stale `check-drift`.
- PR `erp-asof-reads` and `ui-review-deploy-only` — both clean, nothing blocking them now.
- Open the owletto PR for the line-item grid.
- Tell me which thing edge-authority was, and I'll fold it into the board.
you say bulk upload but if connectors was able to generate edges we wouldn't need the bulk
You're pressing on the right seam. Let me verify rather than agree — I've been wrong on this in both directions already.

You're right that it's the same question, and my "bulk import" framing was sloppy. But when I actually traced it, the capability splits in a way that matters — and the split is exactly why the gap survives.

**There are two different edges, and connectors can only bulk-produce one of them.**

*Event → entity attribution.* Declared in the manifest as `attributions` on `eventKinds`, with roles `authored_by` / `about` / `mentions` / `belongs_to`. This is fully declarative and rides the sync path, so it *is* bulk. Its own doc comment defines the scope: "event attribution answers what resolved entity should this particular event be connected to."

*Entity → entity relationship.* A separate table, `entity_relationships`, with `entity_relationship_types` and `entity_relationship_type_rules` beside it. Nothing in the connector manifest materializes these. The writers are `manage_entity.ts` (the imperative tool behind the reaction client's `entities.link`), `auto-linker.ts` (NER-lite name matching that creates `mentions`, capped at 20 links per event), and three purpose-built graph materializers — `github-team-graph`, `channel-about`, `access-graph`. I also confirmed `entity-link-upsert.ts` never touches `entity_relationships` — it writes identities only.

**For Prodma the edges you need are all the second kind**: invoice→customer, line→product, movement→warehouse. Those are foreign keys between domain entities. A connector's only route to them is the reaction client, one call per edge, each its own commit.

So the honest statement of the gap isn't "bulk import is missing" — it's **there is no declarative way for a connector to say "this event's `CariID` field means invoice→customer"**. Attribution rules can point an event at an entity; nothing turns a foreign key into an entity-to-entity edge. That's a manifest surface that doesn't exist, not a throughput problem.

**One detail that suggests this was intended and never built:** `relationship-validation.ts` defines the valid relationship sources as `['ui', 'llm', 'feed', 'api']`. There's a **`feed`** source already in the enum — the schema anticipates feed-produced relationships. There's just no way to declare one.

And this lands on the same missing piece as everything else: an entity→entity edge per SDK call is its own transaction, so an invoice header plus 20 lines plus their edges can't be written atomically. That's the write funnel again, from a different direction.

I'll correct the memory — the note currently says "bulk ERP/relational import has no good path, the reaction client is per-call," which is true but reads like a volume problem and had me proposing a loader. The real ask is a declarative FK→relationship rule in the connector manifest.

**Confidence: high (88)** — traced the manifest types, the table writers, and confirmed `entity-link-upsert` writes no relationships. The one thing I haven't checked is whether `x-lobu-resolution` or the entity-schema surface offers a relationship rule I haven't found; my grep covered `entity_relationship_type_rules`, which is validation only.

Want me to write up the declarative-edge rule as a proper proposal? It's a smaller, sharper piece of work than the funnel, and it's the thing that actually unblocks modelling Prodma's 422 tables.

Lobu · design proposal · revision 3 
 Edge Authority Model 
 The entity graph is already the intended substrate for authorization — locked in June, largely unbuilt. This revision survived an adversarial pass against twelve concrete use cases and fixes the four it failed. 
 Revision history — read this first 
 Rev 1 proposed a claims table and reserved-type tiers, designed without reference to the locked architecture. Rev 2 withdrew both. Rev 3 restores claim semantics — as a column, not a table — after rev 2 failed use cases 5, 6, 10, 11 and 12 under adversarial review. 
 The lesson worth keeping: rev 2 was wrong because dropping the claims table and dropping claim state are different decisions, and it conflated them. 
 Answering the question directly 
 Does this replace $resource and the ACL? 
 No, and it must not. The locked architecture already says the entity graph is the universal substrate. Principals are entities . Memberships are member_of edges. ACLs are can_read / deny_read edges. One SQL gate reads all of it. 
 The ambition of "use links for every use case, up to row and column level" is not a new direction — it is the direction already chosen. The work is to finish it, not to design it again. 
 Locked decision #1, verbatim: 
 Store: PG-native, reuse the entity graph. Memberships = entity_relationships ; ACLs = compiled flat principal sets; one SQL gate. No external ReBAC engine. No new principal/edge/identity tables. 
 Built vs. designed 
 Piece Status Where 
 member_of memberships built authz/access-graph.ts 
 Slack / GitHub ACL sync built authz/slack-acl-sync.ts, github-acl-sync.ts 
 Resource read gate built authz/resource-visibility.ts 
 $resource registry built authz/access-graph.ts 
 can_read / deny_read not built Zero occurrences in packages/ on origin/main 
 Boolean ACL expression compiler not built Designed in §3 
 Freshness / aclSupport state not built Designed in §5 
 Connector acl / principal / membership records not built Designed in §8 
 Connector knowledge edges not designed The actual gap 
 The one constraint that limits "links for everything" 
 This is the most important thing to understand before extending the graph to row and column level, and the locked doc is emphatic about it: 
 From the locked design — §3 
 Boolean ACL expressions (Jira browse AND issue-security ) compile to effective-read principals — NEVER naive can_read edges to both groups (that is OR → a leak). 
 Edges are inherently OR. Two can_read edges mean "either audience may read." Real permission rules frequently need AND — "in the finance group and assigned to this region." Expressing that as two edges silently widens access to anyone in either set. 
 The design's answer is not to make traversal smarter. It is to compile the expression down to an effective principal — a synthetic intersection principal or a concrete member set — before it ever becomes an edge. And if a source cannot be compiled safely, it is aclSupport: none ⇒ owner-only. Fail closed. 
 This is what makes "one graph for everything" safe, and it is also what bounds it: 
 Use case Fits the edge model? Why 
 Resource-level read (channel, repo, document) 
 yes — built 
 Membership is already an effective set; no expression to compile 
 Row-level (this invoice, this customer) 
 yes 
 A row is just a finer-grained resource; the same gate applies once rows are entities with can_read edges 
 Intersectional rules (A and B) 
 only via compiler 
 Naive edges are OR and leak. Needs the expression compiler, which is unbuilt 
 Column-level (hide invoice.total ) 
 breaks outright 
 A row edge gates the whole event. The connector RFC (§Gaps) already lists field-level security as beyond the resource gate 
 Correction — masking after the gate is too late 
 Revisions 1–2 proposed treating column-level as a projection mask applied once the gate resolves. That is unsafe. By then the value has already entered search text, embeddings, prompt construction, summaries, exports, caches and logs. A mask would have to run before every content-consuming seam. 
 The simpler and safer representation: store the sensitive field as a separate finance-only facet event and omit it from the base invoice event, so both point at the same invoice entity but only the facet carries the restricted ACL. If arbitrary field masking is a hard product requirement, it is an admitted separate subsystem — not something ordinary edges cover. 
 Stress test: twelve use cases 
 Revision 2 was run against twelve concrete scenarios. It failed five. Those failures are what revision 3 fixes. 
 # Use case Rev 2 What it needed 
 1 ERP: invoice belongs_to order, 5-hop chain partial Breaks on reassignment — superseding the event does not retract the edge. Needs assertion keys 
 2 Slack membership → read, fast revocation partial Locked design holds; the code does not — see defect below 
 3 Jira browse AND issue-security holds Via the locked expression compiler 
 4 Row-level: rep sees their region's customers holds One can_read edge per row per audience; domain belongs_to must not itself confer access 
 5 Column-level: only finance sees total_amount fails Facet events, not masking 
 6 Agent creates a link via $links fails Protection must sit in the store, not in connector validation 
 7 auto-linker 0.4-confidence mentions holds After store migration; must never enter authz closure 
 8 Summary over three events inherits ACLs holds Locked §6 provenance table — notably not an edge 
 9 Cross-org public-catalog reference holds Existing scope rule; security edges stay same-org 
 10 Entity merge collapsing two edge sets fails Merge discards a producer whose triple collides; needs assertion-aware repoint 
 11 Two connectors assert the same edge fails One live row per triple cannot record two owners 
 12 Feedless Okta/SCIM directory sync fails No-feed connectors throw if polled; needs its own lifecycle, not afterPersist 
 Spike results — measured, not argued 
 Four questions were settled by running things rather than reasoning. Two changed the design; one changed its priority. 
 Question Result Consequence 
 Does dropping the live-triple unique index break reads? 
 no 
 The ACL gate is EXISTS (SELECT 1 …) , indifferent to how many rows back an edge. 0 of 23 read sites do single-row-per-triple lookups. Duplicate assertions are read-safe 
 Does it break writes? 
 three statements 
 access-graph , channel-about and github-team-graph all use ON CONFLICT (from, to, type) , which Postgres will reject without that index. All three are already in scope for migration, so the blast radius is contained — but it is not free 
 Can the graph actually answer ERP questions? 
 yes — 18 ms 
 A 3-hop customer → quote → invoice → payment traversal over ~1,000 edges and ~320 entities returns in 18 ms. Performance is not the constraint at this scale 
 Can agents express graph traversal? 
 no 
 The agent SQL tool rejects WITH RECURSIVE outright. Plain selects, non-recursive CTEs and N-way self-joins all pass. Agents get bounded, hand-written traversal only — a product gap independent of this design 
 Escalation path — traced end to end in code, not executed 
 The $links action has no approval branch and no mutation gate . entity-mutation-gate.ts guards only update and contains no reference to link ; the approval branches in manage_entity.ts (lines 346, 597, 781, 1397) all sit outside the link handler at 1463–1571. 
 Combined with the earlier findings — validateTypeRule permits any pair when no rules are seeded, and the ACL read trusts any live member_of edge — an agent holding manage_entity in an ACL-synced org can assert an access-granting edge. Prerequisites: the org runs ACL sync (so member_of exists), and a $resource entity is targetable. Mitigation: access-graph 's reconcile sweeps the edge on next sync, making the window time-bounded rather than permanent. 
 I traced this, I did not execute it. It should get a proper security review rather than being taken as proven — but it is specific enough to act on, and it is the reason the protected-type check moved to the top of the sequence. 
 Two defects found while testing 
 The locked plan is wrong about Slack revocation 
 §5 cites member_left_channel as an "already-subscribed" event backing high-priority membership invalidation. It is not subscribed: SLACK_BOT_EVENTS contains member_joined_channel and zero occurrences of member_left_channel . Bounded revocation SLA is locked decision #2, so the mechanism it depends on does not exist yet. 
 A third class of mutator 
 entity-management.ts:1027 issues a hard DELETE FROM entity_relationships — not a soft delete. Any consolidation that inventories only the insert paths will miss it, and any assertion model must decide what a hard delete means for other producers' claims. 
 Separately, buildAccessGraph is treated as atomic by its callers but takes no transaction, opens its own client, writes edges incrementally, and marks freshness afterward ( access-graph.ts:280,378 ). Freshness should be set only after the whole reconcile commits. 
 Settled approach 
 After twelve use cases, two adversarial passes and four spikes, this is the position I would defend. It is unchanged in shape from revision 3; the spikes moved one item's priority and confirmed the rest. 
 Sequence 
 1 · Gate $links . Smallest diff, highest urgency — the spike showed no gate exists. Protected relationship types enforced in the write path, behind an internal capability only audited compilers hold. 
 2 · The claim-aware relationship store. Every mutator migrated — the six inserters plus merge repointing, tool unlink, and the hard DELETE at entity-management.ts:1027 . Rewrite the three ON CONFLICT upserts the index change invalidates. 
 3 · assertion_key column + index move. Verified read-safe. Fixes channel-about , ACL over-deletion, merge, and multi-connector assertion in one change. Amends a locked decision — needs explicit sign-off. 
 4 · Connector domain-edge rules in afterPersist , plus a separate feedless directory lane for principal|membership|identity . 
 5 · The locked authz program as its own track, starting with the Slack revocation gap it wrongly assumes is closed. 
 Deliberately out of scope 
 A separate claims table — only if the live-triple index proves immovable. 
 Field masking as a post-gate projection — replaced by facet events. 
 Recursive traversal for agents — a real gap the spike exposed, but a query-surface problem, not an edge-model one. 
 What the spikes did not cover 
 The demo holds invoices, quotes, payments, products and customers, but zero order , stock-movement and journal-entry rows — so the full five-hop chain was never traversed end to end. The 18 ms figure is a measured three-hop result, not an extrapolation to five. Row-level can_read cardinality was estimated, not measured. 
 The gap that is actually open 
 The locked SDK shape (§8) already covers the authorization half of connector emission: 
 // Locked design, §8 — connectors emit a typed record union: 
event | acl | principal | membership | identity
 // plus: declare provides[] and aclSupport 
 // "Per-connector ACL compiler = the trusted security boundary" 
 What no design covers is domain knowledge edges : invoice belongs_to order, order fulfils quote, product in price list. These carry no authorization meaning, they are the substance of an imported business system, and there is no way to express them at all — the word "relationship" does not appear in the connector SDK. 
 That is one narrow addition, and it needs exactly one safety rule rather than a tier system: 
 interface EntityRelationshipRule {
 key: string; // stable, for retraction

---
name: project_edge_authority_model
description: "Edge Authority Model rev 3 — one relationship write path for entity_relationships; survived 12 use cases + 4 spikes; the 5-step sequence, the OR-leak constraint, and the connector domain-edge gap it already identified"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T03:00:00.000Z
---

Designed 2026-08-14, revision 3. **This was NOT in memory and I failed to find it when
asked — that is why it is here now.** Artifact:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e9a8f908-bcae-4f22-b4e0-ba5be33cb417

**The problem.** `entity_relationships` is one graph table with **six independent
writers**, two trust levels, and no enforced boundary. It is also the locked authz
substrate (June): principals are entities, memberships are `member_of` edges, ACLs are
`can_read`/`deny_read` edges, one SQL gate reads all of it. So "links for everything, up
to row and column level" is the direction ALREADY CHOSEN — the work is to finish it.

**Built vs designed:** built = `member_of`, Slack/GitHub ACL sync, resource read gate,
`$resource` registry. NOT built = `can_read`/`deny_read` (zero occurrences on
origin/main), boolean ACL expression compiler, freshness/`aclSupport` state, connector
`acl`/`principal`/`membership` records.

**The constraint that bounds "links for everything": edges are inherently OR.** Two
`can_read` edges mean "either audience may read". Real rules need AND, and expressing AND
as two edges silently WIDENS access. The answer is not smarter traversal — compile the
expression to an effective principal BEFORE it becomes an edge; if a source cannot be
compiled safely it is `aclSupport: none` => owner-only, fail closed.
- Resource-level read: YES, built. Row-level: YES (a row is a finer resource).
- Intersectional (A AND B): only via the unbuilt compiler.
- **Column-level: BREAKS OUTRIGHT.** Post-gate masking is UNSAFE — by then the value is
  already in search text, embeddings, prompts, summaries, exports, caches, logs. Use
  **facet events** (sensitive field as a separate finance-only event pointing at the same
  entity), not masking.

**Spikes (measured, not argued):** dropping the live-triple unique index is READ-safe
(gate is `EXISTS`, 0 of 23 read sites do single-row-per-triple lookups) but breaks THREE
`ON CONFLICT (from,to,type)` writers (`access-graph`, `channel-about`,
`github-team-graph`). 3-hop customer->quote->invoice->payment over ~1000 edges = **18 ms**
(performance is not the constraint). **The agent SQL tool rejects `WITH RECURSIVE`** —
agents get bounded hand-written traversal only; separate product gap.

**Escalation path traced (not executed):** `$links` has NO approval branch and NO mutation
gate — `entity-mutation-gate.ts` guards only update and never mentions `link`; the approval
branches in `manage_entity.ts` (346, 597, 781, 1397) all sit OUTSIDE the link handler
(1463-1571). With `validateTypeRule` permitting any pair when no rules are seeded, an agent
holding `manage_entity` in an ACL-synced org can assert an access-granting edge. Wants a
real security review.

**Two defects found:** the locked plan cites `member_left_channel` for fast revocation but
`SLACK_BOT_EVENTS` does NOT subscribe it (bounded-revocation SLA depends on a mechanism
that does not exist). And `entity-management.ts:1027` issues a **hard `DELETE FROM
entity_relationships`** — a third mutator class any consolidation will miss.
`buildAccessGraph` is treated as atomic but takes no transaction (`access-graph.ts:280,378`).

**Settled sequence:**
1. **Gate `$links`** — smallest diff, highest urgency, no gate exists today.
2. Claim-aware relationship store; migrate all six inserters + merge repointing + tool
   unlink + the hard DELETE; rewrite the three `ON CONFLICT` upserts.
3. `assertion_key` column + index move (read-safe; fixes channel-about, ACL
   over-deletion, merge, multi-connector assertion). **Amends a locked decision — needs
   explicit sign-off.**
4. Connector domain-edge rules in `afterPersist` + a feedless directory lane for
   `principal|membership|identity`.
5. The locked authz program as its own track, starting with the Slack revocation gap.

**IT ALREADY IDENTIFIED THE CONNECTOR EDGE GAP.** "The gap that is actually open" =
**domain knowledge edges** (invoice belongs_to order, order fulfils quote, product in price
list) — no authorization meaning, the substance of an imported business system, and *"the
word relationship does not appear in the connector SDK"*. Proposed
`interface EntityRelationshipRule { key: string; ... }` with ONE safety rule, not a tier
system. **I re-derived this same gap from scratch on 2026-08-15 — do not derive it a third
time; it is step 4 above.**

Out of scope deliberately: a separate claims table (only if the live-triple index proves
immovable); field masking as post-gate projection (replaced by facet events); recursive
traversal for agents (real gap, but query-surface not edge-model).

Not covered by the spikes: the demo had zero `order`/stock-movement/journal-entry rows, so
the full 5-hop chain was never traversed; row-level `can_read` cardinality was estimated,
not measured.

Related: [[project_authz_acl_finalized]] · [[project_erp_gap_branches_status]] ·
[[project_entity_write_hook_design]] · [[reference_connectors_cannot_emit_entities]]

content.text:
Both good questions. Taking them in order.

## asOf: not ducttape, and here's the specific evidence

The strongest signal isn't the implementation — it's that **the contract already existed on main before any of this work**:

```ts
// packages/connector-sdk/src/metrics.ts:27 — already on origin/main
export type MetricReadMode = 'current' | 'raw' | { asOf: string };
```

The branch touches five server files and adds zero lines to `connector-sdk`. So `asOf` was a **declared-but-unimplemented** part of the public metric contract, and this fills it. That's the opposite of a bolt-on — nobody invented an ERP hook, someone finished a promise the SDK was already making.

Three more things that make it general rather than special-cased:

- **It's one range predicate on `occurred_at`, ANDed into a filter that already exists**, placed first because it's the most selective. No new table, no new column, no new query path. That's why it measured *cheaper* than the `current` read it derives from.
- **It refuses what it can't do correctly.** `asOf` is valid-time ("what do we now know the state to have been on 31 March"). System-time ("what did we *believe* on 31 March") would need to walk the supersede chain per row — reconstructing history on a read path, which the invariant forbids — so it raises `MetricNotImplementedError` instead of approximating. Ducttape approximates; this declines.
- **It validates at apply time, not first query.**

Use it anywhere you have an append-only event store: MRR as of quarter end, headcount as of 1 Jan, open tickets as of last Friday. ERP is just the loudest consumer.

**Where it genuinely stops**, and you should know this before treating it as done: it's **metrics-only**. You can ask "what was revenue as of 31 March" but not "show me the customer list as of 31 March" — no as-of entity reads, no as-of search. And the valid-time choice means an auditor's question — "what did the books say *when we closed*" — is a system-time question this deliberately doesn't answer. Both are real ERP needs. So: a general capability with a bounded surface, not complete, but not tape either.

## `$links` vs a connector edge API — that's a false alternative

Two things worth separating:

**Connectors already have an imperative edge API.** The reaction client exposes `entities.link` / `unlink` / `updateLink` today. So the question isn't whether connectors *can* create edges — they can. It's that each call is its own commit, so a relational import is N round trips and N transactions.

**`$links` is a different actor on the same table.** It's the agent-facing action. Its problem isn't its existence — it's that it's **ungated**: `entity-mutation-gate.ts` guards only `update` and never mentions `link`, and every approval branch in `manage_entity.ts` sits outside the link handler. That's the escalation path the Edge Authority Model traced.

So "replace `$links` with a connector API" would leave the agent surface ungated *and* add a seventh writer to a table that already has six with no shared boundary. That makes the actual problem worse.

The model's answer, and I think it's right:

1. **Gate `$links`** — smallest diff, highest urgency, closes a live escalation path.
2. **Claim-aware store** — one write path all mutators go through, including the hard `DELETE FROM entity_relationships` at `entity-management.ts:1027` that any insert-only inventory would miss.
3. `assertion_key` so two connectors can assert the same edge without one clobbering the other.
4. **Then** connector domain-edge rules in `afterPersist` — declarative, bulk, materialized server-side.

Note that step 4 is the thing you're asking for, and it's *declarative*, not another imperative API. That's the distinction that matters: a rule in the manifest ("this event's `CariID` means invoice→customer") rides the sync path and materializes in bulk through the same store. An imperative API is another dialect.

The ordering also isn't arbitrary — steps 1 and 4 both write to a table that step 2 is what makes safe for multiple writers. Doing 4 before 2 gets you bulk edges with no claim model, which is how you end up with one connector silently deleting another's assertions.

## Meanwhile

`erp-asof-reads` gate is at 16/18 lanes, no failures. #2764 passes `check-drift` after the rebase; #2762's checks are still running.

One flag on step 3: it **amends a locked architecture decision** (the live-triple unique index), so it needs your explicit sign-off rather than being something I just do.

System-time ("what did we *believe* on 31 March") would require walking the supersede chain per row — reconstructing history on a read path — so it raises `MetricNotImplementedError` rather than approximating it.
- Date-only input is inclusive of the whole UTC day: `2026-03-31` lowers to `occurred_at < '2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z'::timestamptz`.

boundary, an explicit instant, the superseded-row mask, the system-time refusal, and

## Notes

**On the "request paths never aggregate history" invariant.** `asOf` adds exactly one
range predicate to the events filter the `current` read already builds, placed first
because it is the most selective available. No new aggregation, join, or per-row
function, and no new scan — it strictly *reduces* the rows `current` was already

STATUS: designed, NOT approved.

- `channel-about` correctness
- ACL over-deletion
- entity merge collapsing two edge sets (rev 2 failed this use case)

  owners, so today one silently clobbers the other

  `EXISTS (SELECT 1 …)`, indifferent to how many rows back an edge, and 0 of 23 read

- It is NOT write-safe as-is: three `ON CONFLICT (from,to,type)` statements
  (`access-graph`, `channel-about`, `github-team-graph`) will be rejected by Postgres
  without that index. Rewrite them as part of task 03.

A separate claims table — only if the live-triple index proves immovable. Rev 1 proposed

# 05 · Connector domain-edge rules — the declarative FK→edge surface

STATUS: designed (Edge Authority Model step 4), not started.
DEPENDS ON: tasks 03 and 04. Doing this first gets you bulk edges with no claim model,
which is exactly how one connector silently deletes another's assertions.

## The gap, stated precisely
Two different edges exist, and connectors can only bulk-produce one:
- **event → entity attribution**: declarative via `attributions` on `eventKinds`
  (`authored_by|about|mentions|belongs_to`), rides the sync path, IS bulk. Its own doc
  comment scopes it: "what resolved entity should this particular event be connected to".
- **entity → entity relationship**: table `entity_relationships`. NO manifest surface at
  all. `entity-link-upsert.ts` writes identities and NEVER relationships (verified).

Every ERP edge — invoice→customer, line→product, movement→warehouse — is the second kind.
So importing a relational graph today means one imperative reaction-client call per edge,
each its own commit. **This is not a volume problem.** It is a missing declaration.

Evidence the design anticipated it: `relationship-validation.ts` already lists `feed` as a
valid relationship source. The source enum has a slot; nothing can fill it.

## Do
A manifest rule mapping a foreign key on an emitted event to a typed entity→entity edge,
materialized server-side in `afterPersist`. Sketch from the design:

    interface EntityRelationshipRule {
      key: string;   // stable, for retraction
      ...
    }

The design is emphatic that this needs exactly ONE safety rule, not a tier system:
these edges carry NO authorization meaning and must never enter the authz closure.
Keep them structurally separable from `member_of` / `can_read` / `deny_read`.

## Also in this task
A separate feedless lane for `principal | membership | identity` records — no-feed
connectors (Okta/SCIM-style directory sync) throw if polled, so they need their own
lifecycle rather than `afterPersist`. Rev 2 failed this use case.

## Verify
The acid test is reassignment: an invoice moved to a different order must RETRACT the old
edge, not just add a new one. Superseding the event does not retract the edge — that is
what `key` is for. Test that path explicitly.
EOF

# 06 · The entity write funnel — prerequisite for entity write hooks

STATUS: not started. THE gate on the whole write-hook programme.

rules in an isolate inside the write transaction. Codex's condition for that design
being sound: **hooks stay disabled until the write funnel has no production bypasses.**
A hook without a chokepoint is worse than nothing — it gets documented as an invariant
while six code paths walk straight past it.

## The six known bypassers
1. `entity-merge.ts`
2. `entity-link-upsert.ts` (creates entities with its own INSERT; also never allocates
   a document number)
3. classifier extraction
4. member-entity maintenance
5. approval application
6. canvas/eval system entities and ACL-resource refreshes

Verify this list yourself before trusting it:
`git fetch -q origin && git grep -n "INSERT INTO entities" origin/main -- 'packages/*/src'`

## Known trap — do NOT repeat this
A previous `make review-fix` "fixed" `entity-merge.ts` by adding `runMutationGate` to it.
**That change regressed every agent auto-merge** and was reverted. The reason is in
memory `reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules`: the gate folds approval
policy and data rules together, and `WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete`
is `"approval"`, so routing merge through the gate turns every merge into an approval.

`runMutationGate`'s transaction context is INCONSISTENT (memory
`reference_entity_gate_transaction_context_is_inconsistent`): create/delete pass a POOL

# 07 · Separate approval policy from data invariants in the mutation gate

STATUS: not started.
DEPENDS ON: nothing strictly, but do it with or before task 06.

## The problem
`runMutationGate` folds two unrelated questions into one answer: "does a human need to
approve this?" and "is this write legal?". Because
`WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete` is `"approval"`
(`write-action-manifest.ts:64`), any operation routed through the gate as a delete
inherits an approval requirement. That is why gating entity-merge regressed every agent
auto-merge.

Consequence today: you cannot add a data invariant to an operation without also
changing its approval behaviour. That blocks the whole hook design, which needs to
express "this write is illegal" independently of "a human should look at this".

## Do
Split the two. A data invariant refuses unconditionally; an approval requirement queues.
Keep the existing approval behaviour byte-identical for every operation that has one —
this is a refactor, not a policy change.

## Verify
The regression test that matters: an agent auto-merge must still auto-merge. Write it
FIRST, confirm it passes on origin/main, then keep it green through the refactor.
EOF

cat > 08-merge-unmerge-first-class.md <<'EOF'
# 08 · merge and unmerge as first-class write operations

STATUS: not started.
DEPENDS ON: tasks 06 and 07.

## Why

`entity-merge.ts:450` — is hidden behind update/delete. Codex was explicit: hiding
unmerge recreates exactly the hole merge has now. Both need to be operations the funnel
and the hook can see and reason about.

## Open design question you must answer
What is `candidate` for a merge? A merge has a winner and one or more losers, so the
hook's context shape (`current` + `candidate`) does not map cleanly. Settle this before
writing code — it is listed as an open risk in the write-hook design and it determines
the whole ctx contract.

## Do NOT

agent auto-merge and was reverted. There is a comment recording this at the
`applyMerge` call site (commit c27a77d9d) — read it before starting.

cat > 09-entity-write-hooks.md <<'EOF'
# 09 · Entity write hooks — project-authored rules in the write transaction

STATUS: designed, DO NOT BUILD YET.
DEPENDS ON: tasks 06, 07, 08. All three. No exceptions.

Full design: memory `project_entity_write_hook_design`.

## Shape
Project-authored hooks run in a V8 isolate INSIDE the write transaction, after row
locks (so TOCTOU disappears and no CAS scheme is needed). Core ships exactly three
things and ZERO domain vocabulary — no `lifecycle`, `periodClose` or `numbering` config
keys, which is core smuggling accounting back in:
1. the write funnel,
2. the hook (locked `current` + normalized final `candidate` + `deny` + `patch` + a
   platform-prefetched declared read set),
3. a gapless-ordinal allocation capability the hook REQUESTS.

## Codex rejected two things — do not rebuild on them
1. **No in-process tenant code in the gateway.** The gateway holds the transaction and
   locks; a separate, credential-free executor process runs the pure synchronous code.
   Helper crash ⇒ kill and replace it, roll back.
2. **"Bounded by construction" is FALSE.** A CPU budget does not bound wall-clock
   transaction hold time. Every phase needs its own deadline — cardinality, byte, queue,
   execution AND wall.

## Authoring — a closure will NOT work
`defineEntityType` is intentionally a plain-data producer, and a closure cannot be
serialized (`Function#toString` drops imports and lexical bindings). Use a file
reference:

    defineEntityWriteHook({
      key: "ledger-write-rules",
      targets: [{ entityTypes: [invoice, payment], operations: ["create","update","delete","merge","unmerge"] }],
      reads: { period: entityByUniqueKey({ entityType: accountingPeriod, lock: "share", maxRows: 1 }) },
      handler: writeHookFromFile("./hooks/ledger-write.ts"),
    })

The read-set DSL exposes only indexed, statically bounded platform ops — never arbitrary
SQL — each with max rows, max bytes, lookup keys and lock mode.

## Non-negotiables
- Fail closed on everything: deny, throw, timeout, invalid output, oversized patch,
  undeclared read, patch conflict, OOM, helper crash.
- NO general `skipHooks` flag. Connector writes to project-defined types run project hooks.
- The TS-interface + lint chokepoint is an ENGINEERING boundary, not a security one — the

gapless-ordinal capability.

## Why it cannot be a sequence
`nextval()` is deliberately non-transactional and burns numbers on rollback.
Gaplessness requires allocating inside the CALLER's transaction, which forces
serialization from allocation to COMMIT. That is the whole design constraint —
gapless and unique are different problems.

  a pool client, so allocating there commits early and is NOT rolled back. Proven by
  mutation test: swapping `tx` for the pool client reddens exactly ONE case — the
  rollback one. The concurrency test stays green, because contiguity alone cannot see a gap.
- KNOWN UNFIXED in the old branch: allocation happens at create, but should happen on
  the `draft → issued` transition. Numbering a draft that is later deleted leaves an
  apparent legal gap. Fix this in the salvage.
- `entity-link-upsert.ts` creates entities with its own INSERT and never allocates.

## Verify
The rollback case is the one that matters. A test that only proves two concurrent
allocations differ does NOT prove gaplessness.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Two distinct edge types.** *event→entity attribution*: declarative via `attributions` on `eventKinds` (`EventAttributionRole = 'authored_by'|'about'|'mentions'|'belongs_to'`), rides the sync path, IS bulk. *entity→entity relationship*: table `entity_relationships`, **no manifest surface at all**. Every ERP edge (invoice→customer) is the second kind.
- **Edge Authority Model rev 3** — one relationship write path. Edges are inherently **OR**, so AND rules must compile to an effective principal before becoming edges or they silently widen access. Column-level **breaks outright**; post-gate masking is unsafe (value already in search text, embeddings, prompts, exports, logs) → use **facet events**.
- **`MetricReadMode = 'current' | 'raw' | { asOf: string }`** already existed in `packages/connector-sdk/src/metrics.ts:27` — asOf fills a declared-but-unimplemented contract.
- **Valid-time vs system-time**: asOf is valid-time (restricts `occurred_at`); system-time would require walking the supersede chain per row — forbidden on read paths — so it raises `MetricNotImplementedError`.
- **`Date.parse` rolls over impossible dates** — `2026-02-30` → 2 March. Shape-matching a regex is not validation.
- **Attestation model**: `ATTESTATION_FILE="$(git rev-parse --git-path lobu-remote-preflight)"`, written only at the end of `scripts/run-remote-ci.sh`, keyed on `git write-tree`. No resume flag.
- **Write funnel / entity write hooks**: isolate-in-transaction, gated on the funnel having zero bypassers; executor must run out-of-process; "bounded by construction" is false.
- **`runMutationGate` transaction context is inconsistent**: pool client on create/delete (`manage_entity.ts:320` + 3 sites), write `tx` on update and Behavior promotion.

```ts
/**
 * `Date.parse` ROLLS OVER an impossible calendar date instead of failing:
 * `2026-02-30` parses happily and lands on 2 March, so a successful parse is
 * not proof the date exists. Matching {@link DATE_ONLY} is not proof either —
 * it only checks the shape. Compare the parsed UTC components back against the
 * digits that were written; a rollover changes at least one of them.
 *
 * Without this, a typo'd close date silently answers as of a different day, and
 * apply-time validation reports no error.
 *
 * @param date the `YYYY-MM-DD` head of an asOf value (already shape-checked).
 */
function isRealCalendarDate(date: string): boolean {
  const year = Number(date.slice(0, 4));
  const month = Number(date.slice(5, 7));
  const day = Number(date.slice(8, 10));
  const back = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day));
  return (
    back.getUTCFullYear() === year &&
    back.getUTCMonth() === month - 1 &&
    back.getUTCDate() === day
  );
}
```
and in `asOfBound`:
```ts
  if (DATE_ONLY.test(asOf)) {
    if (!isRealCalendarDate(asOf)) {
      throw new MetricCompileError(`eventSet "${label}": asOf "${asOf}" is not a real date`);
    }
    const start = Date.parse(`${asOf}T00:00:00Z`);
    const next = new Date(start + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
    return { op: "<", literal: next };
  }
  if (INSTANT.test(asOf) && isRealCalendarDate(asOf.slice(0, 10)) && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(asOf))) {
    return { op: "<=", literal: asOf };
  }
```
Also note the existing constraint comment: the compiled literal must be `'…'::timestamptz`, NOT `TIMESTAMPTZ '…'`, because `@polyglot-sql/sdk` in `validateAndScopeQuery` rejects the typed-literal spelling.

input.content:
## Summary

Three additions to the schema-driven entity form, all generic — no ERP or domain vocabulary enters the frontend:

- **Line-item grid.** An `array` property whose `items` is an `object` now renders as an editable table (one column per item property, add/remove row) instead of a raw JSON blob. This is the keystone gap: any document with lines — invoice lines, order lines, stock movements — was previously uneditable in the UI.
- **Linked-entity picker.** `x-link-entity-type` (optionally with `x-link-lookup-field`) renders a searchable combobox over that entity type rather than a free-text id field.
- **Date / date-time controls.** `format: "date"` and `format: "date-time"` get a calendar popover, with a time input when the format carries one.

Field rendering moved out of the `DynamicSchemaForm` body into a standalone `SchemaField` component so the grid can reuse it per cell — that refactor is most of the diff.

## Rebase note (please read)

This branch was 32 commits behind and conflicted with #828 (`fix(entities): stop a numeric schema enum from crashing the entity page`). #828's fix lived inside the inline field-rendering body that this branch replaced with `<SchemaField>`, so resolving to either side alone would have been wrong:

- taking main's side would have dropped the grid;
- taking the branch's side would have **silently reverted #828** — the numeric-enum crash fix and the `"20"`-instead-of-`20` round-trip bug.

Both parts of #828 were re-applied inside `SchemaField`. Verified by mutation: reverting the re-applied enum handling turns `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` (#828's own test, untouched on main) red, and restoring it turns it green. That test is the regression guard for this resolution.

## Test plan

- [x] `bunx vitest run` on the three affected suites: 5/5 pass
  (`dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` 2, `dynamic-schema-form.test.tsx` 1, `entity-tabs/index.test.ts` 2)
- [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `biome lint src` — repo error count goes 43 → 42; this branch introduces none
- [ ] Hosted UI proof, to be attached on the Lobu pointer-bump PR

New tests added by this branch: `dynamic-schema-form.test.tsx` (grid renders and round-trips rows) and `entity-tabs/index.test.ts`.

## Notes

The one lint error this branch would otherwise add is `noArrayIndexKey` on the grid rows. Suppressed with a rationale rather than "fixed": line-item rows are plain metadata objects with no natural id, and every edit rebuilds the row object, so keying on object identity would remount the row on each keystroke — strictly worse than the index. Cells are fully controlled from row data, so a delete still renders correct values; only transient focus can move.

Formatting was deliberately left alone. Running `biome check --write` over these files reformats them wholesale (quote style and indentation differ from what's committed on main), which would have buried the real change; the diff here is the change only.

Prodma ERP gap program · 15 August

Three calls to make

The shipping queue is clear. What's left needs you rather than me — one outward-facing merge, one question of ownership, and one amendment to a locked design.

Landed since we last spoke

  • ✓#2766 88fa2e84 — asOf point-in-time metric reads. Review caught a real bug ten green tests had missed: 2026-02-30 silently answered as of 2 March.
  • ✓#2767 e6f605b8 — deploy-only pointer moves now pass ui-review as not applicable.
  • ✓Gap audit backed up — 42 files, 10 scope reports, out of the repo to ~/Code/prodma-gap-audit-analysis. It was untracked and not even gitignored, so a git clean would have taken all of it.
  • ✓owletto#844 opened — the line-item grid, rebased across 32 commits.
Ready · needs your go

Merge owletto#844 and start the UI-proof capture?

The branch was 32 commits behind and conflicted with #828, the numeric-enum crash fix. That fix lived inside the exact block this branch replaced with a SchemaField component, so both naive resolutions were wrong: main's side drops the grid, the branch's side silently reverts a merged bug fix.

I re-applied both halves of #828 inside the new component and proved it by mutation — reverting my re-application turns #828's own test red, restoring it turns it green. tsc clean, 5/5 tests pass, and the branch adds no new lint error.

What merging costs

Merging is the outward-facing step, and ui-review can only key its proof to a merged owletto PR. After that the pointer bump needs hosted UI proof of the grid: local runtime, an entity type seeded with an array-of-object property, DOM reads and screenshots. That's the real work, and it isn't quick.

My recommendation

Go. It closes the keystone UI gap every other UI "no" in the audit hangs off, and the pointer bump doubles as the first live exercise of the deploy-only path that just merged. Say the word and I'll merge, capture the proof, and open the bump.

Waiting on you

#2764 and #2762 — yours to merge, or their sessions'?

Both were stuck on a failing check-drift; I rebased them and both now sit green and mergeable. They aren't mine:

  • #2764 — deletes the orphaned config-source about writer.
  • #2762 — resolves entity-type slugs through one canonical normalizer.
My recommendation

Leave them. I unblocked the mechanics but never read their substance, and merging a branch I haven't reviewed is exactly how a stale tree reverts merged work. If you want them gone today, tell me and I'll review them properly first rather than merge on green alone.

Blocks a whole program

Approve assertion_key on entity_relationships?

This is step 3 of the Edge Authority Model, and nothing downstream of it can start until it's settled. It adds an assertion_key column and moves the unique index off the live (from, to, type) triple. That amends a locked architecture decision and changes DB design, so by your own rules it needs you, not me.

What it buys

Four bugs that are really one bug: channel-about over-deletion, ACL over-deletion, merge repointing, and two connectors asserting the same edge. All of them trace to "one row per triple" being the wrong notion of identity — an edge has an asserter, and today there's nowhere to put one.

What the spike measured

Dropping the live-triple unique index is read-safe: the gate is an EXISTS, and none of the 23 read sites do a single-row-per-triple lookup. It does break three ON CONFLICT writers, which the same change rewrites.

My recommendation

Approve it. Routing around it means fixing the same bug four times in four places and still not having edge provenance. But it is a genuine amendment to something you locked, so I won't start it on my own read of the tradeoff.

Not asking here: whether to collapse the twelve task briefs into two program files. You pushed back on the count and I still think you're right, but the split is what makes each one a single session's work, so I'd rather you skim /tmp/lobu-tasks/00-README.md before I restructure anything.

Everything durable is written down — the program board and the Edge Authority Model are both in memory now, the second one because I couldn't find it when you asked and that shouldn't happen twice.

name: reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes
description: "Resolving a rebase conflict with `git checkout --theirs` silently reverts bug fixes main landed inside the block your branch rewrote — find main's commits on that file since the merge-base and re-apply them, then mutation-verify with THEIR test"
metadata:

---

The mirror image of [[merge-main-conflict-resolution]]. That one warns that picking
**main's** side loses feature work. This is the other direction: picking the **branch's**
side loses bug fixes main landed while the branch was stale — and it is easier to miss,
because the branch side is "your" work and looks obviously correct.

**Concrete instance (2026-08-15, owletto#844 `feat/prodma-form`).** The branch extracted all
of `DynamicSchemaForm`'s inline field rendering into a `SchemaField` component, so a ~290-line
block became one `<SchemaField/>` call. Meanwhile owletto#828 had landed a fix *inside that
block*: a numeric JSON-Schema `enum` (`vat_rate: [0,1,10,20]`) crashed the whole entity page in
`formatLabel`, plus a round-trip bug writing `"20"` instead of `20`. Git reported one conflict
where main's side was the entire old block and the branch's side was EMPTY. Both naive
resolutions were wrong — main's drops the grid, the branch's reverts #828.

**The procedure that catches it:**
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..origin/main -- <conflicted-file>` — enumerate what main
   changed in that file. This is the step that turns an invisible loss into a checklist.
2. `git show <each-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply each fix into the branch's new structure
   (not the old one — the block may no longer exist).
3. **Mutation-verify with main's OWN test**, which survives the rebase untouched precisely
   because it is a different file. Revert your re-application → the test must go RED; restore
   → GREEN. Here `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` did exactly that. If main's fix
   had no test, write one before resolving.

`git checkout --theirs -- <file>` is still the right *starting* move when the branch
restructured the file (hand-deleting a 290-line conflict region gets blocked or botched), but
it is step one of three, never the resolution itself.

**Two traps hit while doing this:**
- `biome check --stdin-file-path=X < X` did NOT reproduce a lint error the same file reports
  on disk. A clean stdin probe is not evidence. Write the candidate content to a real path in
  the same directory and lint that instead.
- `biome check --write` reformatted a whole file (quote style + indentation) because owletto's
  committed files do not match its own biome config. That buries the real change in ~70 lines
  of noise. Revert the formatting, keep only the semantic hunk; the repo already carries 42
  pre-existing lint errors, so formatting is demonstrably not gated.

12	
13	The CLI path is NOT broken — it needs **two** overrides together. Without them
14	`lobu call` builds `https://lobu.ai/api/buremba/<tool>` and returns **405**;
15	adding only `--url` trips a credential guard ("Refusing to send stored context
16	credentials"). Both, plus the token pulled out of `credentials.json`:

21	  --url https://app.lobu.ai/api/v1 --raw \

27	`--arg k:=<json>` for non-strings. `config.json` holds `contexts.prod.url =
28	https://app.lobu.ai/api/v1`; `credentials.json` holds the token separately.

31	base64. Through `run_sdk` (the MCP tool) that lands in the agent context —
32	~150k tokens per shot. Through the CLI it goes straight to a file at zero

52	Check the submodule out at the base SHA, force a server restart, capture, restore:
53

57	```

## Summary

Three regressions introduced by #844, all found by review on the Lobu pointer-bump PR (lobu-ai/lobu#2769) before the pointer landed — so none of them reached production. Each was reproduced red, then fixed.

They share a shape worth naming: the new code was correct for the case the feature was demoed with, and wrong for the neighbouring case.

**1. Edits failed validation on any type with required fields.** `buildMetadataPatch` sent only the changed keys. The server validates the patch as a document in its own right rather than the merge of patch and stored row, so a payload of `{invoice_number}` alone fails the moment the type declares anything else `required`. It now sends the whole current object, still carrying explicit `null` for cleared keys, and still returning `undefined` when nothing changed so a name-only edit sends no metadata.

**2. Integer foreign keys never got the picker.** `x-link-entity-type` was checked *after* the scalar `type` branches, so an `integer` key matched the number branch and rendered a bare spinner. In an imported relational system an integer FK is the common case, not the edge case. **`make review` blocked #2769 with three real defects — and it was right.**

I verified each independently rather than taking the verdict at face value, and confirmed all three are regressions introduced by #844, not pre-existing:

1. **Every edit on a type with required fields would fail validation.** #844 narrowed the save payload from the whole cleaned object to only changed keys. The server validates the patch as its own document, not the merge — something already in my notes — so a patch omitting an untouched required field is rejected.
2. **Integer foreign keys never got the picker.** `x-link-entity-type` was checked after the scalar `type` branches, so an integer FK rendered a bare number spinner. For an imported relational system that's the common case, not an edge case.
3. **Date-only values showed the previous day west of UTC.** `new Date("2026-08-01")` parses as UTC midnight and was formatted locally — `Jul 31, 2026` under `America/Los_Angeles`.

**My UI proof could not have caught any of them.** The fixture used a string foreign key, I captured at UTC+1, and the harness never saved. That's the honest limit of what a rendering harness proves, and it's why the 75 I gave earlier was still too generous.

I also nearly filed a false positive of my own: my first linked-entity test asserted against a plain text input and looked like a fourth defect. It was correct behavior — `LinkedEntityField` deliberately degrades when `orgContext` is absent, which my test omitted. The test was wrong, not the code.

**#2769 is not merged and should not be.** Its pointer targets `3b657a76`, which contains all three defects. Since the pointer never landed, none of this reached production.

**What I got wrong in process**

I skipped `make review-fix` on the grounds that the Lobu diff was one line. For a pointer bump the effective diff is the whole owletto range, and review-fix should have run against that. Had it, these three would have surfaced before a posted review round.

When invoked via Bash with `run_in_background: true` or in any non-tty context **without** `< /dev/null`, the process blocks in S state at 0% CPU, makes no model API calls, and produces no output — looks "still processing" but is actually hung.

*Entity write path* — the write funnel first (six known bypassers), then approval/invariant separation, then merge and unmerge as first-class ops, then the write hooks. The hooks are explicitly gated on the funnel having zero bypassers, so this order isn't negotiable.

## Summary

Bumps the Owletto pointer `958e5481` → `c34837ad`. Four commits:

- **owletto#843** `13dfa210` — "Open post" opens a fresh tab instead of hijacking the active one.
- **owletto#844** `3b657a76` — generic line-item grid, linked-entity picker, and date controls in the schema-driven entity form. A schema `array` of `object` now renders as an editable table instead of falling through to the comma-separated string-array branch.
- **owletto#845** `c34837ad` — fixes three regressions #844 introduced (below).
- **owletto#846** `2fac997d` — validates `openTab` URLs and fixes the standalone popup path.

No Lobu-side source changes — this PR is the pointer move only.

### Why the range includes its own fix

The first version of this PR pointed at `3b657a76`. `make review` blocked it with three defects, all introduced by #844 and all reproduced with probes. Because the pointer never moved, **none of them reached production**:

1. **Every edit on a type with required fields would fail validation.** #844 narrowed the save payload from the whole cleaned metadata object to only the changed keys. The server validates the patch as a document in its own right rather than the merge of patch and stored row, so a payload of `{invoice_number}` alone fails the moment the type declares anything else `required`.
2. **Integer foreign keys never got the picker.** `x-link-entity-type` was checked *after* the scalar `type` branches, so an `integer` key matched the number branch and rendered a bare spinner. In an imported relational system an integer FK is the common case, not the edge case.
3. **Date-only values displayed the previous day west of UTC.** `format: "date"` carries no timezone, but `new Date("2026-08-01")` parses as UTC midnight and the label was formatted in local time — so under `America/Los_Angeles` the control read "Jul 31, 2026".

## Test plan

- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean (full Linux CI graph on Depot; `make pre-pr` only as local fallback)
- [x] Tests run: full owletto suite on the fix branch — **172 files, 1586 tests, all passing**; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome lint src` unchanged at 42 pre-existing errors
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted on owletto#845
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval

UI proof: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5c4f3005-ec8b-4904-ac6c-24ade8900c06**

Three arms, one fixture schema, one viewport, each arm a `git checkout <sha> -- src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx` over the identical harness. Captured with an **integer** foreign key in **America/Los_Angeles** — the two conditions under which #844's regressions were visible, and precisely what the first proof failed to cover. DOM assertions ran before every screenshot, and each arm reports the timezone it actually resolved so the premise is checked rather than assumed.

| Probe | Base `958e5481` | #844 `3b657a76` | Head `c34837ad` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser timezone | America/Los_Angeles | America/Los_Angeles | America/Los_Angeles |
| Grid table present | false | true | true |
| Body rows | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| Customer control | `input[type=number]` | `input[type=number]` | `button[role=combobox]` |
| Date label for stored `2026-08-01` | none | `"Jul 31, 2026"` | `"Aug 01, 2026"` |
| Add row affordance | absent | present | present |

In the mid-range shot the values readout reads `"issued_on": "2026-08-01"` while the control above it displays **Jul 31, 2026** — the defect and the ground truth in one frame.

## Notes

Beyond the feature itself: before #844 the old form rendered an array-of-objects as `[object Object],[object Object]` **in an editable text box**. Anyone typing there would have written that literal string back over their line items. The grid replaces a data-destroying control, not merely a missing one — worth grepping for anywhere else a schema array-of-object reaches a form.

Honest limit on the proof: the harness is unauthenticated, so the company picker renders but its option list is empty. The head arm proves the control appears, not that it resolves `4021` to a name. The picker's numeric write-back is covered by a mutation-tested unit test instead.

The two extension-bridge commits (#843, #846) change tab-opening behaviour rather than a rendered surface, so they are not screenshot-provable; both carry their own tests.

Verified against `origin/main` before answering: `entity-mutation-gate.ts` contains **zero** occurrences of `link`, so the gap itself is real. The Slack agent is still alive (~4 min in, no output yet).

Now your actual question — I think your instinct is right, and I'd change the plan.

**What's weak about gating `$links`.** The brief's approach is a list: protected types (`member_of`, `can_read`, `deny_read`, `$resource` types) can't be asserted by agent principals. It fails closed for unknown types *today*, but it fails open along the axis that matters — the next authz-relevant relationship type someone adds is assertable until a human remembers to extend the list. It's a guard that has to be maintained in lockstep with a growing vocabulary.

**The structural alternative.** The real defect isn't that agents can *write* `member_of`. It's that the ACL read gate trusts an edge based on its **type** rather than its **asserter**. If `member_of`/`can_read` are only honored when written by an audited internal writer, an agent asserting `member_of` grants exactly nothing — and no write-path blocklist is load-bearing for security at all.

That capability is edge provenance, which is `assertion_key` — the thing you already approved. So the sharper sequencing is: build provenance, make the read gate trust-by-asserter, and the `$links` write gate drops to hygiene rather than being the security boundary.

**The honest cost.** Provenance is a bigger chunk than the brief implied, because it effectively merges steps 2 and 3: every one of the six writers has to stamp its asserter, and the read gate changes. The write gate is genuinely small and closes the path today. Against that: the live window is already time-bounded (`access-graph` reconcile sweeps a rogue edge on the next sync) and requires an agent holding `manage_entity` in an ACL-synced org — so this isn't a fire.

**My recommendation:** skip the type gate, go straight to provenance. Your own standing guidance is to prefer adding the missing capability over routing around the gap, and a maintained blocklist is the routing-around version. If we do want something in the write path meanwhile, it should sit at the relationship-write chokepoint so the provenance work extends it instead of replacing it — not in the `manage_entity` handler.

I've not re-dispatched anything on `$links` — worth settling this first, and the failed codex run means nothing was built on the old plan. Which way do you want it?

---
name: reference_pointer_bump_review_must_cover_the_owletto_range
description: "For an owletto pointer bump the effective diff is the whole submodule RANGE, not the one-line SHA — skip make review-fix and a posted review round gets spent on real defects; plus the three regression CLASSES #844 shipped and why green tests and a UI proof both missed them"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**The process error (2026-08-15, lobu#2769).** I skipped `make review-fix` because the lobu-side
diff was ONE line — a submodule SHA. But `make review` looks THROUGH the pointer into the owletto
range and found three real defects, each reproduced with probes. So for a pointer bump the
effective diff is the submodule range; run `review-fix` against that, or a posted review round
(review + CI cycle) gets spent on findings that could have been caught for free.

**The three defects, as CLASSES — all introduced by owletto#844, fixed in #845:**

1. **A narrowed write payload met a validator that reads the payload alone.** `buildMetadataPatch`
   sent only CHANGED keys; the server validates the patch as its own document rather than the
   merge, so any edit on a type declaring `required` failed. Ties to
   [[reference_entity_update_validates_the_patch_not_the_merge]] — I had this memory and still
   shipped the collision. Fix: send the whole current object, explicit `null` for cleared keys,
   `undefined` when nothing changed.
2. **Dispatch order — a marker check placed after the type checks.** `x-link-entity-type` was
   tested AFTER `prop.type === "number"|"integer"`, so an INTEGER foreign key rendered a number
   spinner and never reached the picker. In an imported relational system an integer FK is the
   COMMON case. Fix: marker branches before type branches; also convert the selection back to a
   number on write.
3. **A date-only value parsed as UTC then formatted locally.** `new Date("2026-08-01")` is UTC
   midnight; formatted local it renders 31 July anywhere west of UTC. Build date-only values from
   components (`new Date(y, m-1, d)`). Same class as the asOf `Date.parse` rollover in lobu#2766 —
   **date handling has now produced a real bug in two different layers in one session.**

**Why nothing caught them.** Ten green tests, a full CI graph, AND a hosted UI proof all passed.
The proof used a STRING foreign key and was captured at UTC+1; CI runs in UTC. Every artefact was
correct for the case the feature was demoed with. **A UI proof can only see bugs its fixture and
its environment can express** — so a proof must vary the axes the change is sensitive to (value
type, timezone, locale), not just show the happy path.

**What a good proof looks like after this:** three arms — base, the regressed mid-range commit,
head — so the proof demonstrates the FIX and not merely the feature; browser context pinned via
Playwright `timezoneId`; an integer FK in the fixture; and every arm reports the timezone it
actually resolved so the premise is asserted, not assumed. A test whose premise can silently stop
holding is decorative ([[feedback_a_wait_condition_that_cannot_report_failure_is_decorative]]).

Related: [[reference_ui_review_screenshot_capture_recipe]] ·
[[reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes]] ·
[[feedback_verify_the_surface_not_the_builder]]

**Where my argument broke**

I claimed provenance would make the write gate "not load-bearing for security." That's false. `handleUnlink` takes a `relationship_id`, checks only that it belongs to your org, and soft-deletes it — no type check at all. So an agent can **delete a `deny_read` edge**. That's a poisoning vector I didn't see.

It doesn't. And checking made the case for one weaker still.

**The two problems that supposedly need it are both solvable without one:**

The multi-assertion problem — one row per `(from, to, type)`, so you can't record that both an agent and ACL sync asserted the same edge — is fixed by `assertion_key` plus the index move. That's a **column**, and you already approved it.

The isolation problem — agents mutating authz rows — is fixed by a gate at the relationship-write chokepoint. That's Option A. No schema change at all.

**What a separate table would actually buy** is blast radius: generic code that touches `entity_relationships` without thinking about authz physically couldn't reach authz rows. That's the only real argument, and it's a judgment call about how much you trust future writers — not a requirement.

**And that argument just got weaker.** My notes claimed `entity-management.ts` issues a hard `DELETE FROM entity_relationships`, which I was about to cite as a second such path. It doesn't exist on `origin/main` — zero matches across `packages/*/src`. Either it was fixed or the spike recorded it wrong. I'm glad I grepped rather than repeated it.

What *is* confirmed is merge repointing, and it's more interesting than the table question:

```sql
UPDATE entity_relationships
SET from_entity_id = CASE WHEN from_entity_id = loserId THEN winnerId ...
WHERE organization_id = orgId AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND (from_entity_id = loserId OR to_entity_id = loserId)
```

Scoped by org, no type awareness. So merging two entities silently repoints `member_of` and `can_read` edges onto the winner — and agents can trigger merges. That's a **fourth** mutation surface, alongside `link`, `unlink`, and `update_link`. Neither the original brief nor provenance covers it, and a separate table wouldn't fix it either — merge would just need the same awareness against the new table.

**So: no new table.** Do Option A, scoped to all four surfaces — link, unlink, update_link, and merge repointing — keyed on database-resolved types. Hold `assertion_key` for when the multi-assertion problem actually bites; it's approved and available, but nothing yet forces it.

The honest summary of the last three exchanges: I argued for provenence, codex showed me `unlink` defeats it, and now checking codex's own preferred alternative shows the table isn't load-bearing either. What survives all of it is a comprehensive chokepoint gate.
