# 02 · Gate authz edges at the relationship-write chokepoint

STATUS: not started. HIGHEST URGENCY of everything on this board.
DEPENDS ON: nothing.
DECIDED 2026-08-15: comprehensive chokepoint gate. NOT edge provenance, NOT a separate table.
  Rationale and the arguments that were defeated: memory
  `project_links_gate_vs_edge_provenance_open_decision`.

## The finding (traced in code on origin/main, NOT executed — treat as needing security review)
`$links` has no approval branch and no mutation gate:
- `entity-mutation-gate.ts` guards `update` and `forceDeleteTree`, and contains NO
  reference to `link`.
- The approval branches in `manage_entity.ts` (346, 597, 781, 1397) all sit OUTSIDE the
  link handler at 1463-1571.
- `validateTypeRule` permits any pair when no rules are seeded.
- The ACL read trusts any live `member_of` edge.

Consequence: an agent holding `manage_entity` in an ACL-synced org can assert an
access-granting edge. Prerequisites: the org runs ACL sync (so `member_of` exists) and a
`$resource` entity is targetable. Mitigation today: `access-graph` reconcile sweeps the
edge on next sync, so the window is time-bounded, not permanent.

## Scope: FIVE agent-reachable surfaces, not one
A write-only guard is insufficient. Verified inventory of every `entity_relationships`
writer on origin/main (14 sites / 8 files; grep WITHOUT a `packages/*/src` pathspec — that
glob silently matches nothing in a tree-grep):

AGENT-REACHABLE — all five must be covered:
1. `manage_entity.ts:1545` INSERT — link. Ungated. The original finding.
2. `manage_entity.ts:1599` UPDATE — unlink (soft-delete). **Ungated and type-blind**: it
   checks only that `relationship_id` exists and `organization_id` matches the caller.
   An agent can therefore DELETE a `deny_read` edge. This is why provenance-on-writes was
   rejected: stamping who asserted an edge does nothing about removal.
3. `manage_entity.ts:1642` UPDATE — update_link. Same exposure; can retype an edge.
4. `entity-merge.ts:291/320/666` — merge repointing. Scoped by org and `deleted_at IS NULL`
   only, with NO relationship-type awareness, so merging two entities silently repoints
   `member_of` / `can_read` onto the winner. Reachable via `manage_entity` merge and
   `entity-field-approval.ts:288`.
5. `entity-management.ts:1029` DELETE — force-delete-tree, hard, no org filter on the
   delete itself (relies on the tree ids being org-scoped). Reachable via
   `manage_entity` delete `force_delete_tree` and `client.entities.delete`.
   ALREADY behind `entity-mutation-gate` (`forceDeleteTree`, line 114) and arguably
   correct — the entity is gone, so its edges go. Audit it, do not necessarily change it.

INTERNAL, must keep working unchanged — these are the legitimate asserters:
`access-graph.ts:417/445` (ACL sync) · `channel-about.ts:268/373/439` ·
`github-team-graph.ts:312` · `auto-linker.ts:126`.

## Do
Enforce protected relationship types at the relationship-write CHOKEPOINT, behind an
internal capability that only the four internal asserters hold. Protected = anything the
ACL gate reads (`member_of`, `can_read`, `deny_read`) plus the `$resource` registry types.

Resolve the relationship type from the DATABASE, never from a caller-supplied field.
`source` accepts `'feed' | 'api' | ...` from the caller and agent-created links store
`ctx.userId`, so neither can carry trust.

## Constraints
- Fail closed. An unknown or unseeded type must not be assertable by an agent.
- One chokepoint, not five call-site checks — grep every entry point before writing the
  guard. A guard in the `manage_entity` handler alone is the wrong altitude and will be
  bypassed by the next writer.
- Do NOT add a table. Do NOT add a column. `assertion_key` is approved but NOT needed
  here; hold it for the multi-assertion problem if that ever bites.
- Do NOT try to fix the six-writer provenance problem here. That is task 03.

## Known interaction, do not trip on it
`access-graph.ts:425` does `ON CONFLICT (from_entity_id, to_entity_id, relationship_type_id)
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL DO NOTHING`. With the live-triple unique index, an agent that
pre-plants a matching row makes the legitimate internal grant a no-op — the internal
asserter can never take ownership of that triple. Gating the agent write at the chokepoint
closes this by construction; confirm that in a test rather than assuming it.

## Verify
Write the red test first, one per agent-reachable surface:
- an agent principal asserting `member_of` is refused;
- an agent principal unlinking an existing `deny_read` edge is refused;
- an agent principal retyping an edge into `can_read` is refused;
- a merge whose loser holds a `can_read` edge does not silently repoint it;
- ACL sync, channel-about, github-team-graph and auto-linker all still write.
Each refusal must be visible in the tool result, not swallowed. Then mutation-test:
revert the guard and confirm each test goes red.

2026-08-15: ran the AGENTS.md-mandated absence check and concluded a hard
`DELETE FROM entity_relationships` did not exist on origin/main, **contradicting a correct
memory** ([[project_edge_authority_model]], which named `entity-management.ts:1027`). The memory
was right. The grep was broken:

```
git grep -c "export" origin/main -- 'packages/*/src'   # → NOTHING, exit 0
git grep -n "DELETE FROM entity_relationships" origin/main   # → entity-management.ts:1029 ✓
```

The pathspec matched zero files, so every grep carrying it returned empty regardless of pattern.
Exit code 0 and clean output look identical to a genuine absence.

**How to apply:**
- **Sanity-check any pathspec before trusting an empty result**: run the same pathspec against a
  pattern that MUST match (`git grep -c "export" <rev> -- <pathspec>`). Empty ⇒ the pathspec is
  the bug, not the code.
- Prefer **no pathspec at all** for absence checks and filter the output with `grep -v __tests__`.
  Cheaper and cannot silently under-match.
- If a pathspec is needed, list directories explicitly (`packages/server/src packages/core/src`)
  or use the glob magic prefix `':(glob)packages/*/src/**'`. A bare `packages/*/src` is
  interpreted per git's default pathspec rules and does not behave like a shell glob here.
- This is the failure mode [[feedback_absence_needs_origin_main_grep]] exists to prevent, defeated
  from the inside: the `origin/main` half was correct and the fetch was done. **A correct recipe
  with a silently-empty pathspec is still a false absence.**
- Corollary already learned elsewhere and reconfirmed: when a fresh check contradicts a stored
  memory, suspect the check first ([[feedback_a_query_result_is_not_evidence_of_the_state_you_inferred]]).

content.text:
Here's where things landed.

**The null-clear coupling was real, and worse than I thought.** Red first, in a clean worktree:

```
× preserves an explicit null clear for an optional schema field
  → Metadata validation failed: status: must be one of: backlog, active, done
× rejects an explicit null clear for a required schema field
  → promise resolved instead of rejecting
```

Two distinct bugs. Clearing an optional typed field **400s** — that's the one my owletto whole-object patch would have hit on every cleared field. And clearing a required field didn't just fail to reject, AJV's coercion turned `null` into `""` and **wrote the empty string**. Silent corruption, reachable by any `entities.update` caller today, independent of my change.

Fixed by validating a null-filtered copy and copying coercions back (AJV mutates in place, so skipping that would silently drop them). Green, and mutation-tested — reverting takes both tests red.

I probed the required-clear case rather than guessing:

```
CLEAR-ONLY-REQUIRED        => {"action":null}
CLEAR-REQUIRED-PLUS-OTHER  => REJECTED: missing required field: action
```

So clearing a required field is refused *only* if another key survives the filter. That's `schema-validation.ts:104` short-circuiting `{}` to valid. **I scoped that out** — closing it changes the shared validator's contract for every caller including create, and that's a product decision, not a cleanup. It's documented in the test as a known gap. review-fix went ahead and changed it; I did not take that hunk.

**#2769 is restored to a clean pointer bump** — `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly `packages/owletto`. review-fix had spread into 3 server files and 7 owletto files, none of which belong in a pointer bump. All saved as patches first.

**owletto#848 is open** with the three defects that were sitting in the range #2769 ships. The one that matters: `getEntityLookupValue` read `entity[lookupField]` but custom fields live in `metadata`, so `x-link-lookup-field` silently resolved nothing for exactly the fields it exists to serve. My own test passed against the broken code because my mock invented a top-level `external_id`. Also a second timezone site in the JSON renderer that owletto#845 missed — same class, different file. Both mutation-tested; 173 files / 1595 tests green.

Two judgment calls I made without asking: dropping review-fix's `schema-validation.ts` change, and dropping its whitespace-only reformat of `create-entity-form.tsx`.

Confidence:
- **Server null-clear fix: 90.** Red→green→mutation-verified against a real embedded Postgres, plus a direct probe of the stored value. Not run beyond this one suite.
- **owletto#848: 88.** Full suite green, both fixes mutation-tested, lint-clean. No hosted UI proof yet.

## What

A top-level `null` in an `entities.update` metadata patch is the contract's explicit clear sentinel, but it was handed to AJV as if it were a value. Two failure modes, both silent from the caller's side:

- **On an optional typed property the clear was rejected.** Clearing `status` on a string-enum property returned `400 Metadata validation failed: status: must be one of: backlog, active, done`, so the field could never be emptied through the API.
- **On a required property AJV's coercion turned `null` into `""` and the write went through** — a clear that should have been refused corrupted the row instead.

Validation now runs against a null-filtered copy, so a clear reads as an absent property, which is exactly what it means. Coercions are copied back because AJV mutates its input in place and the field merge below still needs the nulls.

## Why it matters now

Reachable from the entity form as soon as it sends the whole object — which it must, because the server validates the patch as a document rather than the merge of patch and stored row.

## RED

Against `origin/main`, real embedded Postgres:

```
✓ accepts promotion provenance on update under additionalProperties: false
✓ still rejects genuinely unknown metadata keys
× preserves an explicit null clear for an optional schema field
  → Metadata validation failed: status: must be one of: backlog, active, done
× rejects an explicit null clear for a required schema field
  → promise resolved "{ action: 'update', …(9) }" instead of rejecting

Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

## GREEN

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Adjacent suites:
```
entity-schema/ + notify-kind-payload:  7 files, 49 tests passed
entities/:                             5 files, 49 tests passed
```

## Mutation test

Reverting only the filtered-copy argument back to `args.metadata`:

```
Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

Restored, green again.

## Known gap, deliberately not closed here

The required-field guard only holds while the patch carries a surviving key. A patch of `{ action: null }` alone filters to `{}`, and `validateEntityMetadata` short-circuits an empty object to valid (`schema-validation.ts:104`), so that clear lands unvalidated. Probed directly:

```
CLEAR-ONLY-REQUIRED        => {"action":null}
CLEAR-REQUIRED-PLUS-OTHER  => REJECTED: missing required field: action
```

Closing it means changing the shared validator's empty-object contract, which the create path also relies on. That is a separate concern with a different blast radius, and it is documented at the assertion rather than left to be rediscovered.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

- **Optional typed property → the clear was REJECTED.** Clearing `status` on a string-enum property
  returned `400 Metadata validation failed: status: must be one of: backlog, active, done`. The
  field could not be emptied through the API at all.
- **Required property → AJV's `coerceTypes` turned `null` into `""` and the write SUCCEEDED.** A
  clear that should have been refused corrupted the row with an empty string instead.

Fix: validate a null-filtered **copy**, so a clear reads as an absent property. Then
`Object.assign(args.metadata, metadataForValidation)` — AJV mutates its input in place, and the
field merge still needs the nulls, so skipping the copy-back silently drops every coercion.

**Coupling that made this urgent:** the entity form must send the WHOLE object, not just changed
keys ([[reference_entity_update_validates_the_patch_not_the_merge]]), which means it sends
`key: null` for every cleared field. The client fix is what makes this server bug reachable — one
is not shippable without the other.

**KNOWN GAP still open.** The required-field guard only holds while the patch keeps a surviving
key. Probed directly:

```
{ action: null }               => stored as {"action": null}   (unvalidated)
{ action: null, status:'done'} => REJECTED: missing required field: action
```

Cause: `validateEntityMetadata` short-circuits an empty object to valid
(`schema-validation.ts:104`), and filtering `{action:null}` produces `{}`. Closing it means
changing the shared validator's empty-object contract, which the CREATE path also relies on —
`make review-fix` proposed exactly that change and it was deliberately NOT taken. Treat it as its
own PR with the full server suite behind it.

**How to apply:** any layer that validates a patch must decide what `null` MEANS before validating
it. Check for the same bug wherever a JSON-Schema validator sees a partial document — a sentinel
that is not filtered out is validated as data, and with `coerceTypes` on, a rejection can silently
become a write.

Related: [[project_entity_write_path_has_no_identity_contract]] · [[project_entity_write_hook_design]]

content.text:
The review gate earned its keep — it found a real blocker, and it was in the peer session's work rather than mine.

**The bug:** #851 added server-side search to the entity picker, but `Combobox` still ran cmdk's local filter on top. Item values are `name slug entity_type`, so an entity the server found by `external_id` 4021 scores 0 against `"Acme GmbH acme company"` and vanishes — defeating exactly the lookup that `x-link-lookup-field` and the server search exist to support.

I verified it rather than taking the reviewer's word: confirmed `<Command>` had no `shouldFilter`, confirmed the item value contains no metadata, then mutation-tested the fix.

**I fixed it one level up from where review pointed.** Review flagged `dynamic-schema-form.tsx`. But checking all 18 `Combobox` consumers, **two** pass `onQueryChange` — the entity picker and `behavior-sources-editor`, which drives `useReferenceSearch({ query })`. Both had the same bug. `<Command shouldFilter={!onQueryChange}>` fixes both; the other sixteen keep cmdk's matching, which for them is the only filter there is. A call-site fix would have left the second one broken for the next reviewer to find.

That's owletto#853.

restored:  173 files, 1598 tests passed, lint clean
```

And it marked `tests_adequate: false`, which was fair; there was no test covering server-search results at all.

The server validates the metadata PATCH as a standalone document, not the merge of patch and stored row. `buildMetadataPatch` omitted a cleared baseline key, so editing another field while a required field was cleared sent a schema-invalid document and the save failed validation.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **`git grep <pat> <rev> -- 'packages/*/src'` matches NOTHING** and exits 0 — a wildcard directory pathspec silently defeats the mandated absence check. Sanity-check any pathspec against a pattern that must match.
- **`make review` mechanically requires a full Depot preflight** for the current committed tree, regardless of the attestation being semantically vacuous for a pointer PR.
- **Depot CLI exits 0 on failure** (`Depot run X failed (CLI exit 0)`), and piping `make` through `tail` masks its real exit code — double false-green.
- **vitest in `packages/server` EXCLUDES** `src/gateway/**/__tests__/**` and ~10 other dirs; those run under `bun test ./<path>` (leading `./` required or bun treats it as a name filter).
- **owletto has no `tsc` lane in its PR checks** (CodeRabbit only). `vitest` + `biome lint` pass on type errors; only the lobu pin gate catches them.
- **check-drift** turns red on **every** open lobu PR when an owletto pointer bump lands; rerunning replays the stale merge ref, so the fix is rebasing.
- **AJV singleton runs with `coerceTypes`** — `null` becomes `""`/`0` for typed fields, so an unfiltered clear sentinel silently corrupts.
- **`manage_entity.list` search predicate** is `({e}.name ILIKE $N OR {e}.metadata->>'domain' ILIKE $N)`; limit is `Math.min(Math.max(filters.limit || 100, 1), 500)` — so `limit: 2000` is clamped to 500.
- **cmdk `shouldFilter`** defaults true; a server-searched Combobox must disable it or results get scored a second time against the item `value`.
- **Artifact publishing** produces a hosted HTTPS URL accepted by `ARTIFACT=<url> make ui-review`.
- **Playwright `timezoneId: "America/Los_Angeles"`** for date-only proof; the defect is invisible at or east of UTC.

	// Validate metadata against entity type's JSON schema (if being updated)
	if (args.metadata !== undefined && Object.keys(args.metadata).length > 0) {
		/*
		 * A top-level null is the update contract's explicit clear sentinel, not a
		 * value, so it must not reach the validator as one. Passing it through had
		 * two failure modes, both silent from the caller's side: on an optional
		 * typed property the clear was REJECTED ("status: must be one of ..."),
		 * and on a required property AJV's coercion turned null into "" and wrote
		 * the empty string, so a clear that should have been refused corrupted the
		 * row instead. Filtering nulls out makes a clear read as an absent
		 * property, which is exactly what it means: optional clears validate,
		 * required clears fail as a missing required property.
		 *
		 * Validating a filtered COPY rather than `args.metadata` itself is
		 * deliberate: the field merge below still needs the nulls to know which
		 * keys to clear. But AJV coerces its input in place, so every non-null
		 * coercion has to be copied back afterwards or the write silently stores
		 * the uncoerced value.
		 */
		const metadataForValidation = Object.fromEntries(
			Object.entries(args.metadata).filter(([, value]) => value !== null),
		);
		const validation = await validateEntityMetadata(
			before.entity_type as string,
			metadataForValidation,
			ctx,
		);
		if (!validation.valid) { ... throw new ToolUserError(...); }
		Object.assign(args.metadata, metadataForValidation);
	}
```

---
name: reference-deployed-prod-sha-from-image-tag
description: "How to resolve which commit is actually running on prod — the image tag's numeric suffix is the 'Build and Push Images' workflow RUN NUMBER, not a SHA"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: caf26cd6-7152-465a-818d-0afdf6a9b617
  modified: 2026-08-08T03:44:16.972Z
---

The rollout gate in AGENTS step 11 needs a `DEPLOYED_SHA`, but nothing on the
cluster carries one. The deployment image is `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:<TAG>`
with `TAG = YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-NNNNNN`, and there is **no** commit label, env var,
pod label, or annotation exposing the SHA. `/api/v1/health` returns no version
either. Anonymous GHCR manifest pulls fail (private package), so reading
`org.opencontainers.image.revision` off the image is a dead end too.

**`NNNNNN` is the `Build and Push Images` workflow RUN NUMBER.** That is the join key:

```bash
TAG=$(kubectl -n summaries-prod get deploy summaries-app-lobu-app \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
N=$(echo "$TAG" | sed 's/.*-0*\([0-9]*\)$/\1/')
DEPLOYED_SHA=$(gh run list --workflow "Build and Push Images" --limit 30 \
  --json number,headSha --jq ".[]|select(.number==$N)|.headSha")
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"   # merge commit FIRST
```

Verified 2026-08-08: tag `20260808-025311-001973` → run 1973 → `6c290b5967`,
which is #2590's squash commit.

Two traps. **The three images roll independently** — `lobu-worker` and
`lobu-embeddings` were at run 1974 while `lobu-app` was still on 1973, so gate
on the specific deployment you care about, not "the latest tag". And **the
pod's `AGE` is a better rollout clock than the tag timestamp**: the tag records
when the image was BUILT, Flux picks it up later.

Related: [[feedback_post_merge_prod_verify_wakeup]] ·
[[project_prod_flux_image_automation]] ·
[[project_behavior_output_visibility_2590]]

Three things running in parallel. Status while they work:

**#2770 — review-fix output settled.** I kept two of its three edits and discarded one:

| review-fix change | verdict |
|---|---|
| `packages/owletto` pointer `b72e39de5` → `958e5481b` | **discarded** — a stale submodule checkout, would have reverted #2769's merged pin |
| `schema-validation.ts`: drop the `isEmptyObject` short-circuit | **kept** — see below |
| `manage_entity.ts`: 15-line comment → 2 lines | kept, plus one line naming the contract |

I was wrong to scope the `schema-validation.ts` change out earlier. My reason was "every other caller depends on the empty-object contract" — there are only two callers (`manage_entity.ts:273` create, `:441` update) and **both already guard `Object.keys(...).length > 0`**, so `{}` never reaches the validator from production code. The only path that reaches it is the one this branch creates: `{action: null}` filtering down to `{}`. Zero blast radius, and it closes the gap I'd documented as known-and-unfixed. The `isEmptyObject` export stays live for `event-kind-validation.ts:230`.

Mutation-tested both halves:

```
restore `|| isEmptyObject(metadata)`   → × rejects an explicit null clear for a required schema field
disable the null filter                → × preserves an optional null clear …
                                         × rejects an explicit null clear …
restored                               → Tests 4 passed (4)
```

Wider sweep green: `entities`/`entity-schema` vitest 62 passed (6 files), `metadata-limits` bun 15 passed. Amended onto `2efb9590d`; `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly the 3 server files, no pointer.

**#2769 prod verify — not yet rolled.** Prod runs `lobu-app:20260814-155904-002133` → build run 2133 → `c3146601c` (#2763). #2769's squash `2a87dea41` built as run **2137**, successfully, but Flux hasn't picked it up. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2a87dea41 c3146601c` → **false**. A bounded 60-minute poll is watching for the tag to advance; it exits nonzero and says so if it never does.

**#2771** had the same stale `packages/owletto` checkout — synced before starting, so its gate won't fail closed on a dirty tree.

Running now: `make pre-pr-remote` on #2770, `make review-fix` on #2771, and the rollout watch.

content.text:
The review found a real bug in my change, and it was a blocker:

```
verdict: bug_free 22, simplicity 88, slop 0, bugs 1, 1 blockers, risk high
blocker: manage_entity.ts:440 filters nulls before the untrusted-metadata limit
         check, allowing oversized null-only metadata to bypass the
         10,000-node/256-KiB guard and be persisted.
```

It's correct. `exceedsValidationLimits` lives *inside* `validateEntityMetadata`, so it only ever sees what I hand it — and I was handing it the null-free copy. A patch of 10,001 null keys shrinks to `{}`, sails past the size guard, and then the merge below persists all 10,001. The reviewer reproduced it: `originalRejected=true, filteredRejected=false, 10,001 persisted candidates versus 0 validated keys`. Before my change the guard saw the whole patch, so I introduced this.

Fix at `manage_entity.ts:433` — bound the whole patch before filtering, since the guard has to see what actually gets stored:

```ts
if (args.metadata !== undefined && !isEmptyObject(args.metadata)) {
    if (exceedsValidationLimits(args.metadata)) {
        throw new ToolUserError(
            "Metadata validation failed: metadata exceeds size/nesting limits", 400);
    }
```

I also swapped both call sites (`create` at :273, `update` at :433) from `Object.keys(x).length > 0` to `isEmptyObject(x)`. That's not cosmetic: removing the validator's empty-object short-circuit removed the documented allocation-free guard on untrusted input, and `Object.keys` materializes the whole key array of an attacker-sized object before anything bounds it.

Regression test added and mutation-verified:

```
guard disabled → × rejects an oversized null-only metadata patch
                   expected /exceeds size\/nesting limits/, got 'missing required field'
guard restored → Tests 5 passed (5)
```

The mutation failing with `missing required field` is worth noting — on a schema *without* required fields the oversized patch would have persisted silently, which is why the test asserts the specific message rather than just "throws".

Broader sweep green: 12 files / 106 tests across `entities` + `entity-schema`. Amended, `pre-pr-remote` re-running on the new tree, then I'll re-run `make review` — the prior verdict was posted against a tree that no longer exists.

Still pending: `review-fix` on #2771, and #2769's prod verify (prod still on run 2133; build 2137 carries the squash but Flux hasn't rolled it).

content.text:
**#2770 is clean now:**

```
verdict: bug_free 88, simplicity 92, slop 0, bugs 0, 0 blockers, risk medium
tests_adequate: true, suggested_fixes: []
```

It then failed `ui-review`, which wanted hosted proof for owletto#857. That wasn't a real pointer change on my side — `origin/main` had moved its owletto pin to `0db1fbdf` while my branch still carried `b72e39de`, so the tool saw a pointer delta. Rebased onto current main; both pins now read `0db1fbdf` and the file list is still exactly the 3 server files. The rebase changed the tree (the submodule pointer is part of it), so the Depot attestation no longer applies and `pre-pr-remote` is re-running before I re-run review and ui-review.

**#2771 — I rejected the fixer's headline change.** It moved ACL invalidation *ahead* of `forwardWebhook`, justified as "deliveries already verified by the public router." That claim is false. `/api/v1/app-webhooks/slack` is public, carries no org context, and does no signature check; Slack's `v0` HMAC is verified inside the Chat SDK adapter, which only runs once the request is forwarded (`chat-instance-manager.ts:1480`). With its ordering, an unauthenticated POST naming any `team_id` flips that workspace's ACL to `stale`, and since the gate fails closed, that denies recall until the next periodic sync — an internet-triggerable DoS on any workspace.

I restored invalidate-after-successful-delivery and documented why, so it doesn't get "fixed" back. The fixer's underlying concern is real (a delivery failure drops that revocation signal), and I noted the proper closure — verify the signature at the coordinator before invalidating, which needs the connector's declared webhook schema plumbed into that layer. Slack does declare the full `v0` scheme in `packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:99`, but `getPrimedBundledMethod` only exposes auth methods, not the webhook schema, so that plumbing is a separate change rather than something to bolt on here.

Its test asserted `stale` for all three cases including the 401 and 503 arms — encoding the vulnerability as the contract. Rewrote it as a table: `[200→stale, 401→fresh, 503→fresh]`. 42 pass, 0 fail.

What I kept from the fixer: narrowing invalidation to `member_left_channel` only (a *join* marking the graph stale would deny access on an access-**granting** event, and `member_joined_channel` was already subscribed on main for other purposes, so nothing is orphaned), the exact preview-workspace match, the `ensureConnectionRunning` dedupe, and the `access-graph.ts` freshness fence.

One thing I still want to check on the fence before this ships: it compares `updated_at` against a `clock_timestamp()` snapshot, but `invalidateSlackConnectionAcl` stamps `current_timestamp`, which is *transaction* start, not statement time. A revocation whose transaction opened before the snapshot but committed after would slip under the fence and get overwritten as fresh — the exact race the fence exists to stop.

Verified 2026-08-15 on the rebuilt (~22h old) cluster:

```
kubectl get imageupdateautomation -A
  → error: the server doesn't have a resource type "imageupdateautomation"
kubectl get imagepolicy,imagerepository -A
  → (empty)
```

The image-automation CRDs are **not installed**. The deployment's image tag is
pinned literally in git, so a merged PR's image can exist and still never reach
prod. `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:20260814-155904-002133` stayed put while builds
2134–2137 all completed successfully.

**The deploy manifests live in the `owletto` repo, not `lobu`:**

```
kubectl get gitrepository -n flux-system
  flux-system   https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto.git   main@sha1:0db1fbdf…
  lobu-charts   https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu.git      main@sha1:d973ebe7…
kubectl get kustomization apps -n flux-system -o jsonpath='{.spec.path}'
  → ./deploy/k8s/apps/lobu/overlays/lobu-prod   (sourceRef: flux-system → owletto)
```

So `lobu`'s own `deploy/` is not what runs prod, and grepping the lobu worktree
for `lobu-app:` finds nothing. This is a third shipping path on top of
[[reference_owletto_submodule_pin_is_not_the_deploy_path]].

**Consequence for AGENTS step 11.** "Verify live after rollout" cannot be
satisfied by waiting — `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA"
"$DEPLOYED_SHA"` stays false indefinitely. Either bump the tag in owletto's
overlay or report the verify as blocked on deploy; do not let a rollout watch
run to timeout and call it a wait.

This supersedes the "Flux picks it up later" note in
[[reference_deployed_prod_sha_from_image_tag]] — that held when automation was
installed; the run-number → SHA join in that memory is still correct and still
the only way to resolve `DEPLOYED_SHA`.

Final verdict was `bug_free 88, simplicity 92, slop 0, bugs 0, 0 blockers, tests_adequate: true`, ui-review not applicable, and all 10 required contexts verified SUCCESS against the branch-protection list (not `gh pr checks`, which omits unreported contexts).

**#2769's prod verify can't be completed by waiting, and I stopped pretending otherwise.** I killed the rollout watch after finding out why nothing was moving:

```
kubectl get imageupdateautomation -A
  → error: the server doesn't have a resource type "imageupdateautomation"

```
gitrepository/flux-system → github.com/lobu-ai/owletto.git
kustomization/apps .spec.path → ./deploy/k8s/apps/lobu/overlays/lobu-prod
```

So prod ships from **owletto's** `deploy/k8s/...` overlay — a third path beyond the two I already had recorded. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2a87dea41 c3146601c` stays false until someone bumps that tag; #2769 is merged but **not deployed**. content.text:
The review caught a second real one on #2771, and it's a good catch:

```
blocker: slack-acl-sync.ts:75 only UPDATEs an existing ACL row, so a
member_left_channel arriving during the first in-flight sync is ignored and that
older snapshot can INSERT fresh, preserving the departed member's recall access.
```

A never-graphed connection has no row, so the revocation matched nothing and the in-flight sync then blessed its pre-departure snapshot. The old doc comment defended that as intentional ("no ACL state to invalidate"), which was the wrong instinct.

I did **not** take the suggested fix as written — inserting a plain stale sentinel would enroll a previously un-enforced connection and deny recall that was already flowing. Enforcement requires `acl_support='full'` **and** `freshness_state='fresh'` (`acl-state.ts:31`), and the column already permits `'none'` (`db/migrations/20260628000000_authz_source_acl_state.sql:41`). So the upsert writes `acl_support='none', freshness_state='stale'`:

```sql
INSERT INTO authz_source_acl_state
  (organization_id, connection_id, acl_support, freshness_state, updated_at)
VALUES (..., 'none', 'stale', clock_timestamp())
ON CONFLICT (organization_id, connection_id)
DO UPDATE SET freshness_state = 'stale', updated_at = clock_timestamp()
RETURNING acl_support
```

The row exists, so `markAclEnforced`'s freshness fence sees the departure and refuses to bless the older snapshot — but nothing gets enrolled into enforcement, so no new denial. An existing row keeps whatever `acl_support` it had. Return type went to `{recorded, enforced}` so the log line stops claiming an un-enforced connection was "invalidated".

Test added for the first-sync path, asserting both halves — stale *and* `acl_support` still `'none'`. Mutation-verified by reverting the upsert to an UPDATE:

```
UPDATE form → × does not let a FIRST sync bless a snapshot taken before the departure
upsert      → Tests 17 passed (17)  ·  coordinator 24 pass, 0 fail
```

Preflight is re-running, then review and merge. Both #2771 blockers so far came from the review rather than my own testing, which is worth saying plainly — my confidence in it is medium (75) until this round comes back clean.

Fair question — the honest answer has two levels, and they've drifted apart.

**Immediately**, I'm doing merge mechanics: pushing #2770 and #2771 through preflight → review → merge, and reacting to whatever the reviewer finds. That's what the last several turns have actually been.

**Originally**, the problem is the Prodma gap analysis: can a 422-table Turkish manufacturing ERP be rebuilt on Lobu, and where does Lobu fall short? Not a migration — a survey of gaps for Prodma's owner.

The two connect unevenly:

**#2770 is on that path.** It came out of the entity write path work — the ERP shape needs entity types with required fields and schemas, and clearing a field through `manage_entity.update` silently corrupted the row (AJV coerced the `null` clear sentinel to `""`). That's exactly the class of gap the analysis exists to find, and it's now fixed and merged.

**#2771 is not.** Slack channel-membership ACL revocation has nothing to do with Prodma. It was sitting in the queue from earlier work, and I picked it up because you said "finish and merge," so I read that as "drain what's open." It's also inert on merge until someone applies the hosted Slack manifest with a `SLACK_CONFIG_TOKEN` I don't have — so merging it changes nothing in production today.

The gap analysis itself hasn't moved this session. What's actually outstanding there: brief 02 (`$links` chokepoint gate) is decided but unbuilt, briefs 03–05 (relationship write path), 06–10 (entity write path), and 12 (cleanup). The findings already recorded — connectors can't emit entities, `apply` never deletes a removed type, `apply` breaks on underscore entity keys, entity hooks have no update point — are the substance of what Prodma's owner would need to see.

So: I'd finish #2771 since its gate is already running and abandoning it mid-flight wastes the two blocker fixes, then stop draining the PR queue and go back to the gap analysis — most usefully by building brief 02, since the `$links` gate is the one where five agent-reachable surfaces are currently ungated and that's a genuine "where Lobu lacks" answer rather than a paper one.

Want me to do that, or is there a different thread you're actually after?

I got the security analysis backwards, and it cost a round. Correcting the record:

**My claim was wrong.** I said nothing upstream authenticates the Slack webhook, so invalidating before `forwardWebhook` would let anyone flip a workspace's ACL. I based that on the comment in `chat-instance-manager.ts` describing the *adapter's* verification and never traced the route itself. The actual path:

```
app-webhooks.ts:1066   if (!provider.verify(rawBody, headers, appSecret)) return json(401, …)
app-webhooks.ts:1073   // 1b. Providers that own their own routing (Slack) take over here,
                       //     after the edge signing check.
```

The edge does the `v0` verify and 401s before delegating to the coordinator. So the fixer's original ordering was right, and my "fix" reintroduced the exact gap it had closed — a 503 or failed delivery silently dropping an authenticated revocation. Reverted; invalidation is back ahead of hydration and delivery, with the comment now pointing at the real verification site.

**The second finding was also right, and worse for me:** I wrote that the `acl_support='none'` sentinel "cannot deny recall that was already flowing." `acl-state.ts:44` says the opposite — any row that exists but isn't enforced is "onboarded-but-stale and must fail closed." So the sentinel *does* deny, from the first revocation until the first sync completes. That's the defensible behavior (don't serve a membership Slack has contradicted), but my comment asserted the reverse, which is exactly the kind of confidently-wrong note that outlives the code. Rewritten to state what actually happens. Also dropped the `recorded` boolean — with an upsert it was structurally always `true`.

Tests corrected to the real contract — the 401 and 503 arms now require `stale`, not `fresh`:

```
[200→stale, 401→stale, 503→stale]   24 pass, 0 fail
first-sync race + gate suite         17 pass
mutation (skip invalidation)         × invalidates a verified leave even when delivery fails
```

Preflight is re-running, then review.

Worth naming the pattern: both of my #2771 errors came from reasoning off a comment instead of tracing the call path, and the reviewer caught both. My confidence on this PR is **low-medium (60)** — the logic is now tested and mutation-verified, but I've been wrong about its security model twice, so I'd rather the next review round come back clean than assert it's right. #2770 remains **high (95)**, merged as `3922c877`.

The prod query got blocked by the permission classifier, so I can't answer the decisive empirical question myself — I'll come back to that. Here's the mechanism, which I can explain from the code.

## What the ACL gate is for

Lobu ingests Slack messages as events. Agent recall (`search_memory`) can surface any of them. Without a gate, anyone in the org could ask the agent a question and get back content from a Slack channel they were never in — including private channels. The ACL gate makes recall membership-aware: you only get events from channels you're actually a member of.

It works off a `member_of` graph — edges from a person entity to a channel resource — built by fetching `conversations.members` for every channel the connection captures, then materialized by `buildAccessGraph`.

## The three states

Per `(org, connection)` there's one row in `authz_source_acl_state`, and `acl-state.ts` projects it into exactly three states:

- **enforced** — `acl_support='full'` AND `freshness_state='fresh'` AND synced within 60 minutes. Recall is membership-gated.
- **stale** — a row exists but isn't enforcing. **Fails closed**: that connection's channels drop out of recall entirely.
- **not-graphed** — no row at all. Falls back to the older, weaker per-agent fence.

That middle state is the important one. "Stale" isn't degraded-but-working; it's *all of that connection's Slack content becomes invisible to recall* until a sync rebuilds the graph.

A cron (`authz-acl-sync`, `*/15 * * * *`) re-syncs every Slack connection. The 60-minute freshness window means that if syncing stops, connections fail closed on their own.

Only one thing: **how fast a departure takes effect.** Today, someone who leaves a private channel keeps recall access to it until the next sync — up to 15 minutes. #2771 subscribes to `member_left_channel` and marks the connection stale the moment Slack reports the departure.

The cost is the part worth weighing: because stale fails closed, **every leave event blanks that connection's entire Slack recall until the next sync catches up** — up to 15 minutes, for everyone, not just the person who left. In a busy workspace with regular channel churn, that's recurring recall degradation in exchange for closing a 15-minute revocation window.

That tradeoff is the actual decision here, and it's a product call, not a code one.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read-only drill-down: which connections are ACL-failed, and are they still live?
set -euo pipefail

NS=summaries-prod
APP_POD=$(kubectl get pods -n "$NS" -o name | grep lobu-app | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
DB_POD=$(kubectl get pods -n "$NS" -o name | grep -E 'lobu-db-prod-[0-9]+$' | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)

DBURL=$(kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$APP_POD" -- printenv DATABASE_URL)
PW=${DBURL#*://*:}
PW=${PW%%@*}
if [ ${#PW} -lt 8 ]; then
  echo "refusing to continue: password looked empty (len=${#PW})" >&2
  exit 1
fi

q() {
  kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$DB_POD" -- \
    env PGPASSWORD="REDACTED" psql -U summaries -h 127.0.0.1 -d owletto -P pager=off -c "$1"
}

# `connections.slug` is the join key: runtime connection ids are `agentconn-<slug>`,
# so strip the prefix rather than expecting an exact match.
q "
SELECT a.freshness_state,
       coalesce(c.connector_key,'(no connection row)') AS connector,
       coalesce(c.status,'-')                          AS conn_status,
       (c.deleted_at IS NOT NULL)                      AS deleted,
       count(*)                                        AS n,
       max(a.last_synced_at)::text                     AS newest_sync,
       max(a.updated_at)::text                         AS newest_update
FROM authz_source_acl_state a
LEFT JOIN connections c
       ON c.slug = regexp_replace(a.connection_id, '^agentconn-', '')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
ORDER BY 1,2;
"

echo "== the failed ones, individually =="
q "
SELECT a.connection_id,
       coalesce(c.connector_key,'?') AS connector,
       coalesce(c.status,'-')        AS conn_status,
       (c.deleted_at IS NOT NULL)    AS deleted,
       a.last_synced_at::text        AS last_ok_sync,
       a.updated_at::text            AS last_touched
FROM authz_source_acl_state a
LEFT JOIN connections c
       ON c.slug = regexp_replace(a.connection_id, '^agentconn-', '')
WHERE a.freshness_state <> 'fresh'
ORDER BY a.updated_at DESC;
"

That's by design: those three are *runtime* credentials the server uses to verify webhooks and do OAuth. `SLACK_CONFIG_TOKEN` is a different class — an app-*configuration* token from api.slack.com that lets you rewrite the app manifest. It's a developer credential, so it correctly isn't deployed to prod.

**What I got wrong:** concluding from that that I can't do it. `scripts/slack-manifest.ts:56` loads `.env` then `.env.local` itself, and both files exist here (7,235 and 111 bytes). I turned "the value isn't visible to me" into "the action is blocked," which isn't the same thing.

There's also a rotation path at line 66: if `SLACK_CONFIG_TOKEN` is absent but `SLACK_CONFIG_REFRESH_TOKEN` is present, it calls `tooling.tokens.rotate` and mints a fresh one. Slack config tokens expire in 12 hours, which is exactly why that path exists — so "we had the tokens" from an earlier session most likely means the refresh token is in `.env` and a rotation would get a working one now.

The safe way to find out is the read-only command, which touches nothing:

Now I can answer it properly — and correct something I told you an hour ago.

**The two GitHub connections predate the feature that's failing on them.**

```
market/github            created 2025-11-17   last updated 2026-07-13
lobu-team/github-app-install  created 2026-06-22   last updated 2026-07-29
both: auth_profile_id null, app_auth_profile_id null, credential_mode null, error_message null

The GitHub ACL sync engine landed **2026-06-28** (#1590). The `market` connection was created seven months before that. When the feature shipped, `runGithubAclSyncTick` began iterating *every active GitHub connection* and building an access graph for it — including connections that have never had credentials attached. Each tick tries, throws, and calls `markConnectionAclFailed`. Nothing in that path asks "can this connection actually sync?" before enrolling it.

Neither has been touched since July, so nothing broke them on Aug 12.

**Which means my "failing since Aug 12" was wrong, and I should have caught it.** That timestamp came from `max(last_synced_at)` across the whole failed *group* — it's dominated by whichever row last succeeded, which is almost certainly the Slack one. SQL `max()` ignores nulls, so two connections that never synced at all are invisible inside that aggregate. I read a group maximum as if it were a per-row fact and told you three connections had regressed three days ago. What the data actually supports is: one Slack connection that worked until Aug 12, and two GitHub connections that may never have worked. The per-row `last_ok_sync` in the drill-down script is exactly what settles it, and it's still the one thing I can't run myself.

That also lowers the urgency I put on this. If those two were never `fresh`, nobody lost recall they previously had — the content was never being served. Still wrong, still worth fixing, but not the live incident I implied.

**How it stayed invisible** is the more interesting half, and it's three independent gaps stacking:

The connection row carries `error_message: null` despite failing every fifteen minutes. The ACL row records only `freshness_state = 'failed'`, never why. The reason exists solely as a structured field on a `logger.error` call that the log formatter drops — which is why, when I went looking for it earlier, I got the message and no detail. And the user-facing symptom of fail-closed is *empty results*, which is indistinguishable from "there's nothing to find."

So a connection can be permanently unsyncable, say so every fifteen minutes for two months, and produce no signal any human would ever encounter. That's the actual defect worth fixing, more than the two connections themselves.

content.text:
Correction first, because I got this wrong in the other direction and it changes the answer.

All three failed rows carry `acl_support = 'full'`. That value is set **only** by `markAclEnforced`, which runs only after a successful graph build. So all three *did* work at some point — "may never have worked" was wrong. Combined with the connection rows last being modified `2026-07-13` and `2026-07-29`, the sequence is: they were graphed successfully while credentialed, the auth profiles came off in July, and every tick since has failed. It is a real regression, caused by a config change rather than code. Per-row timing is still unresolved — `max(last_synced_at)` remains a group aggregate, and the drill-down is still what settles it.

**The fix, in three parts:**

**1. The connections themselves — yours, and no code substitutes for it.** Re-attach an auth profile to `lobu-team/github-app-install` and `market/github`, or delete them if they're dead. Until one or the other happens they'll keep failing every fifteen minutes. I won't guess between "needs credentials" and "should be deleted."

**2. Record why it failed.** `markConnectionAclFailed` currently writes only the state:

```sql
UPDATE authz_source_acl_state SET freshness_state = 'failed', ...
```

`connections.error_message` already exists, is already written by the feed/sync path, and is already surfaced in the connections list — so this needs no schema change and no approval. The caveat worth deciding: that column is currently owned by feed sync, so ACL failures either share it (risking one overwriting the other) or get a distinguishable prefix. I'd prefix.

**3. Make it alert once, instead of failing silently forever.** The connector-health alerter and its `connections.unhealthy_alerted_at` marker already exist for exactly this shape — "fires on the transition into unhealthy via a Postgres-mediated marker." ACL failures don't participate. Wiring them in means this class of problem announces itself on day one rather than surviving two months.

There's a fourth thing I'd argue for but won't do unasked, because it's a behavior change: a connection whose credentials can't resolve at all is a *permanent config error*, not a transient sync failure, and collapsing both into `failed` is why this looked like noise. Distinguishing them makes "this will never work until a human acts" actionable.

Parts 2 and 3 are one small PR against `slack-acl-sync.ts` / `github-acl-sync.ts`, separate from #2771. Say go and I'll write it — including a test that a failed sync leaves a readable reason, which is the thing that would have surfaced this in July.

content.text:
Confirmed, and it's bad. I introduced this.

`syncStartedAt` is captured **once** at `slack-acl-sync.ts:223`, then `buildAccessGraph` is called **once per workspace** inside `for (const [teamId, channelIds] of byTeam)`. So on an enterprise Grid connection:

1. Workspace 1 builds and stamps `updated_at = clock_timestamp()`, which is now later than `syncStartedAt`
2. Workspace 2 hits my generation check, sees a newer write, and **discards itself**
3. `teamsSynced` still increments and the sync returns `ok: true`

Every workspace after the first is silently dropped from the graph, while the connection stays stamped `fresh` — so the gate enforces against a graph that's missing those workspaces' edges, and their members lose recall entirely. That is strictly worse than the 15-minute window I was closing. The existing Grid test passed because it only exercises one workspace.

The second blocker is real too: I compare against `updated_at`, which is a *completion* time. An older sync that commits late stamps a timestamp newer than a newer sync's start, so the newer, more correct snapshot gets discarded and the older data stands as fresh — the exact inversion of what the check is for.

**My recommendation: revert the concurrency work out of #2771.**

I've now had four review rounds on this PR and introduced fresh defects in two of them, each time while fixing the previous one, and my own tests went 18/18 green while I broke multi-workspace Grid. That's not a signal to patch a third time.

Concretely I'd split it:

**Now** — revert `access-graph.ts` to the simple stamp fence and ship #2771 at its original scope: immediate ACL invalidation on `member_left_channel`. That part has been stable since round 3, and the overlapping-sync race it leaves behind is *pre-existing* — I verified against `origin/main` that `markAclEnforced` stamps unconditionally there, so the branch neither creates nor widens it. `pi-review` may still flag it; if so I'll make that pre-existing argument with the evidence rather than patching under pressure.

**Separately** — the concurrency fix as its own PR with a design pass first, because it needs two things this branch can't smuggle in: one `buildAccessGraph` call per *connection* rather than per workspace, and a real snapshot-generation value instead of inferring generation from completion timestamps (which likely means a column, so it needs your sign-off anyway).

Want me to do the revert and push? It's about ten minutes to revert, re-run the gates, and get it back in front of review.

Three states: `enforced`, `stale` (row exists but not enforcing → **fails closed**), `not-graphed` (no row → legacy per-agent fence). `acl_support` CHECK allows `('none','partial','full')`, defaults `'none'`.

content.text:
Round 5's blocker was real, and I fixed it rather than arguing it away.

**The blocker:** `buildAccessGraph` stamped `authz_source_acl_state` at the end of every call, but that row is keyed by `(org, connection)` while `syncSlackConnectionAcl` calls the builder **once per workspace**. On a Slack Grid connection, finishing workspace 1 flipped the connection-wide gate to `fresh` while workspaces 2..n still held pre-revocation edges — briefly restoring recall for someone who had just left a channel. That directly defeats the branch's own guarantee.

**The fix** is narrower than the reviewer's suggested restructure, because I checked the pruning first: departure reconciliation is scoped to `to_entity_id = <resource we just synced>`, so the per-workspace loop is safe for *edges* — the stamp was the only connection-wide write. So instead of accumulating all workspaces into one build (which would also change fetch-failure semantics), I split the stamp out:

- `markAclEnforced` → exported as `markAclFresh`, documented as connection-wide
- `buildAccessGraph` gained `markFresh?: boolean` (default `true`, so GitHub's single-scope caller is untouched)
- `syncSlackConnectionAcl` passes `markFresh: false` and stamps once after the loop — reachable only when every workspace succeeded, since any failure throws to the catch that marks the connection failed

**Verification:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `slack-channel-visibility` | 18/18 (new Grid test included) |
| github-repo-visibility, github-repo-graph, slack-channel-graph, access-graph-member-resolution, search-connection-visibility, slack-byo-bot-identity | 35/35 |
| `tsc --noEmit` / `biome check` | clean |
| **Mutation test** | flipped `markFresh` back to `true` → new test fails with `expected false to be true`; restored → passes |

The new test asserts from *inside* workspace 2's membership fetch that the connection has not yet been blessed `fresh`, and separately that both workspaces really were synced — so it can't pass vacuously on a single-workspace connection.

`make pre-pr-remote` is re-running on the amended diff (no peer gate active). Once it's green I'll commit, push, and run `make review` again for round 6.

Definitive — the manifest API is a dead end for this app, in both directions:

- Keep `external_auth_providers` → `team_not_eligible: OauthProviders cannot be created on a free team`
- Remove it → `unable_to_delete_providers: Deleting external auth providers is not supported: mcp_dcr_lobu`

The app has an MCP DCR OAuth provider that a free-plan team can't re-submit and Slack won't let you drop. So **no manifest push can succeed on `A096D2P623B`**, regardless of what's in it. Nothing I did caused this; the unmodified live manifest fails to round-trip.

**This one needs you, and it's 30 seconds in the UI** — it's the only path, and it's an account-settings change on your app:

> api.slack.com/apps/A096D2P623B → **Event Subscriptions** → *Subscribe to bot events* → **Add Bot User Event** → `member_left_channel` → **Save Changes**

No reinstall needed — it's an event, not a scope, and the app already holds `channels:read`/`groups:read`. The self-install template in the repo already carries the event from the merged PR, so new installs get it automatically; only Lobu's own app needs this toggle.

Here's where the three items stand.

**1. Slack manifest — blocked on Slack's side, needs you (30 seconds).**

I stopped before applying, and it's good I did: the repo manifest is a *self-install template*, not a mirror of your live app. `apps.manifest.update` replaces the manifest wholesale, so running the script would have changed the webhook URL (breaking all event delivery), wiped the MCP server + `mcp_dcr_lobu` OAuth provider, dropped both OAuth redirect URLs, and renamed the app.

So I built the surgical version instead — export live, add only `member_left_channel`, push that back. Slack rejects it both ways:

- manifest as-is → `team_not_eligible: OauthProviders cannot be created on a free team`
- without that block → `unable_to_delete_providers: mcp_dcr_lobu`

The app's *unmodified* live manifest won't round-trip, so no manifest push can succeed on `A096D2P623B` at all. The UI is the only path:

> api.slack.com/apps/A096D2P623B → **Event Subscriptions** → *Subscribe to bot events* → `member_left_channel` → **Save Changes**

No reinstall needed (event, not scope). The repo template already carries it from the merged PR, so third-party installs get it automatically.

**2. Rollout — in flight.** Build `31896543600` for squash `b6e36adac` started at merge time and is still running; prod is on build 2144 (16:34, pre-merge). A background watch will report when the image flips and whether the squash is an ancestor of the deployed SHA.

**3. Connections — done as specified.** Deleted market/github (id 92): 5 feeds, all failing a month with `worker_claim_timeout`, 20 consecutive failures, unhealthy since 2026-07-13. Dry-ran first (one admin call, nothing else), then verified: market went 11 → 10 connections, zero GitHub connections, zero feeds. Its 651 collected events remain — `events` is append-only, so history is intact. lobu-team/github-app-install (id 385, 16 feeds) untouched.

**Confidence: 95 on the connection work** — dry-run previewed, executed, and independently re-queried after. **100 that the manifest can't be applied via API** — proven by the unmodified round-trip failing identically.

Two things you should know:

- **lobu-team/github-app-install has no auth profile attached** (`auth_profile` and `app_auth_profile` both null). That's the `AUTH_MISSING` cause. Keeping it means attaching credentials, or it keeps failing ACL sync every tick.
- **Deleting a connection orphans its ACL row** — nothing deletes from `authz_source_acl_state`, so market/github now leaves a permanent `full|failed` row. Cosmetic (the tick filters on `deleted_at IS NULL`, so no more failure logs), but it inflates any failed-connection count. I'd fold a cleanup into the observability PR.

Next: flip the Slack event when you get a moment, and tell me if you want the ACL observability PR (persist failure reason + wire into the health alerter + orphan-row cleanup) — that's the piece that would have surfaced these two dead connections months ago instead of us finding them by hand.

-- migrate:up

-- Remove ACL-enforcement rows whose connection no longer exists as a LIVE
-- `connections` row. `authz_source_acl_state` is a pure materialization of a
-- source's access graph — rebuilt from scratch by the next ACL sync, referenced
-- by nothing — and no code path ever deleted from it, so every connection
-- deleted before this change left its row orphaned forever as e.g. 'full' or
-- 'failed', inflating any "failed connections" count. Deleting orphans is safe
-- for the same reason: the row is derivable and nothing depends on it.
--
-- `authz_source_acl_state.connection_id` is the connection's RUNTIME id, which
-- differs per connector type:
--   * a managed Slack install is keyed by its `slackinst-…` slug verbatim;
--   * a BYO Slack connection by its `agentconn-`-stripped runtime id;
--   * a data connector (GitHub) by its numeric `connections.id::text`.
-- The predicate below matches every shape and must stay in lockstep with
-- `ACL_ROW_CONNECTION_ALIVE_SQL` in
-- packages/server/src/authz/acl-observability.ts (the connector-health scan
-- matches the same shapes; delete-time cleanup calls `deleteConnectionAclRows`).
DELETE FROM public.authz_source_acl_state a
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM public.connections c
  WHERE c.organization_id = a.organization_id
    AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND (
      a.connection_id = c.slug
      OR a.connection_id = c.id::text
      OR a.connection_id = CASE
            WHEN c.slug LIKE 'agentconn-%' THEN substr(c.slug, length('agentconn-') + 1)
            ELSE c.slug
          END
    )
);

-- migrate:down

-- No-op: the swept rows were orphans whose connection no longer exists, and
-- the ACL state is a materialization the next sync rebuilds anyway — there is
-- nothing to restore.

- The failure REASON is persisted on `connections.error_message` under an
  `acl: ` prefix. That column is shared with feed sync and device-pin
  tombstones, so the write only overwrites NULL-or-`acl:`-owned text and the
  clear only removes `acl:`-owned text. An ACL writer can never clobber another
  subsystem's message. Both writes commit in one transaction with the state
  flip so the reason cannot be lost.
- ACL failures now classify as `acl_failed` in the EXISTING connector-health
  alerter, reusing its `unhealthy_alerted_at` claim, so it alerts once per
  episode rather than every tick. Checked before the feed rules because this
  failure has no feed symptom — the prod shape had healthy feeds throughout.
- `authz_source_acl_state` rows are deleted when their connection is deleted,
  and a migration sweeps rows already orphaned. Nothing ever deleted from that
  table, so every deleted connection left a row behind forever, inflating any
  "failed connections" count.

**The e2e proof came back clean — revocation is verified working in production.**

The full chain, with real timestamps:

| Phase | `freshness_state` | `updated_at` |
|---|---|---|
| Before leave | `fresh` | 17:45:03 |
| After webhook | **`stale`** | 17:47:27 |
| Next sync | `fresh` | 18:00:03 |

- **Webhook arrived**: `POST /lobu/api/v1/app-webhooks/slack`, `Slackbot 1.0`, HTTP 200, 16 ms — plus the coordinator's `"Slack channel membership revoked — invalidated ACL freshness"` log at 17:47:27, matching the ACL row's `updated_at` to the second.
- **Recall actually failed closed**: the identical member-scoped production query returned **1 row before, 0 rows while stale** — and the physical `channel_messages` row still existed during the denial, which rules out deletion as the explanation. That's the assertion that matters, and it's the one I most wanted.
- **Graph rebuilt correctly**: the next sync tombstoned membership edge `74236` four milliseconds before restoring freshness, so the post-sync query still returns 0 — correct, since the member really did leave.
- **Cleanup verified**: channel archived, temp Behavior 104 archived, test message deleted (0 remaining), connection 390 still active, no `events`/orgs/connections deleted. I independently confirmed the worktree is untouched — it did pure read-only prod verification.

So the feature I shipped earlier today is now proven end to end in prod, not just deployed.

**One caveat on its security finding.** It reported that production logs `x-slack-signature` and recommended redacting it. I checked: on `origin/main` that header name appears only in a *comment*, and I found no generic header-dumping logger in application source. So it's most likely the ingress/proxy access log, not our code — worth fixing, but at a different layer than "redact it in the app." Don't send anyone hunting through `packages/server` for it.

Its other finding is more actionable and self-consistent with today's work: an unscoped `slack-acl-sync failed` log at 18:00:01 with no connection id — exactly the blind spot the observability commit exists to close, though that specific log line isn't covered by it.

**Everything is now done except one thing:** `review-fix` on the observability commit is still running (8 min). Both codex agents are finished and their worktrees are clean.

Current tally — Slack revocation shipped, deployed, **and proven**; market/github deleted; GitHub callback fixed by you and the authorize page confirmed rendering (awaiting your click); observability committed and mutation-verified; funnel audit delivered and independently spot-checked; handoff files in `/tmp`.

I'll report `review-fix` when it lands. That's the last open item on my side.

channel recall fails closed until the next sync rebuilds the graph.
Merged `b6e36adac` (#2771), deployed as build 2145, and verified live.

## The prod proof (2026-08-15)
| Phase | freshness_state | updated_at |
|---|---|---|
| before leave | `fresh` | 17:45:03 |
| after webhook | `stale` | 17:47:27 |
| next sync | `fresh` | 18:00:03 |

- Webhook: `POST /lobu/api/v1/app-webhooks/slack`, `Slackbot 1.0`, 200, 16ms,
  plus the coordinator's "Slack channel membership revoked" log at the matching second.
- **Recall genuinely denied:** the identical member-scoped query returned 1 row
  before and **0 while stale**, with the physical `channel_messages` row still
  present — which is what rules out "the row was deleted" as the explanation.
  That assertion is the one that matters; state-flip alone proves nothing.
- Next sync tombstoned the membership edge 4ms before restoring freshness, so
  post-sync recall is still 0 (correct — the member really left).

## Design facts worth keeping
- The stamp (`markAclFresh`) is CONNECTION-wide but a graph build is per-scope.
  Slack Grid = one connection, many workspaces, so the sync passes
  `markFresh: false` per workspace and stamps ONCE after the loop. Stamping
  inside the loop reopens the gate while later workspaces still hold
  pre-revocation edges. GitHub's single-scope caller keeps the default.
- `invalidateSlackConnectionAcl` UPSERTS with `acl_support='none'` sentinel and
  `clock_timestamp()` — matching the fence's clock. `current_timestamp` is
  TRANSACTION start and would let a late-committing revocation slip under.
- Webhook signature IS verified before the coordinator: `provider.verify(...)`
  returns 401 at `routes/public/app-webhooks.ts:1066`, BEFORE the Slack takeover.

- Prod HTTP logs appear to contain `x-slack-signature`. NOT in application source
  on origin/main (only a comment) — so it is likely the INGRESS access log. Fix
  at that layer, don't hunt in `packages/server`.

**Root cause of a 2-month silent failure.** Connection 385
(`lobu-team/github-app-install`) returned `AUTH_MISSING`; auth profile 83
(`buremba-lobu-ai`, kind `oauth_account`) was stuck `pending_auth` with
`granted_scopes: []` since 2026-06-21. Every consent attempt died at GitHub with
**"Invalid Redirect URI"**.

- GitHub OAuth App "Lobu", id `3158444`, client `Ov23liflE0hP2Av3K2ow`
- Had ONE redirect URI: `https://app.lobu.ai/api/auth/callback/github`
  (that is Better Auth's SIGN-IN callback — do not remove it, login breaks)
- Lobu's connector flow sends `https://app.lobu.ai/connect/oauth/callback`

**Lobu was not wrong.** `/connect/oauth/callback` is a real served route —
`gateway/routes/public/connect-auth.ts:260`, documented at `connect/routes.ts:13`
as the "stable OAuth callback", used at four call sites. The URI was simply never
registered.

Fixed 2026-08-15 by ADDING it as a second redirect URI (GitHub supports several
— the settings form is an indexed array with an "Add redirect URI" button; the
old "classic OAuth apps allow only one" belief is outdated). Confirmed working:
the consent page then rendered "Authorize application" instead of the error.

## Mechanics worth reusing
- Mint a fresh consent URL: `client.authProfiles.update({ auth_profile_slug,
  reconnect: true })` → returns `connect_url` (+ `expires_at`).
- `authProfiles.get` takes `auth_profile_slug`, NOT an id.
- `profile_kind` matters: `oauth_app` = app-level client creds (env),
  `oauth_account` = the per-user grant. A connection needs the account one.
- **The assistant may NOT edit OAuth redirect URIs** — that is a security
  setting; it is correctly classifier-blocked. Hand the user the page.

Two GitHub connections sat `AUTH_MISSING` in prod from 2026-06-21 to 2026-08-15 — an OAuth consent that could never complete — failing on **every** ACL sync tick for two months with no symptom anywhere. Three surfaces, all on **existing columns**. No new table, no API change, no SDK change.

1. **The failure reason is persisted** on `connections.error_message` under an `acl: ` prefix. That column is shared with feed sync and device-pin tombstones, so the write only overwrites NULL-or-`acl:`-owned text and the clear only removes `acl:`-owned text — an ACL writer can never clobber another subsystem's message. The first implementation matched ACL rows against an `ANY()` candidate list of {slug, `agentconn-`-stripped slug, numeric id}. A connection whose numeric id collided with another connection's runtime id would delete **that other connection's** ACL row. `aclConnectionIdSql()` now derives the exact `connection_id` from the joined `connections` row, so a caller structurally cannot reach another connection's state. It also caught that the persisted reason exceeded its own 500-char cap (truncated *then* prefixed).

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Slack ACL gate:** `authz_source_acl_state` per (org, connection). Enforcement requires `acl_support='full'` AND `freshness_state='fresh'` AND synced within `ACL_STALE_AFTER_MINUTES = 60`. Any non-enforcing row **fails closed**. States: `enforced`, `stale`, `not-graphed`.
- **Connection-wide stamp vs per-scope build:** the ACL state row is keyed `(organization_id, connection_id)`, but `buildAccessGraph` runs per resource-set. Slack Grid = one connection, many workspaces → stamping inside the loop reopens the gate while later workspaces hold pre-revocation edges.
- **`current_timestamp` = transaction start; `clock_timestamp()` = statement time.** Mixing them across a fence and its writer creates a race.
- **Edge reconciliation is per-resource** (`to_entity_id = resourceEntityId`), so a per-team `buildAccessGraph` loop is safe for edges — only the stamp is connection-wide.
- **Webhook verification order:** `routes/public/app-webhooks.ts:1066` runs `provider.verify(...)` → 401 BEFORE the Slack takeover delegates to the coordinator.
- **Slack manifest API deadlock:** `apps.manifest.update` replaces wholesale and validates first. For app `A096D2P623B`: with `external_auth_providers` → `team_not_eligible: OauthProviders cannot be created on a free team`; without → `unable_to_delete_providers: mcp_dcr_lobu`. **No payload validates.**
- **Lobu browser bridge:** `lobu call run_sdk --org buremba` → `client.operations.execute({ connection_id: 479, operation_key, input })`. Ops: navigate, evaluate, click_ref, type_ref, focus_tab, release_tab, close_tab, get_accessibility_tree, wait_for_selector, console_capture_{start,drain,stop}, network_intercept_*, screenshot, upload_file, close_user_tabs, show_notification.
- **`click_ref` schema:** `ref: { document_epoch: int, ref_id: int }` — NOT `ref_id` at top level, NOT a bare int.
- **Background tabs don't paint virtualized lists** — the Slack event picker sized to 58px but rendered nothing until `focus_tab`.
- **`query_sdk` is read-only and rejects `connections.test`; `run_sdk` allows it.** Scripts need `export default async function () { … }`.
- **`authProfiles.get` takes `auth_profile_slug`, not an id.** `profile_kind`: `oauth_app` (app-level creds) vs `oauth_account` (per-user grant).
- **vitest EXCLUDES `packages/server/src/gateway/**/__tests__`** — those run under `bun test ./<path>`.
- **opencode auto-rejects writes outside cwd** (`external_directory (/tmp/*)`) and exits 0 — the known trap.
- **`gh pr checks` omits unreported required contexts**; `pi-review` and `ui-review` report via the *status* API, not check-runs. Must diff against the branch-protection list.

export function aclConnectionIdSql(tableAlias?: "c"): string {

  return `CASE
    WHEN ${prefix}credential_mode IS NULL THEN ${prefix}id::text
    WHEN left(${prefix}slug, length('agentconn-')) = 'agentconn-'
      THEN substr(${prefix}slug, length('agentconn-') + 1)
    ELSE ${prefix}slug
  END`;
}

export async function deleteConnectionAclRow(sql, params): Promise<void> {

      AND a.organization_id = c.organization_id
      AND a.connection_id = ${sql.unsafe(aclConnectionIdSql("c"))}
  `;
}

Yes, but only about half of them — and the ones that *don't* take it are the risky ones. Verified just now against your installed CLI:

**Accepts `-c/--context`:** `call`, `status`, `whoami`, `chat`, `token`, `link`, `login`/`logout`

**No context flag at all:** `apply`, `agent` (including `list`/`delete`/`update`), `memory` (including `run`), `connector` (including `run`), `org`

I checked the subcommands separately, not just the top-level groups — `lobu agent list`, `lobu memory run`, `lobu org show`, and `lobu connector run` all have zero context flags too, so it's not a case of the flag living one level down.

That's why the stale context still matters. `lobu apply` is the sharp edge: it silently deploys `lobu.config.ts` to whatever the active context points at, with no way to pin it inline. With active = `prodma-dev` it would push to localhost:9455; if someone flips it back to prod and runs an apply meant for local, it goes the other way. Same exposure on `lobu agent delete`.

The clean fix isn't flipping the global context back and forth — it's `lobu link`, which binds a directory to a (context, org) pair in `.lobu/project.json`, so each checkout operates against the right runtime regardless of what the global active context is. input.content:
---
name: reference_connections_updated_at_is_a_chat_instance_memo_key
description: "connections.updated_at is the memo key ChatInstanceManager hydrates chat adapters against — any recurring writer that touches that column silently tears down and rehydrates live Slack/Telegram instances"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**`connections.updated_at` is not a bookkeeping column — it is a cache
invalidation key.** `ChatInstanceManager` stores it as `ManagedInstance.rowVersion`
and re-hydrates the adapter whenever the stored row is newer than the instance.

- `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/chat-instance-manager.ts:309` — the
  `rowVersion` field doc ("a pod-local instance is a pure memo of the row").
- `:359` — lazy hydration "keyed by the row's `updated_at`".
- `:774` — "the row is the source of truth and its post-write `updated_at` is the
  memo key every replica converges on."

That design is deliberate and good: config edits on any replica converge without
cross-pod restart fan-out. The hazard is the flip side.

## The rule
**Any writer on a recurring tick must be a no-op when nothing changed.** An
unconditional `SET … updated_at = current_timestamp` inside a periodic job means
every tick bumps the memo key, so every replica tears down and rebuilds
otherwise-healthy chat adapters for as long as the condition persists.

Caught by `make review` on #2788: `markConnectionAclFailed` rewrote the row on
every ACL failure even when the reason was byte-identical. ACL sync retries on a
15-minute tick, so one ACL-only outage would have thrashed live Slack instances
for its whole duration. Fixed with `IS DISTINCT FROM` guards on both the
`connections` and `authz_source_acl_state` writes.

## Before adding such a guard, check the column's readers
The only reader of `authz_source_acl_state.updated_at` is `markAclFresh`'s
ordering fence (`access-graph.ts:150`, `WHERE updated_at < syncStartedAt`), and
revocation bumps through its own always-writing upsert — so suppressing a
duplicate-failure bump does not weaken the fail-closed path. Verify the
equivalent before guarding any other timestamp.

## Writers that are already correctly guarded

---
name: reference_lobu_cli_context_flag_coverage
description: "Only about half the lobu CLI commands accept -c/--context; apply, agent, memory, connector and org do NOT and silently use the active context — lobu link is the durable fix"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**`lobu apply` has no `--context` flag.** Neither do `agent`, `memory`,
`connector`, or `org` — including their subcommands (checked `agent list`,
`memory run`, `org show`, `connector run`: zero context flags, so the flag does
not live one level down). They silently operate on whatever context is active.

Verified empirically 2026-08-15 against the installed CLI:

| Accepts `-c/--context` | Does NOT |
|---|---|
| `call`, `status`, `whoami`, `chat`, `token`, `link`, `login`/`logout` | `apply`, `agent`, `memory`, `connector`, `org` |

## Why it bites
A dispatched agent can switch the global context (one switched it to
`prodma-dev` → `localhost:9455` mid-session). Every `lobu call` afterwards fails
with a confusing `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError`, whose real cause only shows in
raw output: `MCP fetch failed … Tried: http://localhost:9455/api/<org>/<tool>`.
Pin with `-c prod` to confirm that diagnosis.

The sharp edge is `apply`: it deploys `lobu.config.ts` to the active context with
no way to pin inline, so a stale context sends a prod-intended apply to localhost
or vice versa. Same exposure on `agent delete`.

## The fix is `lobu link`, not flipping the global context
`lobu link` binds a directory to a (context, org) pair in `.lobu/project.json`,
so each checkout operates against the right runtime regardless of the global
active context. That is what makes the flagless commands safe. Flipping the
global context back and forth just relocates the race.

## Unrelated: codex's lobu MCP is NOT affected by the CLI context
`~/.codex/config.toml` hardcodes `mcp_servers.lobu = https://app.lobu.ai/mcp`
(prod) and `mcp_servers.lobu-local` = a tailscale URL. A codex
`MCP startup incomplete (failed: lobu, lobu-local)` is therefore NOT context
drift — prod `/mcp` correctly returns 401 with a well-formed RFC 9728
`www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=… scope="mcp:read mcp:write"`
challenge (codex simply holds no token), and `lobu-local` is unreachable when the
local stack is not running. Do not chase this as a Lobu defect.

Related: [[reference_prod_db_read_only_query_recipe]]

Adding the URI let consent succeed (profile 83 → `status: active`, scopes

385 stayed `AUTH_MISSING` with `auth_profile_id: null`. **A completed consent
does not attach the profile to the connection.** The second step:

```js

```

Proof of real recovery, not a green `test` (which does NOT validate scopes —
[[reference_connections_test_does_not_validate_scopes]]): every feed on 385 went
from `1271` consecutive failures / last sync 2026-07-20 to `last_sync_status:
success` with `consecutive_failures: 0` within minutes, and the connector-health
sweep then re-armed `unhealthy_alerted_at` from `2026-07-29T05:45:00Z` to `NULL`
on its own. Three independent signals.

Note `connections.get` returns `{}` for `auth_profile_id` (the serializer strips
it), so verify attachment via `connections.test` plus feed sync state, not by
reading the field back.

Oddity left behind: 385 carries DUPLICATE active feed rows (two `commits`, two
`pull_requests`), so every sync runs twice. Not breaking, not investigated.
